title: Splunk Login Failure Threshold Exceeded
description: A single source authenticated to Splunk Web/REST with repeated failures within a short window, consistent with a brute-force attempt against a Splunk user account. Legitimate users occasionally mistype passwords a handful of times; a sustained burst from one source is the signal worth alerting on.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Splunk authentication failure events recorded by splunkd.

detection_logic: Counts failed login events per source IP within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=failure
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count values(user) AS attempted_users by _time, src
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known load-balancer health-check sources and SSO-fallback test accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the source IP's ownership (VPN, office, unknown).
Check for a subsequent successful login from the same source (SPL-AUTH-002).
response_guidance: Block the source at the network layer if external; lock the targeted account(s) if internal and unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful Splunk Login Following Failure Burst
description: A Splunk account authenticated successfully immediately following a burst of failed attempts against it — the classic successful-brute-force pattern, and a strong precursor to every other detection in this library since a compromised Splunk account is a compromise of Tier-0/Tier-1 security infrastructure.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Sequenced failure and success login events for the same account.

detection_logic: Correlates a failure burst (>=5 in 10m) against a single account followed by a success event for that account within 5 minutes.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=failure
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count AS fail_count by _time, user
| where fail_count>=5
| join user [search index=_audit action=login attempt=success | table _time, user, src]
| where _time_success>_time AND (_time_success-_time)<=300
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive pattern; investigate all matches.
investigation_steps: Force a password reset on the account.
Review every search, export, and configuration action performed in the resulting session.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed account-compromise incident: reset credentials, terminate active sessions, and review the account's activity for the entire session.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Password Spray Across Multiple Accounts
description: A single source attempted authentication against many distinct Splunk usernames in a short window with a low per-account failure count each — the signature of password spraying, which evades simple per-account lockout thresholds.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Failed login events aggregated per source across distinct usernames.

detection_logic: Counts distinct usernames attempted per source IP within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=failure
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(user) AS user_count values(user) AS users count by _time, src
| where user_count>=10
tuning_guidance: Exclude known SSO-proxy or vulnerability-scanner sources with documented credentials-testing behavior.
investigation_steps: Determine if any targeted account had a subsequent successful login.
Block the source IP.
response_guidance: Block the source and force password resets for every targeted account that had a successful login.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: First-Seen Source IP for Splunk Authentication
description: A successful Splunk login occurred from a source IP never previously observed authenticating to this Splunk instance, which — while common during legitimate travel or new equipment — is a useful enrichment signal, especially when paired with a privileged account.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Successful login events compared against a 90-day source-IP baseline.

detection_logic: Compares each successful login's source IP against a lookup of previously-seen sources for that user, updated on a rolling basis.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup update=true splunk_auth_src_baseline.csv user, src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: Very common in isolation; combine with SPL-AUTH-006 (admin) or SPL-AUTH-009 (service account) for higher-confidence alerting.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user whether this login is expected (new location, VPN change).
Check what actions were taken during the session.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if the account is privileged or if followed by unusual activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Login Outside Normal Business Hours
description: A Splunk account authenticated during a time window well outside its established login pattern, which can indicate compromised-credential use by an attacker operating in a different time zone or automated off-hours access.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Login timestamps compared against each user's historical hour-of-day baseline.

detection_logic: Computes each user's typical login-hour distribution over a trailing baseline period and flags logins falling far outside it.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| eval hour=strftime(_time, "%H")
| lookup user_login_hour_baseline.csv user, hour OUTPUT is_typical_hour
| where isnull(is_typical_hour)
| table _time, user, hour
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-user hour-of-day baseline lookup; exclude on-call/global-team accounts with legitimately irregular hours.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user whether the login was expected.
Correlate with concurrent VPN/badge activity if available.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if paired with sensitive-index access or configuration changes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Admin Account Login
description: An account holding the built-in admin role (or an equivalent role with admin_all_objects) authenticated to Splunk. Not inherently suspicious, but every admin login is a building block for the higher-confidence correlations elsewhere in this catalogue (first-seen admin source, admin session followed by detection tampering, etc.).

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Login events joined against a role lookup identifying admin-capable accounts.

detection_logic: Joins successful login events against a maintained lookup of admin-role accounts.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where is_admin=1
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained admin-account lookup; high volume by design, primarily useful as a correlation building block.
investigation_steps: Track for use in downstream correlations (SPL-X-001 style).
response_guidance: No standalone action; feeds correlation searches.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: First-Seen Source for Splunk Admin Login
description: An admin-capable Splunk account authenticated from a source IP never previously seen for that account, a materially higher-confidence variant of SPL-AUTH-004 given the account's privilege level.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Admin login events compared against a per-user source-IP baseline.

detection_logic: Joins admin-account logins against the same source-IP baseline as SPL-AUTH-004, scoped to admin accounts only.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where is_admin=1
| lookup update=true splunk_auth_src_baseline.csv user, src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: Requires both the admin-account and source-baseline lookups; a strong candidate for a Tier-1 alert.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the admin whether this login is expected.
Review all actions taken during the session for detection tampering, role changes, or data export.
response_guidance: Verify immediately; reset credentials and terminate the session if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Service Account Interactive Splunk Web Login
description: An account designated as a non-interactive service/automation account authenticated to Splunk Web interactively, which — since service-account credentials are typically stored in automation systems rather than known to a human — can indicate the credential was exfiltrated and is being used manually by an attacker.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Web-interface login events joined against a service-account lookup.

detection_logic: Filters successful Splunk Web (not REST/API) login events for accounts flagged as service accounts in a maintained lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup service_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_service_account
| where is_service_account=1
| search NOT useragent="*splunk-sdk*"
| table _time, user, src, useragent
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained service-account lookup; exclude accounts with a documented legitimate reason for interactive use.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether any administrator used the service account intentionally for troubleshooting.
If not, treat as a credential-compromise incident.
response_guidance: Rotate the service account's credential and review its automated integrations for tampering.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Dormant Splunk Account Reactivated
description: A Splunk account with no successful login for an extended period (e.g. 90+ days) authenticated successfully, which can indicate use of a forgotten/orphaned account left over from a former employee or contractor — a classic persistence target.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Login events compared against each account's last-successful-login timestamp.

detection_logic: Joins each login against a lookup of last-successful-login-per-user and flags gaps exceeding the dormancy threshold.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup update=true splunk_last_login.csv user OUTPUT last_login
| eval days_dormant=round((_time-last_login)/86400)
| where days_dormant>=90
| table _time, user, src, days_dormant
tuning_guidance: Correlate with HR/offboarding records where available; some dormancy is legitimate (seasonal auditors, DR-only accounts).
investigation_steps: Verify the account owner is still an active employee/contractor with a business need.
Disable if orphaned.
response_guidance: Disable the account and investigate how the credential was obtained if the owner denies the login.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Local Splunk Authentication Used When SSO Is Expected
description: A user authenticated via Splunk's local/internal authentication scheme in an environment where SAML/LDAP SSO is the configured and expected authentication method, which can bypass any conditional-access, MFA, or centralized-deprovisioning policy enforced only at the identity provider — a common technique for maintaining access after an account is disabled upstream.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Login events with authentication-method field, filtered to auth_type=local in an SSO-enforced environment.

detection_logic: Filters successful login events where auth_type is local rather than the configured external scheme, excluding the documented break-glass admin account.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success auth_type=local
| lookup breakglass_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_breakglass
| where isnull(is_breakglass)
| table _time, user, src, auth_type
tuning_guidance: Exclude the documented break-glass account (tracked separately by SPL-AUTH-011); alert on all other local-auth use once SSO is enforced.
investigation_steps: Confirm the user's SSO account is not disabled or having provisioning issues that would legitimately explain a fallback.
If unexplained, treat as a probable SSO-bypass persistence mechanism.
response_guidance: Disable local authentication for the account and investigate how/when it was enabled for local auth.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Break-Glass Splunk Account Used
description: The designated emergency/break-glass Splunk administrative account authenticated. This account should only ever be used during a declared incident or SSO outage; every use warrants review, and use followed by configuration changes is significantly higher risk.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Login events filtered to the designated break-glass account(s).

detection_logic: Filters successful login events for accounts on the break-glass lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup breakglass_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_breakglass
| where is_breakglass=1
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; this account's usage should always be rare and always be traceable to a documented incident or ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the use against an open incident/change ticket.
Review every action taken during the session.
response_guidance: If no matching ticket exists, treat as a confirmed incident and rotate the break-glass credential immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Concurrent Splunk Login from Geographically Inconsistent Sources
description: The same Splunk account has active sessions from two source IPs whose geolocation makes legitimate concurrent use implausible within the observed time window (an 'impossible travel' pattern), suggesting the credential is in use by more than one party — most likely the legitimate user and an attacker.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Concurrent successful logins for the same account from distinct source IPs, enriched with IP geolocation.

detection_logic: Groups successful logins by user within a short window and flags cases where two sessions originate from distinct countries with a travel-time-implausible gap, using a geo-IP enrichment lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| iplocation src
| stats values(Country) AS countries dc(Country) AS country_count values(src) AS sources by user, _time
| where country_count>1
tuning_guidance: Requires IP geolocation enrichment (the `iplocation` command or an equivalent lookup); exclude known corporate VPN egress points that geolocate incorrectly.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user which session (if any) is legitimate.
Terminate the illegitimate session and force a credential reset.
response_guidance: Treat as a probable account-compromise incident; reset credentials and terminate all active sessions.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SAML Authentication Failure Burst
description: A burst of SAML authentication failures occurred, which can indicate an attacker probing the SSO integration, a misconfigured SAML assertion, or an IdP-side outage affecting Splunk sign-in.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: SAML authentication failure log lines.

detection_logic: Counts SAML-related authentication failure log lines within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=UserManagerPro "SAML*" (ERROR OR WARN)
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count by _time
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Correlate with IdP-side status to rule out a provider outage before treating as an attack.
investigation_steps: Check the identity provider's own logs for a matching failure pattern.
If not IdP-side, investigate for targeted SAML assertion manipulation.
response_guidance: Engage the identity team if the IdP is healthy but Splunk-side failures persist.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SAML User/Role Mapping Changed
description: The SAML group-to-role mapping was modified, which controls what Splunk role a federated user receives on login — a change here can silently grant a broad group of identity-provider users elevated Splunk privileges without any per-user role assignment ever appearing in Splunk's own audit trail.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: SAML configuration change events, specifically groupToRolesMapping edits.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change audit events targeting the SAML authentication stanza's role-mapping settings.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_authentication (object="SAML*" OR info="*groupToRoleMapping*")
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; SAML role-mapping changes should be rare and tightly controlled.
investigation_steps: Diff the mapping before and after the change.
Determine how many IdP-side group members now receive a different Splunk role.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately and audit any logins that occurred under the new mapping.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SAML/SSO Configuration Disabled or IdP Metadata Changed
description: SAML/SSO authentication was disabled outright, or the IdP metadata (entity ID, signing certificate, SSO URL) was changed — either of which can force Splunk back onto local authentication (removing any MFA/conditional-access enforced only at the IdP) or redirect the trust relationship to an attacker-controlled identity provider.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: SAML enable/disable and IdP metadata configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters authentication-configuration-change events where SAML is disabled or IdP metadata fields (entityId, idpSSOUrl, idpCertPath) change.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_authentication object=SAML info="*disabled*" OR info="*idpCertPath*" OR info="*idpSSOUrl*" OR info="*entityId*"
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; this configuration should change only during a planned, ticketed IdP migration.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Verify the new IdP metadata belongs to the legitimate, authorized identity provider.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized and force re-authentication of all sessions.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unexpected Local Admin Login Following SSO Failure
description: A burst of SAML authentication failures (SPL-AUTH-013) was immediately followed by a successful local-authentication admin login — consistent with an attacker deliberately disrupting or exploiting the SSO path to force a fallback to weaker local authentication, then using a compromised or brute-forced local admin credential.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: SAML failure burst (splunkd.log) followed by a local admin login (_audit) within a short window
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a SAML failure burst followed by a successful local-auth admin login within 15 minutes.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=UserManagerPro "SAML*" (ERROR OR WARN)
| bucket _time span=15m | stats count by _time
| where count>=10
| append [search index=_audit action=login attempt=success auth_type=local | lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin | where is_admin=1]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen dc(_time) AS stage_count
| where stage_count>=2 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=900
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; a strong Tier-1 candidate given the severity of the combined pattern.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed incident.
Rotate the local admin credential and re-enable/verify SSO immediately.
response_guidance: Full incident response: lock the local admin account, verify SSO integrity, and audit every action taken during the session.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: LDAP Configuration Changed
description: The LDAP strategy configuration (server host, bind DN, search base, role-mapping) was modified, which — like the SAML equivalent — can redirect authentication to an attacker-controlled directory or silently change which LDAP groups map to privileged Splunk roles.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: LDAP strategy configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters authentication-configuration-change events for the LDAP stanza.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_authentication object=LDAP*
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate directory migrations.
investigation_steps: Verify the new LDAP server/bind account is the authorized directory.
Review the role-mapping diff.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: LDAP Bind Account Credential Changed
description: The service-account credential Splunk uses to bind to the LDAP directory for authentication and group lookups was changed, warranting confirmation that the change was performed through an authorized credential-rotation process.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: LDAP bind-credential configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters LDAP configuration-change events specifically touching the bindDN/bindDNpassword fields.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_authentication object=LDAP* info="*bindDN*"
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a credential-rotation change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the rotation was performed by an authorized administrator.
Verify LDAP authentication continues to function correctly post-change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and rotate again through the proper channel.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LDAP Authentication Failure Burst or Disabled
description: A burst of LDAP authentication failures occurred, or LDAP authentication was disabled outright — either scenario can force a fallback to local authentication and merits the same scrutiny as the SAML-outage chain (SPL-AUTH-016).

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: LDAP authentication failure and disable events.

detection_logic: Counts LDAP-related authentication failure log lines within a rolling window, and separately flags an outright LDAP-disable configuration event.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=UserManagerPro "LDAP*" (ERROR OR WARN)
| bucket _time span=15m | stats count by _time
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Correlate with directory-service health status before treating as an attack.
investigation_steps: Check directory-service health.
If healthy, investigate for targeted LDAP-bind disruption.
response_guidance: Engage the identity team; watch for a subsequent local-auth fallback login per SPL-AUTH-016's pattern.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Splunk User Account Created
description: A new Splunk user account was created. Routine in isolation but a necessary building block for detecting unauthorized account creation, especially when the new account is granted a privileged role (see SPL-AUTH-023 and SPL-RBAC correlations).

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: User-creation events.

detection_logic: Filters user-creation audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info=created
| table _time, user, object, roles
tuning_guidance: Confirm against onboarding/change tickets; high routine volume in growing environments.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new account was created by an authorized administrator for a legitimate business need.
response_guidance: Disable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk User Account Deleted or Disabled at Scale
description: An unusually large number of user accounts were deleted or disabled by a single administrator in a short window, which can indicate a destructive attack aimed at locking out legitimate SOC/administrative staff during an incident.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: User deletion/disable events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts user deletion/disable events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info IN ("deleted","disabled")
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(object) AS affected_users by _time, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Correlate with legitimate offboarding-batch processes; raise the threshold for known HR-integration automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm the actions against an offboarding project or ticket.
Treat as a live incident absent one, especially if SOC/admin accounts are among those affected.
response_guidance: Re-enable affected accounts immediately if unauthorized; lock the acting account.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk User Password Reset by Administrator
description: An administrator reset another user's password, which — while a routine help-desk action — can also be used by an attacker with admin access to take over another user's (especially another admin's) account.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Password-reset events where the acting user differs from the target.

detection_logic: Filters password-change events where the acting user is not the target account itself.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info=password_changed
| where user!=object
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against help-desk tickets; scope closer scrutiny to resets targeting privileged accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm the reset was requested by the account owner through the proper channel.
Check for a subsequent login to the reset account from an unfamiliar source.
response_guidance: Notify the account owner and verify the reset was legitimate; re-reset if not.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New User Created with Admin or Privileged Role
description: A newly created Splunk user account was assigned the admin role or another role with admin_all_objects capability at creation time, skipping the usual pattern of starting with a limited role and escalating later — a common attacker persistence technique when they already hold admin access.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: User-creation events where the assigned roles include admin or an admin-equivalent role.

detection_logic: Filters user-creation events where the roles field includes admin or a role flagged as admin-equivalent in a maintained lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info=created
| search roles="admin" OR roles IN ["sc_admin","*_admin"]
| table _time, user, object, roles
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a privileged-access-request ticket; every occurrence deserves review.
investigation_steps: Confirm the grant against an approved request.
Review the new account's subsequent activity.
response_guidance: Downgrade the role and investigate the creating admin's account if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unusual Volume of User Account Changes
description: A single administrator performed an unusually large number of user account changes (create/edit/delete) in a short window compared to their historical baseline, which can indicate either a bulk legitimate operation or account-management abuse following an admin compromise.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: All user-management events aggregated per actor per window, compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Counts user-management events per actor within a rolling window and flags counts exceeding the actor's historical baseline.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count by _time, user
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count stdev(count) AS stdev_count by user
| where count > (avg_count + 3*stdev_count)
tuning_guidance: Exclude known bulk-onboarding/offboarding automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm the volume against a known project.
Review the specific accounts changed for privilege escalation patterns.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: count exceeds 95th percentile for this actor over trailing 30 days

title: Splunk User Authentication Method Changed for Account
description: An individual user account's authentication method was changed (e.g. from SSO-managed to a local password), which can be used to plant a local-password fallback for a specific account ahead of an SSO-bypass persistence attempt, distinct from the platform-wide SSO-disable covered by SPL-AUTH-015.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Per-user authentication-method change events.

detection_logic: Filters user-edit events where the change touches the account's authentication-type/realm field.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info="*auth_type*" OR info="*realm*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate exception accounts (e.g. a service account intentionally kept on local auth).
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the change.
Monitor the account for a subsequent local-auth login.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Splunk Role Created
description: A new custom Splunk role was created. Routine during legitimate RBAC design work, but a necessary building block for detecting a role deliberately crafted to grant excessive access under an innocuous-sounding name.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role-creation events.

detection_logic: Filters role-creation audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the new role's capabilities and index access once created.
response_guidance: No standalone action; review capability grants via SPL-RBAC-003.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Role Deleted
description: A Splunk role was deleted, which — if the role was actively assigned to users — can unexpectedly strip their access, or (less commonly) be used to remove an audit trail of a role's prior overly-broad configuration.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role-deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters role-deletion audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info=deleted
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets; check for users still assigned the deleted role.
investigation_steps: Determine which users were assigned this role and what access they lose.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Re-create if unauthorized and users were unexpectedly impacted.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: High-Risk Capability Added to Splunk Role
description: A role was modified to add a high-risk capability (admin_all_objects, edit_roles, edit_user, schedule_search with elevated concurrency, output creation, or REST endpoint access) — the core mechanism for both legitimate privilege management and privilege-escalation attacks against Splunk. admin_all_objects in particular effectively grants ownership of every knowledge object regardless of the object's own sharing permissions.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events filtered to a maintained list of high-risk capability names.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events where the new capabilities list includes a capability on a maintained high-risk lookup (admin_all_objects, edit_roles, edit_user, edit_deployment_client, edit_dist_peer, edit_forwarders, edit_httpauths, edit_input_defaults, edit_scripted, edit_server, edit_splunktcp, edit_tcp, edit_udp, edit_web_settings, output_file, restart_splunkd, rtsearch).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*capabilities*"
| rex field=info "capabilities=(?<new_caps>[^;]+)"
| makemv delim="," new_caps
| mvexpand new_caps
| lookup high_risk_capabilities.csv capability AS new_caps OUTPUT is_high_risk
| where is_high_risk=1
| table _time, user, object, new_caps
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained high-risk-capability lookup validated against your Splunk version's actual capability list; confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved access request.
Determine which users hold this role and what they can now do.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Role Modified to Include admin_all_objects
description: A role was granted the admin_all_objects capability specifically — the single most powerful non-admin capability in Splunk's RBAC model, since it bypasses per-object sharing/ACL restrictions entirely and grants effective ownership of every saved search, dashboard, lookup, and other knowledge object in the system regardless of that role's index or search-filter restrictions.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role modification events specifically adding admin_all_objects.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events where the capability diff specifically includes admin_all_objects being added.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*admin_all_objects*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; this specific capability should be granted only to the smallest possible set of true administrators.
investigation_steps: Confirm the grant against an approved request.
Audit every knowledge object this role can now access regardless of sharing.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Role Index Access Expanded to Wildcard or Sensitive Index
description: A role's srchIndexesAllowed list was expanded to include a wildcard (*) or a specific sensitive index (security, authentication, audit) it did not previously have access to, directly enabling every user with that role to search data they could not before.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role index-access configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events touching srchIndexesAllowed where the new value includes a wildcard or a sensitive-index-lookup match.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*srchIndexesAllowed*"
| rex field=info "srchIndexesAllowed=(?<new_indexes>[^;]+)"
| where match(new_indexes, "\*") OR match(new_indexes, "(?i)(security|authentication|audit|identity)")
| table _time, user, object, new_indexes
tuning_guidance: Maintain a sensitive-index lookup to reduce noise; confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the expansion against an approved access request.
Determine which users hold this role.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Role Search Filter Weakened or Removed
description: A role's srchFilter (a search-time restriction limiting what subset of data a role can see even within its allowed indexes) was removed or weakened, expanding effective data access without touching index permissions directly.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role search-filter configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events touching srchFilter where the new filter is empty or a subset of the prior filter's restrictiveness.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*srchFilter*"
| rex field=info "srchFilter=(?<new_filter>[^;]*)"
| where new_filter=""
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets; full weakened-vs-removed comparison requires diffing filter text, which this baseline atomic form does not attempt.
investigation_steps: Verify the change against an approved request.
Determine what data is now visible to this role that was not before.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Role Inheritance Changed to Add Privileged Parent
description: A role's imported-roles list was changed to inherit from a more privileged role (e.g. power or admin), which grants every capability and index access of the parent role indirectly — a way to escalate privilege without touching the role's own capability list, which is what most reviewers check first.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role inheritance configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events touching imported_roles where the new value includes admin or another high-privilege role.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*imported_roles*"
| rex field=info "imported_roles=(?<new_parents>[^;]+)"
| where match(new_parents, "(?i)(admin|power|sc_admin)")
| table _time, user, object, new_parents
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the inheritance change against an approved request.
Enumerate the full effective capability set for the role after inheritance.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: User Assigned Admin or Admin-Equivalent Role
description: An existing user account was assigned the admin role or another role flagged as admin-equivalent in the maintained lookup, escalating an existing account's privilege — distinct from SPL-AUTH-023's new-account variant.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: User role-assignment change events.

detection_logic: Filters user-edit events where the new roles list includes admin or an admin-equivalent role, excluding account-creation events (covered by SPL-AUTH-023).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info="*roles*"
| where info!="created"
| lookup admin_equivalent_roles.csv role_name OUTPUT is_admin_equivalent
| search roles="admin" OR is_admin_equivalent=1
| table _time, user, object, roles
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a privileged-access-request ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the grant against an approved request.
Review the account's subsequent activity.
response_guidance: Revoke if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Self-Privilege-Escalation: User Modifies Own Role Assignment
description: A user account performed a role or capability change that affected its own access — a strong signal of a compromised low-privilege account that has found and exploited a permission gap (e.g. edit_user capability without a corresponding restriction preventing self-modification), or an insider attempting unauthorized self-escalation.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role/capability-change events where the acting user and the target object are the same identity.

detection_logic: Filters role/user-edit events where the acting user matches the target object of the change.
spl:
index=_audit (action=edit_user OR action=edit_roles)
| where user=object
| table _time, user, object, action, info
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; legitimate admins do not typically need to modify their own role assignment.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Determine how the account obtained the capability to modify its own access.
response_guidance: Suspend the account and investigate the underlying RBAC misconfiguration that permitted this.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privilege Escalation Chain: Low-Privilege User to Privileged Action
description: A user account previously holding only a low-privilege role had its role or capability set changed, and shortly afterward performed a privileged search or configuration action consistent with the newly granted access — confirming the escalation was actually exploited rather than simply granted and unused.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_user OR action=edit_roles, followed by a privileged action for the same user
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: role/capability change, then privileged use.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a role/capability-escalation event for a user followed by that user performing a privileged action (config change, sensitive search, export) within 2 hours.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_user info="*roles*"
| lookup admin_equivalent_roles.csv role_name OUTPUT is_admin_equivalent
| where is_admin_equivalent=1
| rename user AS granted_user
| join type=inner granted_user [search index=_audit (action=edit_roles OR action=edit_authentication OR action=search) | rename user AS granted_user]
| where (_time_priv-_time)<=7200 AND (_time_priv-_time)>=0
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; a strong Tier-1 candidate.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed privilege-escalation incident.
Suspend the account and review every action taken with the new privilege.
response_guidance: Full incident response: revoke the escalated role, suspend the account pending investigation, and audit all actions taken.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: REST/Endpoint-Access Capability Granted
description: A role was granted the rest_properties_get/rest_properties_set capability or an equivalent broad REST access grant, which can allow the holder to read or modify Splunk's own configuration through the REST API beyond what Splunk Web's UI would otherwise expose.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events specifically for REST-properties access.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding rest_properties_get or rest_properties_set capability.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*rest_properties*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Review subsequent REST API activity for the affected role's users.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Schedule/Deployment Administration Capability Granted
description: A role was granted a scheduling or deployment-administration capability (schedule_search, edit_deployment_client, edit_deployment_server), enabling either resource-heavy scheduled searches or fleet-management access.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events for scheduling/deployment capabilities.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding schedule_search, edit_deployment_client, or edit_deployment_server capability.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles (info="*schedule_search*" OR info="*edit_deployment*")
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: App Installation Capability Granted to Non-Admin Role
description: A non-admin role was granted the ability to install apps (typically bundled with admin_all_objects, but sometimes achievable through a narrower capability combination), giving that role's users the ability to introduce arbitrary code — including scripted inputs and custom REST handlers — onto the Splunk instance.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events touching app-management capabilities.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding app-installation-related capabilities to a role not already flagged as admin-equivalent.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*app*"
| lookup admin_equivalent_roles.csv role_name AS object OUTPUT is_admin_equivalent
| where isnull(is_admin_equivalent)
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Monitor for subsequent app installations by users holding this role.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Index Management Capability Granted
description: A role was granted edit_indexes or a related index-administration capability, enabling the holder to create, delete, or reconfigure indexes — including retention settings, a mechanism covered further by the SPL-DATA retention-tampering detections.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events for index-management capability.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding edit_indexes capability.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*edit_indexes*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Ingest/HEC Configuration Capability Granted
description: A role was granted edit_tcp, edit_udp, edit_httpauths, or a related ingestion/HEC-configuration capability, enabling the holder to create HEC tokens or configure new data-input listeners.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events for ingestion-configuration capabilities.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding ingestion/HEC-configuration capabilities.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles (info="*edit_tcp*" OR info="*edit_udp*" OR info="*edit_httpauths*")
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Monitor for subsequent HEC token creation by this role's users.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Token Management Capability Granted
description: A role was granted admin_all_objects or a specific token-administration capability enabling the holder to create authentication tokens on behalf of other users, a mechanism that can be used to mint a long-lived credential for persistence.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events touching token-administration capability.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding token-management-related capability.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*token*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Monitor for subsequent token creation on behalf of other users.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Role/Capability Change Across Many Roles
description: A single administrator modified an unusually large number of distinct roles in a short window, consistent with a scripted, attacker-driven mass privilege-escalation operation rather than routine, incremental RBAC administration.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role-modification events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct roles modified per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(object) AS role_count values(object) AS roles by _time, user
| where role_count>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known IaC/RBAC-automation pipelines.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a bulk RBAC-migration project.
Treat as a live incident absent one.
response_guidance: Suspend the actor and audit every role changed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Non-Admin User Attempts Privileged Action and Is Denied
description: A non-privileged user's REST/Web action was denied due to insufficient capability, which — while normal in isolation — can indicate reconnaissance or active probing of the RBAC boundary when repeated across many distinct privileged endpoints by the same user.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: REST API 403 (forbidden) responses.

detection_logic: Counts distinct privileged REST endpoints returning 403 per user within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access status=403
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(uri) AS endpoint_count values(uri) AS endpoints by _time, user
| where endpoint_count>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known misconfigured-integration accounts with a documented pending access request.
investigation_steps: Determine why the user is attempting these endpoints.
Check for a successful privilege-escalation event immediately following (SPL-RBAC-010).
response_guidance: Investigate the user's intent; educate or restrict as appropriate.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1069: Permission Groups Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Role Made Functionally Equivalent to Admin
description: A role's cumulative capability set (direct capabilities plus inherited capabilities) now matches or exceeds that of the built-in admin role, even though the role's name and apparent purpose suggest a limited scope — a technique to hide a fully-privileged account behind an innocuous role name that reviewers may not scrutinize as closely as one literally named 'admin'.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_roles, correlated against a computed effective-capability comparison to the admin role
data_sources.description: Periodic comparison of each role's effective capability set against the admin role's capability set.

detection_logic: A scheduled search (not a real-time event filter) that periodically enumerates every role's effective capability set via the REST API/roles endpoint and flags any non-admin role whose set is a superset of, or equal to, admin's.
spl:
| rest /services/authorization/roles splunk_server=local
| eval cap_count=mvcount(capabilities)
| where title!="admin" AND cap_count>=<admin_capability_count>
| table title, capabilities, cap_count
tuning_guidance: Requires a scheduled search using the REST search command against the roles endpoint (not a log-based detection); update <admin_capability_count> whenever Splunk's built-in admin role's capability count changes across upgrades.
investigation_steps: Review how the role accumulated this capability set (direct grants vs. inheritance chain).
Identify every user holding this role.
response_guidance: Strip down to the intended, documented capability set.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud Role/Capability Change via ACS
description: A role or capability change was made through the Splunk Cloud Admin Config Service (ACS) API rather than Splunk Web/REST directly — ACS-driven changes go through a separate audit path and should be reconciled against the same RBAC change-management process as any other role modification.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role/capability-change events originating from the ACS API path.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification audit events where the originating source indicates the ACS API rather than standard Splunk Web/REST.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles
| search source="*acs*" OR src="*api.scs.splunk.com*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm ACS API calls against Splunk Cloud change tickets; do not assume Splunk Cloud always logs the ACS actor identically to a Splunk Web actor — validate against your stack's actual audit output.
investigation_steps: Verify the change against an approved ACS-driven RBAC request.
Cross-reference with SPL-CLOUD-### ACS authentication detections.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Using index=* Wildcard
description: A user ran an ad-hoc search using index=* (every index the role can access), which — while sometimes a legitimate troubleshooting technique — is also the fastest way for an attacker with search access to discover and enumerate all data available to a compromised account.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search execution events with the raw search string.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution audit events where the search string begins with index=*.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted search="index=\*\*"
| table _time, user, search
tuning_guidance: Exclude known administrative/health-check dashboards that legitimately use index=* for platform monitoring.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the user has a legitimate reason for a cross-index search.
Check for a subsequent large export (SPL-SEARCH-013).
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if paired with export activity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Against Internal Indexes by Non-Admin
description: A non-admin user searched Splunk's own internal indexes (_internal, _audit, _introspection), which can be legitimate app-development activity but also enables reconnaissance of the platform's own configuration, user activity, and administrative history.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search execution events targeting internal indexes, joined against a non-admin user filter.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution events where the search targets an internal index and the user does not hold an admin-equivalent role.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted search="index=_*"
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where isnull(is_admin)
| table _time, user, search
tuning_guidance: Exclude known app-developer accounts with a documented need to query _internal for debugging.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review what specifically was queried (user activity, config changes, other users' searches).
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if paired with other reconnaissance indicators.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: All-Time Search Against a Large Index
description: A user ran a search with an all-time (earliest=0) time range against a large index, maximizing both the historical data exposed to a single search and the resource cost of running it.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search execution events with the effective earliest-time parameter.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution events where search_et equals 0 or the equivalent all-time marker, restricted to large/sensitive indexes via a lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted search_et=0
| lookup index_size_baseline.csv index_name OUTPUT is_large_index
| where is_large_index=1
| table _time, user, search, search_et
tuning_guidance: Exclude known scheduled compliance/retention-audit searches with a legitimate all-time requirement.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check the resulting scan/result count and any subsequent export.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if paired with export activity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Spanning Unusually Many Distinct Indexes
description: A single search referenced an unusually large number of distinct indexes compared to the user's historical search pattern, consistent with broad, exploratory data-discovery behavior.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events with parsed index references, compared to a per-user baseline.

detection_logic: Parses index references out of each search string and flags searches referencing more distinct indexes than the user's historical maximum.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted
| rex max_match=0 field=search "index=(?<referenced_index>[a-zA-Z0-9_\*]+)"
| eval index_count=mvcount(referenced_index)
| eventstats max(index_count) AS historical_max by user
| where index_count > historical_max
| table _time, user, search, index_count
tuning_guidance: Requires a stable per-user baseline; noisy for new accounts with little search history.
investigation_steps: Review the specific indexes referenced.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if sensitive indexes are among those referenced.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sensitive Index Searched by Non-Admin
description: A user without an admin-equivalent role searched an index tagged as sensitive (security, authentication, audit, identity, threat-intelligence, HR, privileged-access, secrets-management, cloud audit), which — regardless of role permissions technically allowing it — warrants review of business justification given the sensitivity of what these indexes typically contain.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events joined against a maintained sensitive-index lookup.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution events referencing an index on the sensitive-index lookup, excluding accounts flagged as admin/security-team members.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted
| rex max_match=0 field=search "index=(?<referenced_index>[a-zA-Z0-9_\*]+)"
| mvexpand referenced_index
| lookup sensitive_indexes.csv index_name AS referenced_index OUTPUT is_sensitive
| where is_sensitive=1
| lookup security_team_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_security_team
| where isnull(is_security_team)
| table _time, user, search, referenced_index
tuning_guidance: Maintain both the sensitive-index and security-team-account lookups to keep this actionable.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the access.
Determine what fields/records were actually returned.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified; consider tightening the role's index access.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: First-Seen Sensitive Index Access by User
description: A user queried a sensitive index they have never previously accessed, a materially higher-confidence variant of SPL-SEARCH-005 given the behavioral novelty.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Sensitive-index search events compared against a per-user historical access baseline.

detection_logic: Joins sensitive-index search events against a lookup of each user's previously-accessed sensitive indexes.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted
| rex max_match=0 field=search "index=(?<referenced_index>[a-zA-Z0-9_\*]+)"
| mvexpand referenced_index
| lookup sensitive_indexes.csv index_name AS referenced_index OUTPUT is_sensitive
| where is_sensitive=1
| lookup update=true user_sensitive_index_baseline.csv user, referenced_index OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, referenced_index
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained baseline lookup; strong candidate for Tier-1 given the low false-positive rate once the baseline stabilizes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for a subsequent large export.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Containing Password/Secret/Credential-Pattern Keywords
description: A user ran a search whose search-string text itself matches credential-hunting patterns (password, apikey, secret, token, private key, connection string, AWS/Azure/GCP credential markers), consistent with an attacker with search access harvesting credentials that were accidentally indexed in log data.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events whose search text matches a credential-hunting keyword pattern.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution events where the search string matches a maintained credential-pattern regex, without exposing any matched secret values in the detection output.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted
| where match(search, "(?i)(password|passwd|apikey|api_key|secret|private_key|BEGIN (RSA|EC) PRIVATE KEY|aws_secret_access_key|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16})")
| table _time, user, search
tuning_guidance: Exclude known security/IR team accounts performing legitimate credential-exposure hunts by scoping this detection to non-security accounts.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the user has a legitimate reason for this search.
Never display the actual search results in the investigation workflow — only the search string itself.
response_guidance: Investigate the user's broader activity; rotate any credentials the search may have surfaced.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Returning Unusually Large Result Count
description: A search returned a result count far above the user's historical norm, which can indicate either an unusually broad exploratory search or a precursor to a bulk export.

data_sources.name: searches.log / scheduler.log
data_sources.description: Search job completion events with result_count.

detection_logic: Compares each search's result_count against the user's historical baseline and flags outliers.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=searches
| eventstats avg(result_count) AS avg_results stdev(result_count) AS stdev_results by user
| where result_count > (avg_results + 3*stdev_results) AND result_count>10000
| table _time, user, search_id, result_count
tuning_guidance: Exclude known reporting/dashboard scheduled searches that legitimately return large result sets.
investigation_steps: Check for a subsequent export of this search's results.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if paired with export.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search with Unusually High Scan Count
description: A search scanned an unusually large number of raw events relative to results returned, consistent with an inefficient (or deliberately resource-exhausting) search pattern that consumes disproportionate indexer/search-head capacity.

data_sources.name: searches.log
data_sources.description: Search job completion events with scan_count.

detection_logic: Flags searches whose scan_count exceeds a fixed high-water threshold and whose result-to-scan ratio is very low.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=searches
| where scan_count>=50000000
| eval efficiency=result_count/scan_count
| where efficiency<0.0001
| table _time, user, search_id, scan_count, result_count, efficiency
tuning_guidance: Tune the scan-count threshold to your environment's indexer capacity; differentiate from a poorly-written but legitimate search using SPL-SEARCH-010's intent analysis.
investigation_steps: Review the search string for unconstrained wildcards or missing index/sourcetype filters.
Determine if this is a deliberate DoS attempt or poor search design.
response_guidance: Contact the user for search optimization if accidental; investigate intent if repeated or targeted.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated Expensive Search Pattern by Same User
description: The same user repeatedly ran high-scan-count or long-running searches within a short window, distinguishing deliberate resource-exhaustion behavior from a single accidental expensive search.

data_sources.name: searches.log
data_sources.description: High-cost search completion events aggregated per user per window.

detection_logic: Counts high-scan-count or long-running search completions per user within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=searches (scan_count>=50000000 OR run_time>=300)
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats count by _time, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known scheduled-search service accounts with legitimately frequent expensive searches.
investigation_steps: Contact the user to confirm intent.
Check concurrency impact on other SOC searches (SPL-SEARCH-011).
response_guidance: Throttle or suspend the account's search concurrency if deliberate abuse is confirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Concurrency Saturation Impacting SOC Searches
description: Search concurrency limits were saturated (skipped scheduled searches, queued ad-hoc searches) at a time correlated with an unusually high volume of expensive searches from a small number of users, consistent with a deliberate or accidental denial-of-service against the search head's capacity to run security-critical scheduled searches (correlation searches, alerts).

data_sources.name: scheduler.log
data_sources.description: Skipped scheduled-search events correlated with concurrent expensive ad-hoc search volume.

detection_logic: Counts skipped scheduled searches within a rolling window and correlates timing against SPL-SEARCH-010-style resource-abuse events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=scheduler status=skipped
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(savedsearch_name) AS skipped_searches by _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known maintenance windows and search-head capacity changes before attributing to abuse.
investigation_steps: Determine which scheduled searches were skipped — flag immediately if any are ES correlation searches.
Identify the concurrent high-cost searches consuming capacity.
response_guidance: Kill the offending searches and raise search-head capacity or concurrency limits as an interim mitigation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Real-Time Search Created
description: A real-time search was created or scheduled, which — unlike historical searches — continuously consumes indexing-pipeline resources for as long as it runs and, in the wrong hands, can be used for near-live surveillance of a sensitive data stream.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events with a real-time earliest-time marker.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution events where the time-range parameters indicate a real-time search.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted search_et="rt*"
| table _time, user, search
tuning_guidance: Exclude known operational-monitoring dashboards with a legitimate real-time requirement.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Determine what index/sensitive data the real-time search targets.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if targeting a sensitive index.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Many Concurrent Real-Time Searches
description: An unusually large number of real-time searches were running concurrently, each consuming dedicated indexing-pipeline resources — a significant resource-exhaustion risk and, if all targeting sensitive data, a surveillance-scale concern.

data_sources.name: introspection_generator
data_sources.description: Real-time search resource-usage introspection events.

detection_logic: Counts concurrently active real-time search jobs at any point in time and flags counts exceeding a capacity-informed threshold.
spl:
index=_introspection component=RealtimeSearch
| stats dc(search_id) AS concurrent_rt_searches values(user) AS users by _time
| where concurrent_rt_searches>=10
tuning_guidance: Tune the threshold to your search head's actual real-time search capacity.
investigation_steps: Identify the users/roles running these searches.
Determine business justification for each.
response_guidance: Kill unnecessary real-time searches; consider restricting the rtsearch capability to fewer roles.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Large Search Result Export
description: A user exported a search's results in bulk (CSV, JSON, or raw format) with an unusually large row/byte count, the single clearest signal of data leaving Splunk in a form that can be taken outside the platform entirely.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: REST API export-endpoint access events with response size.

detection_logic: Filters export-endpoint access events where the response byte count exceeds a high-water threshold.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*")
| eventstats avg(bytes) AS avg_bytes stdev(bytes) AS stdev_bytes by user
| where bytes > (avg_bytes + 3*stdev_bytes) AND bytes>10000000
| table _time, user, uri, bytes
tuning_guidance: Exclude known scheduled-report/backup-export automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the underlying search and what data was exported.
Confirm business justification for the export.
response_guidance: Treat as a probable data-exfiltration incident if unjustified; disable the account and investigate the destination of the exported file.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: bytes exceeds 95th percentile for this user over trailing 30 days

title: Repeated Exports by Same User
description: The same user performed multiple search-result exports within a short window, which — even if each individual export is modest in size — can indicate a deliberate strategy to stay under a single-export size threshold while exfiltrating data incrementally.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: Export-endpoint access events aggregated per user per window.

detection_logic: Counts export-endpoint access events per user within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*")
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count by _time, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known reporting-dashboard users with a legitimately high export cadence.
investigation_steps: Aggregate the total volume exported across all events.
Confirm business justification for each export.
response_guidance: Investigate for exfiltration if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Export Outside Normal Business Hours
description: A search-result export occurred well outside the user's established working-hours pattern, a common exfiltration-timing signal used to reduce the chance of real-time detection by a human SOC analyst.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: Export events compared against each user's historical hour-of-day activity baseline.

detection_logic: Joins export events against the same per-user hour-of-day baseline used by SPL-AUTH-005.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*")
| eval hour=strftime(_time, "%H")
| lookup user_login_hour_baseline.csv user, hour OUTPUT is_typical_hour
| where isnull(is_typical_hour)
| table _time, user, uri, hour
tuning_guidance: Requires the same hour-of-day baseline lookup as SPL-AUTH-005; exclude global/on-call teams.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Correlate with SPL-AUTH-005 for a same-session anomaly.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Export by First-Seen User
description: A user with no prior history of exporting search results performed an export, a behavioral novelty worth reviewing especially for accounts that have never needed export capability before.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: Export events compared against a per-user export-history lookup.

detection_logic: Joins export events against a lookup tracking each user's prior export history.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*")
| lookup update=true user_export_baseline.csv user OUTPUT first_export
| where isnull(first_export)
| table _time, user, uri
tuning_guidance: Expect noise for newly onboarded users; combine with SPL-SEARCH-014's size threshold for higher confidence.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the export capability being exercised for the first time.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if the export is large.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Export from Sensitive Index
description: A user exported search results whose underlying search referenced a sensitive index — the single highest-confidence exfiltration signal in this catalogue's search section, combining a known-sensitive data source with a confirmed data-removal action.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Search-execution events referencing a sensitive index, correlated with a subsequent export event for the same search_id
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: sensitive-index search, then export.

detection_logic: Joins export events against the originating search's index references via search_id, filtered to the sensitive-index lookup.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*")
| rex field=uri "search_id=(?<search_id>[^&]+)"
| join type=inner search_id [search index=_audit action=search info=granted | rex max_match=0 field=search "index=(?<referenced_index>[a-zA-Z0-9_\*]+)" | mvexpand referenced_index | lookup sensitive_indexes.csv index_name AS referenced_index OUTPUT is_sensitive | where is_sensitive=1]
| table _time, user, search_id, referenced_index
tuning_guidance: This is the flagship search-exfiltration correlation; alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed exfiltration incident pending confirmation.
Determine the export's destination and content.
response_guidance: Full incident response: disable the account, preserve the export artifact for forensics, and rotate any credentials/secrets that may have been exposed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged Login Followed by Broad Search and Large Export
description: A privileged (admin-equivalent) account logged in, ran a broad search (index=* or a sensitive index with a wide time range), and exported a large result set — all within a short window — a full end-to-end exfiltration sequence using an admin credential's unrestricted access.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Admin login, broad search, and large export events for the same user within a short window
data_sources.description: Three-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) admin-account login, (2) a broad/sensitive search, (3) a large export — all for the same user within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where is_admin=1
| eval stage="1_login"
| append [search index=_audit action=search info=granted search="index=\*\*" | eval stage="2_broad_search"]
| append [search index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*") bytes>10000000 | eval stage="3_export"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by user
| where stage_count>=3 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=1800
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; a Tier-1 flagship exfiltration chain.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed exfiltration incident.
Disable the account and preserve forensic evidence of the export.
response_guidance: Full incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories
MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New/Rare Account Runs Sensitive Search Then Exports
description: An account with a first-seen source IP (SPL-AUTH-004) ran a sensitive-index search and exported the results within the same session, a full exfiltration sequence anchored on account novelty rather than account privilege — catching a compromised low-privilege account rather than an admin one.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: First-seen-source login, sensitive-index search, and export events for the same user within a short window
data_sources.description: Three-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) first-seen-source login, (2) sensitive-index search, (3) export — all for the same user within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup update=true splunk_auth_src_baseline.csv user, src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| eval stage="1_new_login"
| append [search index=_audit action=search info=granted | rex max_match=0 field=search "index=(?<referenced_index>[a-zA-Z0-9_\*]+)" | mvexpand referenced_index | lookup sensitive_indexes.csv index_name AS referenced_index OUTPUT is_sensitive | where is_sensitive=1 | eval stage="2_sensitive_search"]
| append [search index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access (uri="*/results*" OR uri="*/export*") | eval stage="3_export"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen_ts latest(_time) AS last_seen_ts values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by user
| where stage_count>=3 AND (last_seen_ts-first_seen_ts)<=1800
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; a Tier-1 flagship exfiltration chain distinct from SPL-SEARCH-019 in that it does not require the account to be privileged.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed exfiltration incident.
Disable the account and reset credentials.
response_guidance: Full incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories
MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Poorly Constrained Subsearch Explosion
description: A search's subsearch returned a result count near or at the subsearch result-count limit, a common performance anti-pattern (rather than a security threat in most cases) that nonetheless consumes disproportionate search-head resources.

data_sources.name: searches.log
data_sources.description: Subsearch completion events with result counts near the configured limit.

detection_logic: Flags subsearch executions whose result count is within 5% of the configured maxout limit.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=searches search_id="*subsearch*"
| where result_count>=(<maxout_limit>*0.95)
| table _time, user, search_id, result_count
tuning_guidance: Primarily a search-design/performance issue; differentiate from deliberate DoS with SPL-SEARCH-010's repetition pattern.
investigation_steps: Contact the user to help redesign the search (e.g. use join with a more selective subsearch or switch to stats-based correlation).
response_guidance: Educate; no security response needed unless repeated and deliberate.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Regex-Heavy Search Pattern Repeated
description: A user repeatedly ran searches containing multiple chained rex/regex commands over a broad time range, a search pattern significantly more CPU-intensive than field-based filtering and, at scale, capable of degrading search-head performance for other users.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events with regex-heavy search text, aggregated per user.

detection_logic: Counts searches per user containing two or more rex/regex/erex commands within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted
| eval regex_count=mvcount(split(search, "| rex")) - 1
| where regex_count>=2
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count by _time, user
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Primarily a search-optimization coaching opportunity; escalate only if paired with other resource-abuse indicators.
investigation_steps: Suggest field-extraction-based alternatives to the user.
response_guidance: Educate; no security response needed in isolation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service
