author: Threat Detection Library

title: Data Model Acceleration Manually Triggered Repeatedly
description: A user repeatedly triggered manual data-model acceleration rebuilds, an expensive operation that can be used to intentionally saturate indexer resources when repeated at scale.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Manual acceleration-rebuild trigger events.

detection_logic: Counts manual acceleration-rebuild trigger events per user within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=DataModelAccelerationRebuild triggered_by=manual
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count values(datamodel) AS datamodels by _time, user
| where count>=3
tuning_guidance: Exclude known data-model-development accounts during active build/test cycles.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess indexer resource impact.
response_guidance: Educate; escalate only if resource impact is severe and repeated.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Saved Search / Report Created
description: A new saved search or report was created. Routine, but the necessary building block for the higher-value scheduled-export and detection-tampering detections elsewhere in this catalogue.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search creation events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search creation audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: High routine volume; useful primarily as a correlation building block.
investigation_steps: Review the search's schedule, action, and target index once created.
response_guidance: No standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Saved Search Schedule or Cron Changed to Unusual Cadence
description: A saved search's cron schedule was changed to an unusually frequent cadence (e.g. every minute) or to run outside its previous window, which can indicate either a performance-impacting misconfiguration or an attacker tuning a malicious scheduled search's execution frequency.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search schedule-change events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events touching cron_schedule where the new schedule implies a sub-5-minute cadence.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*cron_schedule*"
| rex field=info "cron_schedule=(?<new_cron>\S+)"
| where match(new_cron, "^\*/[1-4] ")
| table _time, user, object, new_cron
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate high-frequency alerting needs.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review what the search's action does (alert, script, export).
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Saved Search Owner Changed
description: Ownership of a saved search was reassigned to a different user, which — because a search executes with its owner's effective permissions — can be used to run a search with broader index access than the modifying user's own role would otherwise permit.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search ownership-change events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events touching the owner field.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*owner*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate re-ownership during team transitions.
investigation_steps: Determine the new owner's role/index access relative to the old owner's.
Check whether this expands the search's effective privilege.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Saved Search Permissions Broadened to Global Sharing
description: A saved search's sharing level was broadened from private/app to global, making its content (including any embedded SPL logic, credentials in lookup references, or sensitive-index queries) visible and executable by every user across every app on the instance.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search sharing-level configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events where the sharing level changes to global.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*sharing=global*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; many legitimate reports are intentionally global.
investigation_steps: Review the search content for sensitive-index references or embedded credentials before it was made global.
response_guidance: Revert if it exposes sensitive logic or data unintentionally.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scheduled Search Deleted
description: A saved search was deleted. Not inherently high-risk, but a necessary companion to SPL-DETECT-### detection-tampering coverage — a security-relevant scheduled search deleted rather than merely disabled leaves less of an audit trail for the deletion decision itself.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search deletion audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info=deleted
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; correlate against a security-content naming pattern for higher-priority triage.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
If the deleted search was security-relevant, treat with the same urgency as SPL-KO detection-tampering coverage.
response_guidance: Restore from version control/backup if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scheduled Search Alert Action Changed to External Destination
description: A scheduled search's alert action was modified to send its results to a new email address, webhook, or script — since scheduled searches routinely run against sensitive data on a recurring basis, redirecting their output is a durable, low-effort exfiltration channel that doesn't require repeated manual searches.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Alert-action configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events touching email recipient, webhook URL, or script action fields.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search (info="*action.email.to*" OR info="*action.webhook.param.url*" OR info="*action.script*")
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; scope closer scrutiny to searches referencing sensitive indexes.
investigation_steps: Verify the new destination is authorized (internal domain, known webhook, approved script).
Determine what data this search regularly produces.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if the destination is external/unrecognized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scheduled Report Delivering Sensitive Data with High Result Count
description: A newly created or recently modified scheduled search references a sensitive index and its recurring execution consistently returns a high result count, consistent with a durable exfiltration pipeline established via routine report scheduling rather than manual ad-hoc searches.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Saved-search creation/modification events referencing a sensitive index, joined with the search's own execution history and result counts
data_sources.description: Correlation between search definition and its execution outcomes.

detection_logic: Joins saved-search creation/modification events against sensitive-index references, then joins the search's subsequent scheduled-execution result counts.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search (info=created OR info="*search=*")
| rex field=info "search=(?<search_text>[^;]+)"
| where match(search_text, "(?i)index=(security|authentication|audit|identity)")
| join type=inner object [search index=_internal sourcetype=scheduler savedsearch_name=object status=success | stats avg(result_count) AS avg_results by savedsearch_name | rename savedsearch_name AS object]
| where avg_results>1000
| table _time, object, search_text, avg_results
tuning_guidance: Confirm against approved compliance/reporting use cases; escalate only when the recipient list is unrecognized (correlate with SPL-SEARCH-029).
investigation_steps: Review the report's delivery destination.
Confirm business justification for the recurring sensitive-data delivery.
response_guidance: Disable the report if the destination is unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security Correlation Search Disabled
description: A saved search tagged as a security-detection/correlation search was disabled, which directly removes a specific piece of detection coverage — the single highest-priority knowledge-object tampering event in this catalogue since it can be a precursor step immediately before the matching malicious activity occurs.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search disable events joined against a security-content tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search disable events where the search is tagged as security-relevant in a maintained lookup (naming pattern, app membership, or explicit tag).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*disabled=1*"
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection
| where is_security_detection=1
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; maintain the security-detection-search lookup carefully — this detection's own entry should be on that list.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Re-enable immediately and review for a subsequent matching malicious event during the gap.
response_guidance: Re-enable the search immediately and retroactively run it against the exposure window.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: T1562 (Impair Defenses) most directly describes this activity but is not present in this library's validated MITRE technique cache; treat this citation as informational until the cache is refreshed against a newer ATT&CK release.

title: Security Correlation Search Deleted
description: A saved search tagged as a security-detection/correlation search was deleted outright — more severe than disabling in that it also removes the search's own configuration and history, complicating recovery and forensic reconstruction of what the detection covered.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search deletion events joined against a security-content tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search deletion events where the search is tagged as security-relevant.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info=deleted
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection
| where is_security_detection=1
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; restore from version-controlled backup (e.g. app source-control) immediately.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Restore from version control and review for a subsequent matching malicious event during the gap.
response_guidance: Restore the search immediately from source control and retroactively run it against the exposure window.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security Correlation Search SPL Modified
description: A security correlation search's underlying SPL was modified — the most subtle form of detection tampering, since the search continues to run and appear healthy while its actual matching logic may have been narrowed, broken, or made to exclude a specific pattern the attacker wants to hide.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Saved-search SPL-text-change events joined against a security-content tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events touching the search field, restricted to security-tagged searches.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*search=*"
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection
| where is_security_detection=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against detection-engineering change tickets (pull requests, tuning notes); alert on all unauthorized changes.
investigation_steps: Diff the SPL before and after the change.
Determine whether the change narrows the search's matching scope.
response_guidance: Revert to the version-controlled definition if the change was not part of an approved tuning process.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security Correlation Search Schedule or Throttle Changed
description: A security correlation search's schedule was lengthened (reducing detection latency to unacceptable levels) or its throttle/suppression window was extended (causing repeat malicious activity to go unalerted after the first occurrence).

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Schedule/throttle-change events joined against a security-content tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events touching cron_schedule or alert.suppress.period, restricted to security-tagged searches.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search (info="*cron_schedule*" OR info="*alert.suppress*")
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection
| where is_security_detection=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against detection-engineering change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the schedule/throttle before and after.
Assess the resulting detection-latency or suppression impact.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Notable/Risk Alert Action Removed from Correlation Search
description: A correlation search's notable-event or risk-scoring alert action was removed while the search itself remains enabled — the search continues to run and match, but produces no notable event or risk score, so the SOC never sees the result even though the underlying detection logic is technically still executing.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Alert-action removal events for the notable/risk action specifically.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events where action.notable or action.risk transitions from enabled to disabled.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search (info="*action.notable*0*" OR info="*action.risk*0*")
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection
| where is_security_detection=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; this is a particularly deceptive form of tampering since the search's enabled/schedule status alone will not reveal it.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Re-enable immediately.
response_guidance: Re-enable the notable/risk action immediately and retroactively review the search's matches during the exposure window.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Detection Modified Immediately Before Matching Malicious Activity
description: A security correlation search was disabled, deleted, or had its SPL/notable action modified, and within a short window the raw activity that search was designed to catch occurred anyway (as evidenced by the underlying source data) — the highest-confidence signal in this entire catalogue that detection tampering was deliberate and targeted rather than incidental tuning.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Detection-tampering event (SPL-KO-001/002/003/005) followed by the raw activity the modified detection targets, using the detection's own search logic against the raw source
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: tampering, then the activity it hid.

detection_logic: A meta-correlation that re-runs each disabled/modified security search's own underlying SPL against the exposure window to check whether it would have matched anything had it remained active.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search (info=deleted OR info="*disabled=1*")
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection, underlying_search
| where is_security_detection=1
| map search="search $underlying_search$ earliest=$_time$ latest=$_time$+3600" maxsearches=50
tuning_guidance: Requires each security detection's own SPL to be re-executable in isolation via the underlying_search lookup field; a strong Tier-1 candidate given how rare and severe a true positive would be.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, deliberate defense-evasion incident.
Immediately restore the detection and investigate the matching activity as a live incident in its own right.
response_guidance: Full incident response on both the tampering and the underlying activity it was meant to catch.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Uses the map command against a small, pre-filtered set of tampering events only (never against the full search population); still expensive per-run — schedule at a low frequency (hourly) rather than real-time, and cap maxsearches.

title: Widely-Used Macro Modified
description: A macro referenced by many saved searches was modified — since macros are expanded inline at search time, a single malicious edit here silently propagates into every search that calls the macro, making it a uniquely high-leverage tampering target: one change, many affected detections.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Macro modification events joined against a reference-count lookup.

detection_logic: Filters macro-modification events where the macro's reference count (number of searches invoking it) exceeds a threshold in a maintained lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_macro
| lookup macro_reference_counts.csv macro_name AS object OUTPUT reference_count
| where reference_count>=5
| table _time, user, object, info, reference_count
tuning_guidance: Maintain the reference-count lookup by parsing saved-search SPL for macro invocations (`macro_name`); confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the macro's definition before and after.
Enumerate every search that references this macro and assess the blast radius of the change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized; re-verify every dependent search's behavior.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Macro Modified to Contain Suspicious SPL
description: A macro's definition was modified to include content matching suspicious patterns — a NOT clause that excludes a specific host/user/IP from every search that calls it, a subsearch against an unexpected index, or a reference to lookup/eval logic that could exfiltrate or mask data — hidden inside logic most reviewers assume is benign string substitution.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Macro modification events whose new definition matches a suspicious-pattern regex.

detection_logic: Filters macro-modification events where the new definition matches patterns like a hardcoded NOT-exclusion, an outbound lookup to an external file, or a sendemail/script reference.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_macro
| rex field=info "definition=(?<new_def>.+)"
| where match(new_def, "(?i)(NOT (host|user|src)=|outputlookup|sendemail|script\()")
| table _time, user, object, new_def
tuning_guidance: Tune the suspicious-pattern regex to your environment's legitimate macro-usage conventions to reduce false positives.
investigation_steps: Review the full macro definition for intent.
Enumerate dependent searches (SPL-KO-007) and assess impact.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if malicious intent is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Macro Permissions Broadened to Global Sharing
description: A macro's sharing level was broadened to global, making it available for any user in any app to reference — increasing both its exposure to tampering by less-trusted accounts and the number of searches that might inadvertently or maliciously come to depend on it.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Macro sharing-level configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters macro-modification events where sharing changes to global.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_macro info="*sharing=global*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; many legitimate macros are intentionally global.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unnecessary.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Lookup File Modified or Overwritten
description: A CSV lookup file's content was replaced or modified, which — depending on the lookup's purpose — can weaken threat-intelligence matching, remove asset/identity enrichment, or alter the baselines this catalogue's own behavioral detections depend on.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Lookup file edit/upload events.

detection_logic: Filters lookup-file modification audit events, joined against a lookup-purpose tag identifying threat-intel/allowlist/baseline files for priority triage.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup
| lookup lookup_purpose.csv lookup_name AS object OUTPUT purpose
| table _time, user, object, purpose
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; prioritize alerts for lookups tagged threat-intel or allowlist over general-purpose reference data.
investigation_steps: Diff the lookup content before and after.
Determine what searches depend on it.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Threat-Intelligence Lookup Manipulated to Remove Indicators
description: A lookup file tagged as threat-intelligence had its indicator count decrease significantly compared to the prior version — meaning IOCs were removed rather than the expected append-only growth of a threat-intel feed, which can be used to deliberately blind IOC-matching detections against a specific known-malicious indicator.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Threat-intel lookup modification events compared to the prior version's row count.

detection_logic: Compares each threat-intel lookup edit's resulting row count against its immediately prior version and flags decreases.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup
| lookup lookup_purpose.csv lookup_name AS object OUTPUT purpose
| where purpose="threat-intel"
| eval row_count=<row_count_field>
| streamstats window=2 current=f last(row_count) AS prior_row_count by object
| where row_count<prior_row_count
| table _time, user, object, row_count, prior_row_count
tuning_guidance: Requires a way to compute row_count on each edit (e.g. a scheduled search comparing lookup snapshots); exclude scheduled feed-refresh jobs that legitimately prune expired/stale indicators.
investigation_steps: Diff the specific indicators removed.
Determine whether any of the removed indicators correspond to current or recent malicious activity.
response_guidance: Restore the removed indicators immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Allowlist Entry Added with Broad Wildcard Scope
description: A new entry was added to an allowlist/exception lookup using an overly broad wildcard pattern (e.g. a full /8 CIDR, a bare domain suffix, or a wildcard username), which can silently suppress detection coverage for far more activity than a legitimate, narrowly-scoped exception would require.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Allowlist/exception lookup edit events where the added entry contains a broad wildcard.

detection_logic: Filters lookup-edit events on allowlist-tagged lookups where the newly added row's key field matches a broad wildcard pattern.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup
| lookup lookup_purpose.csv lookup_name AS object OUTPUT purpose
| where purpose="allowlist"
| where match(new_entry, "\*$") OR match(new_entry, "/(8|16)$")
| table _time, user, object, new_entry
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; scope the wildcard-breadth regex to your environment's naming conventions.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the broad scope.
Narrow the exception to the minimum necessary scope.
response_guidance: Revert to a narrowly-scoped entry if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Known-Malicious Entity Added to Allowlist
description: An entry was added to an allowlist matching an indicator currently or recently present in the threat-intelligence lookup, meaning an entity flagged as malicious was simultaneously (or subsequently) exempted from detection.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_lookup, correlated against the threat-intel lookup
data_sources.description: Allowlist additions cross-referenced against active threat-intel indicators.

detection_logic: Joins new allowlist entries against the current threat-intel lookup for a match.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup
| lookup lookup_purpose.csv lookup_name AS object OUTPUT purpose
| where purpose="allowlist"
| lookup threat_intel_indicators.csv indicator AS new_entry OUTPUT is_known_malicious
| where is_known_malicious=1
| table _time, user, object, new_entry
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; essentially no legitimate reason to allowlist a currently-flagged malicious indicator.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed defense-evasion incident.
Investigate why this specific indicator was targeted for exemption.
response_guidance: Remove the allowlist entry immediately and investigate the actor's broader activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Large Number of Allowlist/Exception Entries Created
description: An unusually large number of allowlist/exception entries were added in a short window, consistent with a bulk, scripted attempt to suppress detection coverage across many entities at once rather than routine, incremental tuning.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Allowlist-lookup edit events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts allowlist-lookup edit events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup
| lookup lookup_purpose.csv lookup_name AS object OUTPUT purpose
| where purpose="allowlist"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count by _time, user
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known bulk-tuning projects with a documented change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented tuning project.
Review the specific entries added.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Field Alias or Calculated Field Suppressing Security Field
description: A field alias or calculated field was modified in a way that overwrites a CIM-relevant field name (e.g. aliasing a benign field onto 'user' or 'action', masking the real value), which can break the field-based filtering that many of this catalogue's detections and Enterprise Security's CIM-driven correlation searches depend on.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Field-alias/calculated-field modification events targeting CIM-relevant field names.

detection_logic: Filters field-alias/calculated-field modification events where the target field name matches a CIM-critical field on a maintained lookup (user, src, dest, action, signature).
spl:
index=_audit (action=edit_field_alias OR action=edit_calc_field)
| lookup cim_critical_fields.csv field_name OUTPUT is_cim_critical
| where is_cim_critical=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against field-extraction/CIM-mapping change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the field definition before and after.
Determine what searches/data models depend on the affected field.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and verify dependent detections resume matching correctly.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Data Model Object Removed or Constraint Changed
description: A data model object (e.g. the Authentication or Change data model used throughout Enterprise Security) had a field or object removed, or its base search constraint narrowed — which can silently reduce what data populates the model without disabling the model or its acceleration outright.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Data model configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters data model modification events, restricted to CIM-standard data models on a maintained lookup for priority triage.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_datamodel
| lookup cim_datamodels.csv datamodel_name AS object OUTPUT is_cim_standard
| where is_cim_standard=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against data-model-engineering change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the data model definition before and after.
Check for a subsequent drop in the model's populated event count (SPL-KO-018).
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Data Model Acceleration Disabled
description: Acceleration was disabled on a data model, which — for any tstats-based correlation search relying on that model — causes the search to either fail or silently fall back to a much slower, potentially timing-out raw search, degrading or breaking detection coverage that depends on it.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Data model acceleration-disable events.

detection_logic: Filters data model modification events where acceleration.enabled transitions to 0.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_datamodel info="*acceleration.enabled=0*"
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences for CIM-standard data models used by security correlation searches.
investigation_steps: Re-enable immediately.
Identify every tstats-based correlation search that depends on this model.
response_guidance: Re-enable acceleration immediately and verify dependent searches resume normal behavior.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Data Model Coverage Sharply Declines
description: The volume of events populating a CIM data model dropped sharply compared to its historical baseline without a corresponding drop in the underlying raw source data, indicating the model's tag/eventtype classification (rather than the source data itself) has been broken — whether through SPL-TAG tampering, source-parsing changes, or the data model's own constraint being narrowed.

data_sources.name: tstats
data_sources.description: Data model event-count trend compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Runs a scheduled tstats count against each CIM-standard data model and compares to its own trailing baseline.
spl:
| tstats count from datamodel=Authentication by _time span=1h
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count stdev(count) AS stdev_count
| where count < (avg_count - 3*stdev_count)
tuning_guidance: Run per data model on a schedule; correlate with SPL-INT audit/internal log-gap detections to rule out a broader ingestion outage before attributing to tag/model tampering specifically.
investigation_steps: Confirm the raw source data volume for the model's underlying sourcetypes is stable (rules out an ingestion problem).
If raw volume is stable but model coverage dropped, investigate tag/eventtype/constraint changes.
response_guidance: Restore the tag/eventtype/constraint configuration and verify model coverage recovers.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security-Relevant Tag Removed from Event Type
description: A tag such as 'authentication', 'malware', or 'attack' was removed from an event type, which — since data models and many correlation searches filter on tags rather than raw sourcetype — can silently exclude matching data from CIM-based detection coverage without altering the underlying event type's search definition at all.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Tag-removal events targeting CIM-relevant tags.

detection_logic: Filters tag-modification events where a CIM-relevant tag is removed from an event type on a maintained lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tags
| lookup cim_critical_tags.csv tag_name OUTPUT is_cim_critical
| where is_cim_critical=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against CIM-mapping change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for a corresponding drop in data model coverage (SPL-KO-018).
response_guidance: Restore the tag if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Event Type Definition Changed to Narrow Classification
description: An event type's search definition was modified, potentially narrowing which raw events are classified under that event type — the same net effect as tag removal (SPL-KO-019) but achieved by editing the classification criteria directly rather than the applied tags.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Event type search-definition modification events.

detection_logic: Filters event type modification events for security-relevant event types on a maintained lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_eventtype
| lookup security_eventtypes.csv eventtype_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_relevant
| where is_security_relevant=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against CIM-mapping change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the search definition before and after.
Assess classification impact.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security Dashboard Panel SPL Changed
description: A panel's underlying SPL was modified on a dashboard used by the SOC for triage/investigation, which can present analysts with an incomplete or misleading view of security-relevant activity without touching any underlying detection logic.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Dashboard/view modification events.

detection_logic: Filters dashboard-modification events for dashboards tagged as SOC-facing on a maintained lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_view
| lookup soc_dashboards.csv view_name AS object OUTPUT is_soc_facing
| where is_soc_facing=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against dashboard-development change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the dashboard's panel SPL before and after.
Confirm the change does not omit or misrepresent security-relevant data.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Dashboard Deleted or Permissions Changed
description: A dashboard was deleted, or its sharing permissions were changed, either removing SOC visibility into a specific investigation view or restricting/expanding who can see the data it presents.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Dashboard deletion/permission-change events.

detection_logic: Filters dashboard deletion and sharing-change events for SOC-facing dashboards.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_view (info=deleted OR info="*sharing*")
| lookup soc_dashboards.csv view_name AS object OUTPUT is_soc_facing
| where is_soc_facing=1
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Restore from version control if unauthorized.
response_guidance: Restore if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deceptive Dashboard Panel Created with External Link
description: A dashboard panel or workflow action was created containing a link to an external URL, which — since SOC analysts routinely click links embedded in trusted internal dashboards during investigations — is a plausible phishing/malware-delivery vector against the security team itself.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Dashboard/workflow-action creation events whose content includes an external hyperlink.

detection_logic: Filters dashboard/workflow-action modification events where the definition contains an href/link to a domain not on a maintained internal-domain allowlist.
spl:
index=_audit (action=edit_view OR action=edit_workflow_action)
| rex field=info "href=[\"'](?<link_url>https?://[^\"']+)"
| lookup internal_domains.csv domain OUTPUT is_internal
| where isnotnull(link_url) AND isnull(is_internal)
| table _time, user, object, link_url
tuning_guidance: Maintain an internal-domain allowlist; scope to SOC-facing dashboards/apps for the highest-value alerting.
investigation_steps: Inspect the destination URL for phishing/malware indicators before anyone clicks it.
Remove the link pending review.
response_guidance: Remove the link immediately if it points to an unrecognized or suspicious domain.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Workflow Action Sends Field Data to External Destination
description: A workflow action was created or modified to submit event field values (potentially including sensitive fields like usernames, IPs, or hashes) to an external URL via a GET/POST link — since analysts trigger workflow actions routinely during investigations, this can become a low-visibility, per-click exfiltration channel.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Workflow-action modification events whose link/URI targets an external destination.

detection_logic: Filters workflow-action modification events where the destination URI is external and includes field-value template substitution ($field$).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_workflow_action
| rex field=info "link\.uri=(?<workflow_uri>[^;]+)"
| lookup internal_domains.csv domain OUTPUT is_internal
| where match(workflow_uri, "\$\w+\$") AND isnull(is_internal)
| table _time, user, object, workflow_uri
tuning_guidance: Maintain an internal-domain allowlist for legitimate external enrichment integrations (e.g. a threat-intel lookup service).
investigation_steps: Verify the destination is an approved, authorized integration.
Determine what field values this workflow action has historically sent.
response_guidance: Remove/revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Knowledge Object Ownership Reassigned at Scale
description: A single actor reassigned ownership of an unusually large number of knowledge objects (saved searches, macros, lookups, dashboards) in a short window — since a search runs with its owner's effective permissions, mass reassignment can be used to consolidate a broad set of objects (including detection logic) under an attacker-controlled account, or to take over orphaned admin-owned detections after compromising the admin account.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Ownership-change events across all knowledge-object types, aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts ownership-change events across all knowledge-object action types per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_* info="*owner*"
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats count values(object) AS objects values(action) AS types by _time, user
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known bulk app-migration/reorganization projects.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented migration project.
Treat as a live incident absent one, especially if security-content objects are among those reassigned.
response_guidance: Revert ownership if unauthorized; investigate the acting account for compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New App Installed
description: A new app was installed on the Splunk instance. On Splunk Enterprise this can introduce arbitrary scripted inputs, custom commands, and binaries; on Splunk Cloud, self-service app installation is restricted to vetted apps from Splunkbase or private apps passing the Cloud vetting process, narrowing but not eliminating the risk.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App-installation events.

detection_logic: Filters app-installation audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; on Splunk Cloud, cross-reference against the app-vetting approval record.
investigation_steps: Identify the app's source (Splunkbase, private, or unknown).
Review its contents for scripted/modular inputs, custom commands, and binaries (SPL-APP-002 through SPL-APP-006).
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized or unvetted.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: App Installed Outside Change Management Process
description: An app was installed by an actor or through a path not matching the organization's documented app-deployment process (e.g. installed manually via Splunk Web rather than through the CI/CD pipeline or Deployment Server that normally pushes apps), a strong signal of unauthorized change.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App-installation events joined against a known-automation-account lookup.

detection_logic: Filters app-installation events where the acting user is not a known CI/CD or deployment-automation account.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info=created
| lookup deployment_automation_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_automation
| where isnull(is_automation)
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Maintain the automation-account lookup; scope to environments where all app deployment is expected to be automated.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the manual installation.
Review app contents thoroughly given the process bypass.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized and investigate how the process bypass occurred.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scripted Input Created
description: A scripted input was created, configuring splunkd to periodically execute an external script or binary and index its output — the single most direct execution-capable persistence mechanism available through Splunk's own configuration, since inputs.conf changes require no code review process most organizations would apply to actual application deployments.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Scripted-input creation events with the configured script path.

detection_logic: Filters input-creation audit events for scripted (as opposed to file-monitor/network) input stanzas.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_input info=created object="script*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; every scripted input on a production Splunk server should be traceable to an approved deployment.
investigation_steps: Review the script's contents and interpreter.
Check the script's directory permissions and whether it executes from a writable/temp path (SPL-APP-005).
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scripted Input Run Frequency Increased
description: An existing scripted input's execution interval was shortened significantly, which can indicate an attacker tuning a persistence mechanism for faster check-in/callback behavior, or (more benignly) a legitimate performance change.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Scripted-input interval-change events.

detection_logic: Filters scripted-input modification events where the new interval is substantially shorter than the prior value.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_input info="*interval*" object="script*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review what the script actually does at the new cadence.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scripted Input Executes from Writable or Temporary Directory
description: A scripted input references a script located in a world-writable or temporary directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, C:\Windows\Temp) rather than the standard $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/*/bin path, which — since these directories are typically writable by any local user or process — creates a script the attacker could modify at any time without any Splunk-side audit trail of the file's own content changing.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Scripted-input creation events where the script path falls outside the standard app bin directory.

detection_logic: Filters scripted-input creation events where the configured script path matches a known-writable/temp-directory pattern.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_input info=created object="script*"
| rex field=object "script://(?<script_path>.+)"
| where match(script_path, "(?i)^(/tmp/|/var/tmp/|C:\\\\Windows\\\\Temp)")
| table _time, user, object, script_path
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; there is essentially no legitimate reason for a production scripted input to run from a world-writable directory.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Inspect the script's current content immediately using OS-level file-integrity tooling.
response_guidance: Remove the input and investigate the underlying host for compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Scripted Input Downloads External Content or Launches a Shell
description: OS-level process telemetry shows the Splunk service account's scripted-input execution spawning a shell interpreter or a network-fetch utility (curl, wget, Invoke-WebRequest), consistent with a scripted input being used as a download-and-execute or reverse-shell mechanism rather than legitimate data collection.

data_sources.name: Sysmon / auditd
data_sources.path: process creation events where the parent process is splunkd
data_sources.description: Process-execution telemetry for children of the Splunk service process.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events where the parent process is splunkd and the child process is a shell interpreter or network-fetch utility.
spl:
index=<endpoint_index> sourcetype IN (Sysmon, auditd) parent_process_name="splunkd*"
| where match(process_name, "(?i)^(bash|sh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|curl|wget)$")
| table _time, host, parent_process_name, process_name, command_line
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level process telemetry (Sysmon on Windows, auditd on Linux) — not visible from Splunk's own internal logs alone; exclude any documented scripted input that legitimately shells out (rare and should itself be flagged for review).
investigation_steps: Treat as a live compromise indicator.
Identify the originating scripted input and isolate the host.
response_guidance: Isolate the host, remove the scripted input, and conduct full incident response on the underlying Splunk server.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1105: Ingress Tool Transfer

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Modular Input Created or Credential Changed
description: A modular input (a packaged, structured alternative to a bare scripted input, typically implemented in Python and stored encrypted credentials in the app's passwords.conf/secure storage) was created, or its stored credential was changed — either action deserves the same scrutiny as scripted-input creation given the equivalent execution and data-collection capability.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Modular-input configuration and credential-change events.

detection_logic: Filters modular-input creation and credential-change audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_modular_input
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the modular input's app source and implementation.
Confirm the credential change was authorized.
response_guidance: Remove/revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Modular Input Collection Endpoint Redirected
description: A modular input's target collection endpoint (e.g. a cloud API, syslog source, or database connection string) was changed to a new value, which — for inputs that pull rather than push data — can redirect what Splunk collects, or (for inputs implementing their own outbound calls) redirect where collected data is sent.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Modular-input endpoint/connection configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters modular-input modification events touching endpoint/URL/connection-string configuration fields.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_modular_input info="*endpoint*" OR info="*url*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new endpoint is the expected, authorized source/destination.
Determine the resulting change in what data is collected or where it flows.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1560: Archive Collected Data

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Custom Search Command Installed
description: A custom search command (defined in an app's commands.conf, backed by a Python script) was installed, extending SPL's own vocabulary with arbitrary code that executes on the search head every time any user's SPL invokes it — a particularly stealthy execution vector since the command appears as ordinary SPL to anyone reviewing a search.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_app OR local commands.conf change
data_sources.description: App-installation/modification events introducing a new commands.conf stanza.

detection_logic: Filters app changes that introduce a new custom search command, using an app-content diff against commands.conf where available.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app
| lookup app_commands_baseline.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT prior_commands
| where isnotnull(new_commands) AND new_commands!=prior_commands
| table _time, user, object, new_commands
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained baseline of each app's commands.conf stanzas, refreshed on every legitimate app update; confirm against change tickets for new commands.
investigation_steps: Review the command's Python implementation for malicious logic.
Check where the command is invoked once installed.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized or malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Custom Search Command Python Implementation Modified
description: An existing custom search command's Python implementation file was modified without a corresponding app-version bump, which — since the command may be invoked by many existing searches unaware of the change — is a high-leverage code-injection point similar in effect to the macro-tampering detections (SPL-KO-007/008) but with direct code-execution capability rather than SPL-text substitution.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.path: file-integrity-monitoring events for $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/*/bin/*.py files backing commands.conf stanzas
data_sources.description: File-modification events for custom-command implementation files.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level file-integrity monitoring on app bin directories; flags modifications to Python files backing an existing commands.conf stanza where the app's version metadata did not also change.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/apps/*/bin/*.py"
| lookup custom_command_files.csv file_path OUTPUT is_command_implementation
| where is_command_implementation=1
| table _time, file_path, user, action
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage of Splunk app bin directories, not available from Splunk's own internal logs; a Splunk Cloud limitation — see docs for the customer-visible alternative.
investigation_steps: Diff the file content against the last known-good version.
Determine every search that invokes this command.
response_guidance: Restore the known-good version immediately and audit for unauthorized code execution since the change.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Custom Search Command Used by Unusual User
description: A custom search command was invoked by a user who has never used it before and whose role does not typically overlap with the app that ships it, which can indicate either legitimate cross-team exploration or a compromised account probing available execution capability.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events invoking a custom command, compared against a per-user command-usage baseline.

detection_logic: Parses custom-command invocations out of search text and compares against each user's historical command-usage baseline.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted
| rex max_match=0 field=search "\|\s*(?<command_used>[a-z_]+)"
| lookup custom_commands.csv command_name AS command_used OUTPUT is_custom
| where is_custom=1
| lookup update=true user_command_baseline.csv user, command_used OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, command_used
tuning_guidance: Requires both a custom-command inventory lookup and a per-user command-usage baseline; expect noise for broadly-used custom commands.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review what the command was used to accomplish in this instance.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Alert Action Script Created or Modified
description: A custom alert action's backing script was created or modified — since alert actions execute automatically whenever their associated saved search fires (which may be scheduled to run frequently against broad data), this is one of the most reliably-triggered execution mechanisms available through Splunk's own configuration.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_app referencing an alert_actions.conf change, or FIM on the backing script
data_sources.description: Alert-action configuration and script-content change events.

detection_logic: Filters app-configuration changes touching alert_actions.conf stanzas, cross-referenced with FIM on the backing script where available.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app
| lookup alert_action_apps.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT has_alert_action
| where has_alert_action=1
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained lookup of apps shipping alert actions; confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the alert action's script for malicious logic.
Enumerate every saved search configured to invoke it.
response_guidance: Remove/revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Alert Action Webhook Destination Changed
description: A saved search's webhook alert-action URL was changed to a new destination, which — since webhook actions POST the search's result payload to the configured URL on every trigger — is a durable, low-visibility exfiltration channel once redirected to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Webhook URL configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events touching the webhook action's URL parameter, restricted to destinations not on an internal-domain allowlist.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*action.webhook.param.url*"
| rex field=info "action\.webhook\.param\.url=(?<webhook_url>\S+)"
| lookup internal_domains.csv domain OUTPUT is_internal
| where isnull(is_internal)
| table _time, user, object, webhook_url
tuning_guidance: Maintain an internal/approved-webhook-domain allowlist; confirm against change tickets for legitimate new integrations.
investigation_steps: Verify the new destination is authorized.
Determine what data the associated search regularly produces.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unrecognized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Alert Email Action Recipient Broadened to External Domain
description: A saved search's email alert-action recipient list was changed to include an address outside the organization's approved email domains, redirecting the search's regularly-produced output (which may include sensitive data) to an external mailbox.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Email alert-action recipient configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events where the email recipient field includes a domain not on the organization's approved-domain list.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*action.email.to*"
| rex field=info "action\.email\.to=(?<recipients>[^;]+)"
| where NOT match(recipients, "(?i)@(yourcompany\.com)$")
| table _time, user, object, recipients
tuning_guidance: Replace the domain pattern with your organization's actual approved domain(s); confirm against change tickets for legitimate external partner reporting.
investigation_steps: Verify the external recipient is authorized.
Review what data this search regularly produces.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Webhook Endpoint Created
description: A saved search was newly configured with a webhook alert action. Routine for legitimate ChatOps/ITSM integrations, but a necessary building block for detecting webhook-based exfiltration (SPL-APP-013, SPL-APP-016).

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Webhook action-enablement events.

detection_logic: Filters saved-search modification events where the webhook action transitions from disabled to enabled.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*action.webhook=1*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the destination URL (SPL-APP-013).
response_guidance: No standalone action.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: High Volume of Webhook Calls from a Single Search
description: A single saved search's webhook action fired an unusually large number of times in a short window, consistent with either a misconfigured alert-per-result setting (each matching row triggering its own webhook call) or a deliberate high-frequency exfiltration channel.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Webhook action-execution events aggregated per saved search per window.

detection_logic: Counts webhook action-execution events per saved search within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=AlertActionsProcess action=webhook status=success
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count by _time, savedsearch_name
| where count>=50
tuning_guidance: Exclude known per-result alerting integrations with a legitimately high call volume.
investigation_steps: Determine if this is a misconfiguration (per-result vs. digest mode) or deliberate.
Review the destination and the data sent.
response_guidance: Reconfigure to digest mode if accidental; investigate if deliberate.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sensitive Field Data Sent to Webhook
description: A webhook action fired for a search whose underlying SPL references a sensitive index, meaning the webhook payload — sent to whatever destination is configured — likely contains sensitive data by extension.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Webhook action-execution events joined against the originating search's index references
data_sources.description: Correlation between a webhook-firing search and sensitive-index references.

detection_logic: Joins webhook execution events against the saved search's own definition, filtered to sensitive-index references.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=AlertActionsProcess action=webhook status=success
| join type=inner savedsearch_name [search index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search | rename object AS savedsearch_name | rex field=info "search=(?<search_text>[^;]+)" | where match(search_text, "(?i)index=(security|authentication|audit|identity)")]
| table _time, savedsearch_name, search_text
tuning_guidance: Confirm against approved integrations; escalate only when paired with SPL-APP-013's unrecognized-destination signal.
investigation_steps: Verify the webhook destination is authorized for sensitive data.
Review the actual payload schema being sent if the integration supports inspection.
response_guidance: Disable if the destination is unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: App Disabled or Removed
description: An app was disabled or removed, which — if the app provides security detections, data inputs, or CIM knowledge — can remove functionality without any single knowledge-object-level detection catching it, since the app's contents disappear as a unit.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App disable/removal events joined against a security-app tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters app disable/removal events, prioritized by a maintained lookup identifying security-relevant apps (ES, TA add-ons for critical sources, custom detection apps).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info IN ("disabled","removed")
| lookup security_relevant_apps.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_relevant
| table _time, user, object, info, is_security_relevant
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; treat security-relevant app disables/removals as high priority.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess what detection/ingestion coverage was lost.
response_guidance: Re-enable/reinstall immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unsigned or Unapproved App Source
description: An installed app is not present on the organization's approved-app inventory (whether internally built and code-reviewed, or a vetted Splunkbase download with a recorded checksum), regardless of whether it passed Splunk Cloud's own vetting for externally-sourced content.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App-installation events joined against an approved-app inventory lookup.

detection_logic: Joins app-installation events against a maintained approved-app inventory and flags any app not present.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info=created
| lookup approved_apps.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Requires and depends entirely on a maintained approved-app inventory; high value once established.
investigation_steps: Determine the app's actual source and publisher.
Review its contents thoroughly before deciding whether to add it to the approved inventory or remove it.
response_guidance: Remove pending review if not immediately justifiable.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: App Setup Handler or Custom REST Endpoint Introduced
description: An app was installed or updated introducing a setup handler (setup.xml/app.conf setup script) or a custom REST endpoint (restmap.conf), either of which registers app-controlled code directly into Splunk Web's or the REST API's own request-handling path — a technique conceptually similar to a web-shell in a traditional web application.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_app, cross-referenced with restmap.conf/setup.xml content changes
data_sources.description: App changes introducing new REST endpoint or setup-handler stanzas.

detection_logic: Filters app changes where a diff against the app-content baseline shows a new restmap.conf stanza or setup.xml/setup script.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app
| lookup app_restmap_baseline.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT had_restmap
| where isnull(had_restmap) AND now_has_restmap=1
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained app-content baseline; a strong Tier-1 candidate given the severity of custom REST-handler code execution.
investigation_steps: Review the REST endpoint's implementation for authentication bypass or arbitrary command execution.
Determine what URL path it registers.
response_guidance: Remove immediately if unauthorized or malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1505: Server Software Component

author: Threat Detection Library

title: App Introduces Custom Authentication Handler
description: An app was installed or updated introducing a scripted authentication handler (authentication.conf's scriptSearchFilters/scriptPath), which — since it can run in place of or alongside Splunk's own authentication logic — could be used to build a hardcoded backdoor credential or bypass condition into the login flow itself.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_app, cross-referenced with authentication.conf scripted-auth stanzas
data_sources.description: App changes introducing a scripted authentication handler.

detection_logic: Filters app changes where a diff against the app-content baseline shows a new scripted-authentication stanza.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app
| lookup app_scripted_auth_baseline.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT had_scripted_auth
| where isnull(had_scripted_auth) AND now_has_scripted_auth=1
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained app-content baseline; alert on all occurrences given the severity.
investigation_steps: Review the script's authentication logic for a hardcoded bypass or backdoor credential.
Treat as a live incident pending review.
response_guidance: Remove immediately and audit all logins since the app was installed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass App Push to Many Hosts via Deployment
description: A single app (whether a genuinely new one or a modified version of an existing app) was pushed to an unusually large number of forwarders/search heads through the Deployment Server or SHC deployer in a short window, which — if the app is malicious — turns a single compromise of the management tier into a fleet-wide compromise. See the dedicated SPL-DS/SPL-SH sections for the deployment-infrastructure-side detections of this same pattern.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: App-deployment events aggregated per app per window across target clients.

detection_logic: Counts distinct deployment-target clients receiving the same app within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component IN (DeployedApplication, ShcDeployer)
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats dc(client_name) AS target_count by _time, app_name
| where target_count>=20
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known org-wide app rollouts with a documented change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a deployment change ticket.
Review the app's contents for anything unexpected.
response_guidance: Halt further rollout and pull the app from affected clients if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New HEC Token Created
description: A new HTTP Event Collector token was created, establishing a new ingestion credential. Routine during legitimate onboarding of a new data source, but a necessary building block for detecting a token created with excessive index scope or by an unauthorized actor.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: HEC token-creation events.

detection_logic: Filters HEC token-creation audit events. Never logs the token value itself.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against onboarding/change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the token's assigned indexes and default sourcetype (SPL-HEC-002).
response_guidance: No standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Token Created with Broad Index Scope
description: A HEC token was created or modified with the ability to write to a wildcard index set or a specific sensitive index (security, authentication, audit), which — since a leaked HEC token allows arbitrary event injection — enables HEC data-poisoning attacks (SPL-HEC-008 onward) against high-value log sources.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: HEC token configuration events with the allowed-indexes list.

detection_logic: Filters HEC token configuration events where the allowed-indexes field includes a wildcard or a sensitive index.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token
| rex field=info "indexes=(?<allowed_indexes>[^;]+)"
| where match(allowed_indexes, "\*") OR match(allowed_indexes, "(?i)(security|authentication|audit)")
| table _time, user, object, allowed_indexes
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; scope every token to the minimum required index set.
investigation_steps: Verify the scope against the token's documented use case.
Narrow the scope if broader than necessary.
response_guidance: Restrict the token's index scope if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Token Deleted
description: A HEC token was deleted, which will silently stop ingestion from every legitimate source still configured to use it — a potential availability/logging-gap issue if unauthorized or accidental.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: HEC token-deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters HEC token-deletion audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token info=deleted
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; correlate with a subsequent ingestion-volume drop for sources known to use this token.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Identify what sources were sending via this token.
response_guidance: Re-create if unauthorized and update the affected sources.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Token Disabled and Re-Enabled in Short Window
description: A HEC token was disabled and then re-enabled within a short window, which can indicate an attacker briefly interrupting ingestion for a specific source (to inject or suppress events during the gap) while minimizing the duration of any resulting ingestion-gap alert.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Token disable/enable events for the same token in sequence.

detection_logic: Correlates a token-disable event followed by a token-enable event for the same token within a short window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token (info="*disabled=1*" OR info="*disabled=0*")
| transaction object maxspan=15m
| where mvcount(info)>1
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change/maintenance tickets.
investigation_steps: Check for a data gap or anomalous event burst during the disabled window.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Authentication Failure Burst
description: A source repeatedly submitted HEC events with an invalid or unrecognized token, consistent with an attacker brute-forcing or guessing HEC token values, or a misconfigured legitimate sender.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: HEC endpoint 401 (unauthorized) responses.

detection_logic: Counts HEC 401 responses per source IP within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/services/collector*" status=401
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, clientip
| where count>=20
tuning_guidance: Exclude known misconfigured legitimate senders after confirming with the owning team.
investigation_steps: Determine if the source is internal (misconfiguration) or external (brute-force attempt).
Block the source if malicious.
response_guidance: Block the source if externally originated and malicious.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Source IP Sending via Existing HEC Token
description: An established HEC token began receiving events from a source IP never previously associated with it, which — since a HEC token is a bearer credential with no inherent IP binding — can indicate the token was exfiltrated and is being used by an attacker to inject events (or, in a legitimate-use case, that the sending infrastructure moved/scaled).

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: Successful HEC submissions compared against a per-token source-IP baseline.

detection_logic: Joins successful HEC submissions against a lookup of each token's previously-seen source IPs.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/services/collector*" status=200
| lookup update=true hec_token_src_baseline.csv token_identity, clientip OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, token_identity, clientip
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-token source-IP baseline; expect noise for tokens used by autoscaling infrastructure with rotating IPs — exclude via a CIDR-range allowlist per token.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new source is expected sending infrastructure.
If not, rotate the token immediately.
response_guidance: Rotate the token if the new source cannot be confirmed as legitimate.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Token Used from Unexpected Network
description: A HEC submission arrived from a source IP outside the organization's expected sending-infrastructure CIDR ranges (internal networks, known cloud-provider egress ranges), which — combined with a valid token — suggests either the token or the sending host has been compromised.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: Successful HEC submissions with source IP outside expected network ranges.

detection_logic: Filters successful HEC submissions where the source IP falls outside a maintained expected-network lookup.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/services/collector*" status=200
| lookup expected_hec_networks.csv clientip OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, token_identity, clientip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-network CIDR lookup; a strong candidate for a Tier-1 alert once tuned.
investigation_steps: Determine ownership of the unexpected source.
Rotate the token if compromise is suspected.
response_guidance: Restrict HEC network access via SPL-HEC-011's IP allow-list control if the exposure is structural.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Source Suddenly Changes Event Structure
description: A HEC token that has historically sent events with a consistent field/JSON schema abruptly began sending events with a materially different structure, consistent with HEC data poisoning — either injecting fabricated events shaped to blend into a trusted source's normal traffic, or an attacker testing what a compromised token can get away with before a larger poisoning campaign.

data_sources.name: metrics.log / introspection
data_sources.path: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd HttpInputMetrics OR field-cardinality comparison over ingested events per token
data_sources.description: Ingested event field-schema comparison per token over time.

detection_logic: Compares the set of fields present in recently ingested events per token against the token's historical field-set baseline.
spl:
index=<hec_destination_index> | fields token_identity, *
| stats values(_raw) AS sample by token_identity
| eval field_set=<computed_field_signature>
| lookup update=true hec_field_schema_baseline.csv token_identity OUTPUT baseline_field_set
| where field_set!=baseline_field_set
| table _time, token_identity, field_set, baseline_field_set
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-token field-schema baseline; expect noise from legitimate schema evolution during planned source upgrades.
investigation_steps: Confirm the schema change against a known source-side deployment/upgrade.
If unexplained, treat as probable data poisoning and rotate the token.
response_guidance: Rotate the token and quarantine/flag the affected events for forensic review before they influence any downstream detection or dashboard.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Field-schema comparison across raw event samples is expensive at scale; implement as a scheduled sampling search against a small per-token subset rather than every event, and prefer a summary-indexed field-signature approach over ad-hoc computation.

title: HEC Events with Host or Source Spoofing an Existing Trusted Source
description: A HEC submission set the host or source field to a value matching an existing, trusted data source (e.g. a domain controller's hostname, a firewall's syslog source path) via HEC's client-controlled override fields, which — since downstream detections and analysts often trust host/source values at face value — allows an attacker with any valid HEC token to impersonate a high-trust log source.

data_sources.name: metrics.log / HEC ingestion metadata
data_sources.description: HEC-ingested events where the client-supplied host/source override matches a known trusted-source identity, joined against a lookup of which token is authorized to claim that identity.

detection_logic: Joins ingested events' host/source fields against a lookup of trusted source identities and their single authorized token, flagging mismatches.
spl:
index=<hec_destination_index>
| lookup trusted_source_identity.csv host OUTPUT authorized_token
| where isnotnull(authorized_token) AND token_identity!=authorized_token
| table _time, host, source, token_identity, authorized_token
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained mapping of trusted host/source identities to their single authorized HEC token; disable HEC's ability to override host/source in indexes.conf/inputs.conf where feasible instead of relying solely on detection.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed spoofing incident.
Quarantine the spoofed events and rotate the misused token.
response_guidance: Restrict the offending token's scope and disable client-side host/source override for tokens that don't need it.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Events with Future or Severely Delayed Timestamps
description: HEC events arrived with a client-supplied timestamp significantly in the future or significantly in the past relative to ingestion time, which can be used to make fabricated events appear to have occurred at a different time than they were actually injected — useful for both alibi construction and evading time-bounded correlation searches.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.description: Ingested events comparing _time (client-supplied) against _indextime (ingestion time).

detection_logic: Computes the gap between _time and _indextime for HEC-ingested events and flags gaps exceeding a threshold in either direction.
spl:
index=<hec_destination_index>
| eval time_gap=abs(_indextime-_time)
| where time_gap>86400
| stats count by token_identity, time_gap
| where count>10
tuning_guidance: Exclude known batch-upload/backfill integrations with a legitimate reason for historical timestamps.
investigation_steps: Determine why the source is sending mistimed events.
If unexplained, treat as probable timestamp poisoning.
response_guidance: Rotate the token if malicious intent is suspected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Management/Global Settings Changed
description: HEC's global settings were changed — enabling HEC where it was previously disabled, disabling SSL requirement, or changing the default index — any of which broadly affects every token's behavior rather than a single token's configuration.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: HEC global-settings configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters HEC global-settings configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_http-eventcollector
| table _time, user, info
