tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; alert on all SSL-disable events.
investigation_steps: Diff the settings before and after.
Assess the resulting exposure of all HEC tokens on the instance.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sudden HEC Volume Spike from Single Token
description: A single HEC token's ingestion volume spiked far above its historical baseline, consistent with either a data-poisoning flood (SPL-HEC-013) or a legitimate but unplanned source-side event burst.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.description: Per-token ingestion volume compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Compares each token's per-hour ingestion volume against its own trailing baseline.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=per_index_thruput
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats sum(kb) AS total_kb by _time, token_identity
| eventstats avg(total_kb) AS avg_kb stdev(total_kb) AS stdev_kb by token_identity
| where total_kb > (avg_kb + 3*stdev_kb)
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known source-side incidents (e.g. an upstream system's own error-log flood) before attributing to malicious HEC abuse.
investigation_steps: Determine the cause of the spike.
Check for a corresponding rise in malformed/invalid-event errors (SPL-HEC-013).
response_guidance: Rate-limit or disable the token if the spike is malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC Invalid/Malformed Event Burst
description: A burst of malformed or oversized events was submitted to a HEC token, consistent with an attacker probing HEC's parsing behavior for a denial-of-service vector or simply flooding the endpoint with garbage to consume indexing capacity.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: HEC endpoint 400 (bad request) responses.

detection_logic: Counts HEC 400 responses per source within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/services/collector*" status=400
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, clientip
| where count>=50
tuning_guidance: Exclude known misconfigured legitimate senders after confirming with the owning team.
investigation_steps: Determine if the source is malfunctioning or deliberately probing.
Block if malicious.
response_guidance: Rate-limit or block the source.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: High-Concurrency HEC Request Volume
description: An unusually large number of concurrent HEC connections/requests were observed, consistent with a denial-of-service attempt against the HEC listener specifically, distinct from the general volume-based detection (SPL-HEC-012) in that it targets connection-level saturation rather than event-volume saturation.

data_sources.name: introspection_generator
data_sources.description: HEC concurrent-connection introspection metrics.

detection_logic: Compares HEC active-connection counts against a capacity-informed threshold.
spl:
index=_introspection component=HttpEventCollector
| where active_connections>=500
| table _time, active_connections
tuning_guidance: Tune the threshold to your HEC deployment's actual configured connection limits.
investigation_steps: Identify the source(s) of the connection volume.
Assess resulting indexing-pipeline health.
response_guidance: Rate-limit or block offending sources; consider HEC-specific load balancing/scaling if the volume is legitimate but unplanned.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sensitive Index Poisoned via HEC
description: A HEC token scoped to a sensitive index (security, authentication, audit) exhibited a schema-change or host-spoofing anomaly (SPL-HEC-008/SPL-HEC-009) — the combination of write access to a high-value index and an active poisoning indicator makes this the flagship, highest-priority HEC detection in this catalogue.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: SPL-HEC-008/SPL-HEC-009 poisoning indicators restricted to tokens scoped to sensitive indexes
data_sources.description: Correlation between sensitive-index token scope and poisoning behavior.

detection_logic: Joins SPL-HEC-008/SPL-HEC-009-style poisoning indicators against the sensitive-index token-scope lookup from SPL-HEC-002.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token
| rex field=info "indexes=(?<allowed_indexes>[^;]+)"
| where match(allowed_indexes, "(?i)(security|authentication|audit)")
| rename object AS token_identity
| join type=inner token_identity [search index=<hec_destination_index> | eval field_set=<computed_field_signature> | lookup hec_field_schema_baseline.csv token_identity OUTPUT baseline_field_set | where field_set!=baseline_field_set]
| table _time, token_identity, allowed_indexes
tuning_guidance: A Tier-1 candidate given the combined severity; investigate every match as a live incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed data-integrity incident against a sensitive index.
Quarantine the affected events and rotate the token immediately.
response_guidance: Full incident response: rotate the token, quarantine/flag poisoned events, and audit any detection or investigation that may have relied on the poisoned data.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Inherits the cost profile of SPL-HEC-008; schedule at a low frequency and scope to sensitive-index tokens only (a small subset) to keep the join tractable.

title: New Index Created
description: A new index was created. Routine during legitimate onboarding of a new data source, but the necessary building block for detecting a subsequent data-diversion pattern (SPL-DATA-011) where a security source's data is redirected to a new, unmonitored index.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Index-creation events.

detection_logic: Filters index-creation audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: No standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Index Deleted or Disabled
description: An index was deleted or disabled — since deleting an index configuration on Splunk Enterprise can be a precursor to removing the underlying bucket data entirely, and disabling an index silently halts both ingestion and search access to it, this is one of the most severe available forms of evidence destruction against the platform.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Index deletion/disable events.

detection_logic: Filters index deletion/disable audit events, prioritized by a sensitive-index lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes info IN ("deleted","disabled")
| lookup sensitive_indexes.csv index_name AS object OUTPUT is_sensitive
| table _time, user, object, info, is_sensitive
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences for sensitive indexes; confirm against change tickets otherwise.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent an approved decommission ticket.
Determine whether underlying bucket data still exists on disk (on-premises only).
response_guidance: Re-enable/restore immediately if unauthorized; preserve any remaining bucket data for forensics.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Index Retention Shortened
description: An index's retention setting (frozenTimePeriodInSecs or equivalent) was shortened, which accelerates when data ages out and becomes unavailable for search — a direct, structural mechanism for evidence destruction that operates silently over time rather than through an immediate, obviously-suspicious deletion action.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Index retention-configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters index configuration-change events where the new frozenTimePeriodInSecs value is lower than the prior value.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes info="*frozenTimePeriodInSecs*"
| rex field=info "frozenTimePeriodInSecs=(?<new_retention>\d+)"
| lookup update=true index_retention_baseline.csv object OUTPUT prior_retention
| where new_retention<prior_retention
| table _time, user, object, prior_retention, new_retention
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences for sensitive/compliance-relevant indexes; confirm against a documented retention-policy change for others.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent an approved retention-policy ticket.
Determine how much historical data will now be lost and by when.
response_guidance: Revert immediately and export any data at imminent risk of aging out before the reversion takes effect.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Index Max Size Reduced Drastically
description: An index's maximum size configuration (maxTotalDataSizeMB or equivalent) was reduced drastically, which can force older data to be frozen/aged out prematurely once the (now much smaller) size cap is reached, achieving an effect similar to a retention-period shortening through a different configuration lever.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Index max-size configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters index configuration-change events where the new max-size value is substantially lower than the prior value.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes info="*maxTotalDataSizeMB*"
| rex field=info "maxTotalDataSizeMB=(?<new_size>\d+)"
| lookup update=true index_size_baseline.csv object OUTPUT prior_size
| where new_size<(prior_size*0.5)
| table _time, user, object, prior_size, new_size
tuning_guidance: Confirm against capacity-planning change tickets; alert for sensitive/compliance-relevant indexes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Determine the resulting data-loss timeline.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Frozen/Archive Path Configuration Changed
description: An index's coldToFrozenDir/coldToFrozenScript path was changed or removed, which controls where data goes when it ages out of searchable retention — removing this path effectively deletes aged-out data rather than archiving it, and redirecting it can send archived data to an unauthorized location.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Frozen/archive path configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters index configuration-change events touching coldToFrozenDir/coldToFrozenScript.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes info="*coldToFrozen*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against archival-infrastructure change tickets; alert if the path is removed entirely (defaults to deletion).
investigation_steps: Verify the new path is the expected, authorized archive location.
Confirm archival is still functioning if a path was removed.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Clean Eventdata or Destructive Index Maintenance Command Run
description: The splunk clean eventdata CLI command (or an equivalent destructive index-maintenance operation) was run against an index, which irreversibly deletes all indexed data for that index — the single most direct data-destruction action available through Splunk's own tooling, requiring OS-level command auditing to observe since it operates below what _audit itself records for a REST/Web action.

data_sources.name: Sysmon / auditd
data_sources.path: process creation events for the splunk binary with clean-eventdata arguments
data_sources.description: OS-level process execution telemetry for the splunk CLI.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events invoking the splunk binary with a clean/eventdata-related argument.
spl:
index=<endpoint_index> sourcetype IN (Sysmon, auditd) process_name="*splunk*"
| where match(command_line, "(?i)clean\s+eventdata")
| table _time, host, user, command_line
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level process telemetry on Splunk servers — not observable from Splunk's own internal logs, since the command typically runs while splunkd is stopped; a documented Splunk Cloud limitation given the customer has no server access.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed data-destruction incident.
Immediately determine which index was targeted and whether backups exist.
response_guidance: Engage incident response immediately; restore from backup if available.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bucket-Level Filesystem Deletion
description: Index bucket directories were deleted directly at the filesystem level (bypassing Splunk's own index-management commands entirely), the most direct and hardest-to-attribute form of data destruction against an on-premises Splunk deployment.

data_sources.name: FIM / auditd
data_sources.description: OS-level filesystem deletion events targeting index bucket directories.

detection_logic: Filters filesystem deletion events (via auditd or FIM) targeting paths under the configured index storage location.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=auditd action=deleted file_path="*/splunk/var/lib/splunk/*"
| table _time, host, user, file_path
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level FIM/auditd coverage on the index storage path — a Splunk Cloud limitation, since customers have no filesystem access to provider-managed indexer storage.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed data-destruction incident.
Determine what buckets/time-ranges were affected.
response_guidance: Engage incident response immediately; restore from backup or from a searchable indexer-cluster replica if the replication factor allowed the loss to be absorbed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Delete Search Command Used
description: A user with the delete_by_keyword capability ran a search using the | delete command, which marks matching events as deleted (removed from search results, though the underlying raw data may remain on disk until the index is cleaned) — a capability so powerful that most Splunk deployments should have zero or near-zero legitimate uses of it outside of a documented data-remediation process.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Search-execution events invoking the delete command.

detection_logic: Filters search-execution events where the search text invokes the delete command.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted search="*| delete*" OR search="*|delete*"
| table _time, user, search
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; confirm against a documented, approved data-remediation (e.g. accidental PII ingestion) process.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent an approved remediation ticket.
Determine exactly what events matched and were marked deleted.
response_guidance: Investigate immediately; the delete_by_keyword capability should be restricted to the smallest possible set of accounts.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Delete Command Used Against Sensitive Index
description: The delete command (SPL-DATA-008) was used against a search scoped to a sensitive index (security, authentication, audit) — this narrower, higher-confidence variant assumes the combination of destructive capability and a high-value target is the clearest possible evidence-destruction signal available in this catalogue.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Delete-command search events filtered to sensitive-index scope.

detection_logic: Filters delete-command search events where the search string also references a sensitive index.
spl:
index=_audit action=search info=granted (search="*| delete*" OR search="*|delete*")
| where match(search, "(?i)index=(security|authentication|audit|identity)")
| table _time, user, search
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences without exception.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed anti-forensics incident.
Preserve any remaining evidence and begin full incident response.
response_guidance: Full incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: outputs.conf New Receiver or Existing Receiver Changed
description: A forwarder's or heavy forwarder's outputs.conf was changed to add a new receiving indexer/endpoint or modify an existing one, which — since outputs.conf controls where every event a forwarder collects actually ends up — is the primary mechanism for the data-diversion attack path: silently redirecting a security data source's output to an unmonitored or attacker-controlled destination.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_tcp OR local outputs.conf change
data_sources.description: Output-routing configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters output-routing configuration-change events where the destination server list changes.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp info="*server*"
| table _time, user, host, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; alert on all changes for forwarders known to carry security-relevant data.
investigation_steps: Verify the new destination is the expected, authorized indexer/receiver.
Check for a subsequent volume drop at the original destination (SPL-DATA-012).
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: SSL Certificate Validation Disabled on Forwarding Output
description: A forwarder's outputs.conf was changed to disable SSL certificate validation (sslVerifyServerCert) on its receiving connection, which — combined with a subsequent receiver-address change (SPL-DATA-010) — removes the safeguard that would otherwise prevent a silently redirected forwarder from trusting an attacker-controlled receiver presenting an invalid certificate.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: SSL validation configuration-change events on output stanzas.

detection_logic: Filters output-routing configuration-change events where sslVerifyServerCert transitions to false/disabled.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp info="*sslVerifyServerCert=false*"
| table _time, user, host, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against TLS-migration change tickets; alert on all occurrences given how commonly this precedes SPL-DATA-010-style diversion.
investigation_steps: Verify the reason for disabling validation.
Check for a subsequent receiver-address change.
response_guidance: Re-enable validation immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Data Diversion: Security Source Volume Drops While New Destination Appears
description: An outputs.conf/routing configuration change (SPL-DATA-010) was followed by an expected security data source's ingestion volume at its original destination dropping sharply, confirming the diversion was actually effective rather than merely configured and unused — the flagship data-diversion correlation.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Output-routing change events followed by an ingestion-volume drop for the affected source's original destination index
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: routing change, then volume drop.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring an output-routing change event for a host followed by a sharp ingestion-volume decline for that host's known sourcetype(s) within a short window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp info="*server*"
| eval stage="1_routing_change"
| append [| tstats count where index=* by host, _time span=1h | eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count stdev(count) AS stdev_count by host | where count < (avg_count - 3*stdev_count) | eval stage="2_volume_drop"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by host
| where stage_count>=2 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=3600
tuning_guidance: Correlate with planned decommission/migration tickets; a Tier-1 flagship exfiltration/defense-evasion chain otherwise.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed data-diversion incident.
Determine the new destination and whether it is monitored/authorized.
response_guidance: Revert the routing change immediately and audit what data flowed to the new destination during the exposure window.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: The volume-drop half of this correlation runs a broad tstats across every index; schedule this at a lower frequency (hourly) and/or scope it to a maintained list of hosts known to carry security-relevant data rather than the entire fleet.

title: props.conf/transforms.conf Change Introduces nullQueue Routing
description: A transforms.conf stanza was added or modified to route matching events to nullQueue (silently dropping them before indexing), which — if applied to a security-relevant sourcetype with a filter matching a specific pattern of interest to an attacker — is one of the most surgical and hard-to-notice defense-evasion techniques available in Splunk's own configuration, since the events never reach any index for later review.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: local transforms.conf change introducing DEST_KEY = queue and FORMAT = nullQueue
data_sources.description: Transform configuration changes routing events to nullQueue.

detection_logic: Requires either app-content diffing on transforms.conf changes or, on Splunk Cloud, review through the customer-visible configuration-change workflow where such changes go through Splunk support/professional services.
spl:
| rest /services/configs/conf-transforms splunk_server=local
| search DEST_KEY="queue" FORMAT="nullQueue"
| table title, eai:acl.app, DEST_KEY, FORMAT, REGEX
tuning_guidance: A scheduled REST-based audit search rather than a real-time event-driven detection; run daily and diff against the prior day's result set to surface new nullQueue routing rules.
investigation_steps: Review the REGEX filter to determine exactly what pattern of events is being dropped.
Determine which sourcetype/index this transform applies to.
response_guidance: Remove the nullQueue routing if unauthorized and assess what data was lost during the exposure window (irrecoverable, since the events were never indexed).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Event Volume Loss Correlated with Recent Parsing Configuration Change
description: A props.conf/transforms.conf configuration change was followed by a sharp, sustained drop in event volume for the affected sourcetype, confirming the parsing change actually resulted in event loss rather than a benign field-extraction/masking adjustment.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Parsing configuration-change events (via the app/config audit trail) followed by a sourcetype's ingestion-volume decline
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: config change, then volume loss.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a props/transforms configuration-change event for a sourcetype followed by a sharp decline in that sourcetype's ingestion volume within a short window.
spl:
| tstats count where index=* by sourcetype, _time span=1h
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count stdev(count) AS stdev_count by sourcetype
| where count < (avg_count - 3*stdev_count)
| eval stage="volume_drop"
tuning_guidance: Correlate against a change-tracking system for props/transforms edits (Splunk's own audit trail for local file changes is limited — see the SPL-CONF section for what is and is not observable).
investigation_steps: Confirm whether a recent parsing configuration change explains the drop.
If so, treat with the same urgency as SPL-DATA-013.
response_guidance: Revert the parsing change and confirm volume recovers.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Full tstats across every index/sourcetype is expensive; schedule hourly and scope to a maintained list of security-relevant sourcetypes rather than the entire fleet where possible.

title: Data Masking Rule Added or Changed on Security-Relevant Sourcetype
description: A SEDCMD or masking-related transform was added or changed for a security-relevant sourcetype, which — while a legitimate PII-redaction technique in many cases — can also be used to strip out a specific field value (a username, an IP, a command line) that an attacker wants hidden from every future search against that data, without dropping the event entirely (avoiding the more obvious volume-loss signal of SPL-DATA-013/014).

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: local props.conf SEDCMD stanza change, cross-referenced against security-relevant sourcetypes
data_sources.description: Masking-rule configuration changes.

detection_logic: A scheduled REST-based audit search reviewing SEDCMD stanzas for security-relevant sourcetypes against a maintained baseline.
spl:
| rest /services/configs/conf-props splunk_server=local
| search SEDCMD=* eai:acl.app=*
| lookup security_relevant_sourcetypes.csv sourcetype AS title OUTPUT is_security_relevant
| where is_security_relevant=1
| table title, SEDCMD*
tuning_guidance: Run daily and diff against the prior day's result set to surface new/changed masking rules; confirm against data-privacy change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the regex pattern for what specifically is being masked.
Determine whether this is a legitimate PII-redaction policy or a targeted evasion technique.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized or if the masking scope is broader than the documented PII-redaction policy.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: PII Masking Removed Exposing Secrets in Plain Text
description: An existing masking rule protecting a field known to carry secrets or PII was removed, which — going forward — exposes that data in plain text to every user with search access to the affected index, a significantly larger exposure surface than any single search or export.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: SEDCMD stanza removed for a sourcetype previously on the masking baseline
data_sources.description: Masking-rule removal events compared against the prior-day baseline.

detection_logic: Compares the daily SEDCMD-stanza audit search (SPL-DATA-015) against the prior day's baseline and flags removals.
spl:
| rest /services/configs/conf-props splunk_server=local
| search eai:acl.app=*
| lookup update=true masking_rule_baseline.csv title OUTPUT had_sedcmd
| where had_sedcmd=1 AND isnull(SEDCMD)
| table title
tuning_guidance: Confirm against data-privacy change tickets; alert on all occurrences given the exposure severity.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess who has search access to the now-unmasked field.
response_guidance: Restore the masking rule immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Ingest Processor Pipeline Destination Changed
description: An Ingest Processor pipeline's output destination was changed, which — since Ingest Processor sits in the data path before events reach an index — is the Splunk Cloud-native equivalent of the on-premises outputs.conf data-diversion technique (SPL-DATA-010).

data_sources.name: Ingest Processor Audit Log
data_sources.description: Pipeline output-destination configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters pipeline output-destination configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*ingest_processor* action=pipeline_updated
| where match(info, "destination")
| table _time, user, pipeline_name, old_destination, new_destination
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — validate the exact audit sourcetype/event schema against your Ingest Processor deployment rather than assuming this SPL's literal field names.
investigation_steps: Verify the new destination is authorized.
Determine what data flows through this pipeline.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Ingest Processor Filter Introduces Event Dropping
description: An Ingest Processor pipeline filter was added or modified to drop matching events before they reach any index, the Ingest Processor equivalent of the on-premises nullQueue technique (SPL-DATA-013) but positioned even earlier in the data path.

data_sources.name: Ingest Processor Audit Log
data_sources.path: Ingest Processor pipeline filter/rule configuration-change events
data_sources.description: Pipeline filter-addition events matching a drop/discard action.

detection_logic: Filters pipeline configuration-change events where a new rule's action is drop/discard.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*ingest_processor* action=rule_updated filter_action=drop
| table _time, user, pipeline_name, filter_action, filter_criteria
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — validate against your Ingest Processor deployment's actual audit schema.
investigation_steps: Review the filter criteria to determine what is being dropped.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Remove the filter if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Ingest Processor Field Masking Exposes Sensitive Field
description: An Ingest Processor pipeline's field-masking configuration was changed in a way that stops masking a previously-protected sensitive field, the Ingest Processor equivalent of SPL-DATA-016.

data_sources.name: Ingest Processor Audit Log
data_sources.path: Ingest Processor pipeline masking-rule configuration-change events
data_sources.description: Masking-rule removal/weakening events.

detection_logic: Compares the current masking-rule set for each pipeline against a maintained baseline.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*ingest_processor* action=masking_rule_updated
| lookup update=true ingest_masking_baseline.csv pipeline_name, field_name OUTPUT was_masked
| where was_masked=1 AND currently_masked=0
| table _time, user, pipeline_name, field_name
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — validate against your Ingest Processor deployment's actual audit schema.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess exposure of the now-unmasked field.
response_guidance: Restore masking if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Ingest Processor S3 Destination Changed
description: An Ingest Processor pipeline configured to write a copy of ingested data to Amazon S3 had its bucket destination changed, which can redirect a durable, potentially bulk copy of ingested security data to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket.

data_sources.name: Ingest Processor Audit Log
data_sources.path: Ingest Processor S3 output destination configuration-change events
data_sources.description: S3-destination bucket/ARN configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters pipeline S3-destination configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*ingest_processor* action=pipeline_updated destination_type=s3
| table _time, user, pipeline_name, old_bucket, new_bucket
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — validate against your Ingest Processor deployment's actual audit schema.
investigation_steps: Verify the new S3 bucket is owned by and authorized for your organization.
Determine what data is written to this destination.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Edge Processor Pipeline or Output Changed
description: An Edge Processor pipeline's parsing/transformation/filtering rules or output destination were changed. Edge Processor runs closer to the data source than Ingest Processor, so a compromise here can affect data before it ever reaches Splunk's own cloud/on-premises boundary — the same data-diversion and event-dropping risks as SPL-DATA-017/018 apply, one hop earlier in the pipeline.

data_sources.name: Edge Processor Audit Log
data_sources.description: Pipeline rule/output configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters Edge Processor pipeline configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*edge_processor* action=pipeline_updated
| table _time, user, pipeline_name, info
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — Edge Processor's exact audit event schema should be validated against your specific deployment before relying on this SPL literally.
investigation_steps: Verify the change against an approved edge-configuration change ticket.
Assess the resulting data-path impact given Edge Processor's position ahead of the ingestion boundary.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Edge Processor Endpoint Configuration Changed
description: An Edge Processor instance's own management/connection configuration was changed (which pipelines it runs, which control plane it registers with), which can be used to detach an Edge Processor from legitimate management or re-point it at an attacker-controlled control plane.

data_sources.name: Edge Processor Audit Log
data_sources.path: Edge Processor instance registration/control-plane configuration-change events
data_sources.description: Instance-level configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters Edge Processor instance-configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*edge_processor* action=instance_updated
| table _time, user, instance_id, info
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — validate against your Edge Processor deployment's actual audit schema.
investigation_steps: Verify the change against an approved change ticket.
Confirm the instance still registers with the expected, legitimate control plane.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bulk Index Configuration Change Across Many Indexes
description: A single actor modified an unusually large number of distinct indexes' retention, size, or routing settings in a short window, consistent with a scripted, fleet-wide attack against the platform's data-retention posture rather than routine, incremental index administration.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Index configuration-change events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct indexes modified per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(object) AS index_count values(object) AS indexes by _time, user
| where index_count>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known IaC-driven index-management pipelines.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented bulk-migration project.
Treat as a live incident absent one.
response_guidance: Suspend the actor and audit every index changed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Duplicate Event Flood Suggesting Replay Attack
description: An unusually large number of exact-duplicate events (identical raw content and timestamp) were ingested in a short window, consistent with either a legitimate forwarder retry/replay after a network interruption or a deliberate attempt to flood an index with noise to obscure genuine events or exhaust storage.

data_sources.name: metrics.log / raw event comparison
data_sources.description: Ingested events compared for exact-duplicate content within a short window.

detection_logic: Hashes raw event content within a rolling window and flags hash values appearing an unusually large number of times.
spl:
index=<destination_index>
| eval event_hash=md5(_raw)
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, event_hash, host
| where count>=100
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known forwarder connectivity interruptions (which cause legitimate retry-driven duplication) before attributing to malicious replay.
investigation_steps: Determine the source of the duplication.
Assess storage/licensing impact.
response_guidance: Investigate the source host/forwarder for malfunction or compromise if not explained by a known connectivity issue.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unexpected Ingest Volume Spike Causing License Impact
description: Daily ingest volume rose sharply above its historical baseline, which — on Splunk Enterprise's license-metered model — can trigger license-violation warnings and, if sustained, search-blocking enforcement, in addition to being a legitimate operational signal of an unexpected new/misconfigured source.

data_sources.name: license_usage.log
data_sources.description: Daily license-pool usage compared to historical baseline.

detection_logic: Compares daily total indexed volume against a historical baseline.
spl:
index=_internal source=*license_usage.log* type=Usage
| bucket _time span=1d
| stats sum(b) AS total_bytes by _time
| eventstats avg(total_bytes) AS avg_bytes stdev(total_bytes) AS stdev_bytes
| where total_bytes > (avg_bytes + 3*stdev_bytes)
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known planned onboarding of new data sources before treating as anomalous; ordinary organic growth should not be treated as malicious without additional context per the specification's own guidance.
investigation_steps: Identify which index/source contributed the spike.
Confirm whether it is a known, planned change.
response_guidance: No security response needed if explained by legitimate growth; investigate further if not.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Stops Reporting
description: A forwarder that has historically reported metrics/phoned-home on a regular interval stopped doing so, which — while frequently a benign host outage or network issue — removes visibility into every log source that forwarder was collecting and warrants the same investigative rigor as any other logging-gap detection.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log (indexer-side)
data_sources.description: Forwarder connection/phone-home metrics compared to expected reporting interval.

detection_logic: Flags forwarders with no phone-home/metrics event within 3x their expected reporting interval.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=Metrics group=tcpin_connections by hostname
| eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60)
| where minutes_since>=45
| table hostname, last_seen, minutes_since
tuning_guidance: Exclude forwarders on known-decommissioned or maintenance-mode hosts; tune the multiplier to your fleet's actual phone-home interval.
investigation_steps: Determine if the host is down, network-isolated, or the Splunk service specifically was stopped (SPL-FWD-006).
Check for a concurrent deployment-server or output configuration change.
response_guidance: Investigate the host directly; treat as a potential defense-evasion incident if the service was deliberately stopped rather than the host being down.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Forwarder Registers with Fleet
description: A new forwarder connected to an indexer or registered with the Deployment Server for the first time. Routine during legitimate fleet growth, but the necessary building block for detecting an unauthorized/rogue forwarder joining the environment.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: New forwarder connection events.

detection_logic: Joins new forwarder connections against a lookup of previously-known forwarder GUIDs.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc "connected"
| lookup update=true known_forwarder_guids.csv guid OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, hostname, guid
tuning_guidance: Confirm against provisioning/onboarding records.
investigation_steps: Verify the new forwarder against an approved asset inventory.
response_guidance: Remove/block if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder GUID Duplication Across Multiple Hosts
description: The same forwarder GUID was observed connecting from multiple distinct hostnames/IPs, which — while frequently the result of cloning a golden image without regenerating the GUID (a common operational mistake) — can also indicate an attacker cloning a legitimate forwarder's identity to blend malicious traffic in with a trusted source.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Forwarder connection events grouped by GUID, checking for multiple distinct hostnames.

detection_logic: Groups forwarder connection events by GUID within a rolling window and flags GUIDs associated with more than one distinct hostname.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc "connected"
| stats dc(hostname) AS host_count values(hostname) AS hosts by guid
| where host_count>1
tuning_guidance: Common in environments using unmanaged golden images; treat as an operational-hygiene issue in most cases, escalate if the duplication is new/unexpected.
investigation_steps: Determine if this is a known imaging issue or an unexpected duplication.
Regenerate the GUID on the offending host(s) if imaging-related.
response_guidance: Investigate for spoofing if not explained by known imaging practices.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Hostname Changed
description: A forwarder's reported hostname changed for the same GUID, which can indicate a legitimate host rename or an attempt to make a compromised/rogue forwarder present as a different, more trusted-sounding host identity.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Forwarder connection events compared against a per-GUID hostname baseline.

detection_logic: Joins forwarder connection events against a lookup of each GUID's previously-reported hostname.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc "connected"
| lookup update=true forwarder_hostname_baseline.csv guid OUTPUT prior_hostname
| where isnotnull(prior_hostname) AND hostname!=prior_hostname
| table _time, guid, prior_hostname, hostname
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change/rename tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the rename.
Verify the host's identity through an independent asset-management source.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Output Destination Changed
description: A universal forwarder's outputs.conf destination was changed at the endpoint level (as opposed to via a centrally-managed deployment app), which — like the heavy-forwarder/data-routing detections elsewhere in this catalogue — can silently redirect the endpoint's collected data to an unauthorized destination.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.path: file-integrity-monitoring events for the forwarder's local outputs.conf
data_sources.description: Local outputs.conf file-modification events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the forwarder's local configuration directory; flags modifications not attributable to a deployment-app push.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/system/local/outputs.conf" OR file_path="*\\etc\\system\\local\\outputs.conf"
| lookup deployment_push_events.csv host, _time OUTPUT is_deployment_push
| where isnull(is_deployment_push)
| table _time, host, file_path
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage on every forwarder endpoint, correlated against known deployment-push timing to exclude legitimate centrally-managed changes.
investigation_steps: Verify the new destination.
Treat as a live incident if not attributable to an authorized deployment push.
response_guidance: Revert and investigate the endpoint for compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Forwarder Service Stopped on Endpoint
description: The Splunk forwarder service was stopped on an endpoint by an OS-level action (as opposed to a documented maintenance procedure), a common technique for temporarily blinding endpoint telemetry ahead of malicious activity on that specific host.

data_sources.name: Windows Event Log / systemd journal
data_sources.path: service-stop events for the SplunkForwarder service
data_sources.description: OS-level service-control events for the forwarder service.

detection_logic: Filters OS service-management events where the SplunkForwarder service transitions to stopped, outside a documented maintenance window.
spl:
index=<endpoint_index> sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog:System", "linux_secure") service_name="SplunkForwarder" action=stopped
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host, user, service_name
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level service-management telemetry (Windows Security/System log or Linux systemd journal), not visible from Splunk's own logs once the service is stopped.
investigation_steps: Confirm the stop against a documented maintenance ticket.
If unexplained, investigate the host for concurrent malicious activity during the blind window.
response_guidance: Restart the service and investigate the host as a potential defense-evasion incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Deployment Server Reassigned
description: A forwarder's deploymentclient.conf targetUri was changed to point at a different Deployment Server, which — if pointed at an attacker-controlled server — hands that attacker the ability to push arbitrary apps (including scripted inputs) to the forwarder going forward.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.path: file-integrity-monitoring events for the forwarder's local deploymentclient.conf
data_sources.description: Deployment-server target configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the forwarder's local deploymentclient.conf.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*deploymentclient.conf"
| table _time, host, file_path, action
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage on every forwarder endpoint; treat any change outside a documented DS-migration project as suspicious.
investigation_steps: Verify the new targetUri is the authorized, legitimate Deployment Server.
Investigate what apps this forwarder receives from the new server.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1071: Application Layer Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Version Downgraded
description: A forwarder's reported version number decreased compared to its prior connection, which can indicate a deliberate downgrade to reintroduce a fixed vulnerability, or the deployment of an older/unofficial forwarder binary.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Forwarder connection events with version string, compared to a per-host version baseline.

detection_logic: Joins forwarder connection events against a lookup of each host's previously-reported version and flags downgrades.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc "connected"
| lookup update=true forwarder_version_baseline.csv hostname OUTPUT prior_version
| where isnotnull(prior_version) AND version<prior_version
| table _time, hostname, prior_version, version
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate rollback scenarios.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check whether the downgrade reintroduces a known vulnerability.
response_guidance: Upgrade back to the approved version if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Monitored Inputs Modified
description: A forwarder's inputs.conf monitored-path list was changed, which — if a path is removed — silently stops collection from that source, or — if a blacklist regex is added — can exclude a specific pattern of log lines from ever being forwarded.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.path: file-integrity-monitoring events for the forwarder's local inputs.conf
data_sources.description: Monitored-input configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the forwarder's local inputs.conf; flags changes not attributable to a deployment-app push.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/system/local/inputs.conf" OR file_path="*\\etc\\system\\local\\inputs.conf"
| lookup deployment_push_events.csv host, _time OUTPUT is_deployment_push
| where isnull(is_deployment_push)
| table _time, host, file_path
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage; correlate with deployment-push timing to exclude authorized centrally-managed changes.
investigation_steps: Diff the input configuration before and after.
Determine what monitoring coverage was affected.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Heavy Forwarder App Installed
description: An app was installed on a heavy forwarder — since heavy forwarders both execute the full search-processing pipeline (unlike a universal forwarder) and sit in the data-routing path, a malicious app here combines the code-execution risk of SPL-APP with the data-diversion risk of SPL-DATA in a single higher-value target.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_app info=created, restricted to hosts flagged as heavy forwarders
data_sources.description: App-installation events on heavy-forwarder-tier hosts.

detection_logic: Filters app-installation events where the target host is on a maintained heavy-forwarder inventory.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info=created
| lookup heavy_forwarder_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_hf
| where is_hf=1
| table _time, user, object, host
tuning_guidance: Maintain the heavy-forwarder inventory lookup; treat all HF app installs with elevated scrutiny relative to a search head.
investigation_steps: Review the app's contents for scripted inputs, custom commands, and routing changes.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Heavy Forwarder indexAndForward Setting Changed
description: A heavy forwarder's indexAndForward setting was changed, which controls whether the HF also retains a local copy of the data it processes and forwards — enabling this unexpectedly creates an unmonitored local data store; disabling it on an HF that was relied on for local search removes that capability.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: indexAndForward configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters server-configuration-change events touching indexAndForward on heavy-forwarder-tier hosts.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_server info="*indexAndForward*"
| lookup heavy_forwarder_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_hf
| where is_hf=1
| table _time, user, host, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
If enabled, determine what local index the data now populates and who can search it.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Heavy Forwarder Local Interactive Login
description: A user authenticated to Splunk Web on a heavy forwarder directly, which — since heavy forwarders are typically operated as headless data-processing infrastructure rather than an interactive analyst tool — is unusual and warrants the same review as an unexpected admin login on any other management-tier system.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=login attempt=success, restricted to heavy-forwarder-tier hosts
data_sources.description: Login events on heavy-forwarder-tier hosts.

detection_logic: Filters successful login events where the target host is on the heavy-forwarder inventory.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup heavy_forwarder_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_hf
| where is_hf=1
| table _time, user, host
tuning_guidance: Exclude known operations-team accounts with a legitimate, documented reason for direct HF administration.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review actions taken during the session.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Heavy Forwarder HEC Token Created
description: A HEC token was created directly on a heavy forwarder rather than at the indexing tier, which — depending on the HF's role in the architecture — may be an unusual/unexpected ingestion point that bypasses whatever additional processing or governance normally applies at the standard ingestion boundary.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token info=created, restricted to heavy-forwarder-tier hosts
data_sources.description: HEC token-creation events on heavy-forwarder-tier hosts.

detection_logic: Filters HEC token-creation events where the target host is on the heavy-forwarder inventory.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_tcp-token info=created
| lookup heavy_forwarder_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_hf
| where is_hf=1
| table _time, user, object, host
tuning_guidance: Confirm against your architecture's documented HEC ingestion-point design.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for HEC ingestion at this tier.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: TLS Certificate Changed on Forwarder-to-Indexer Connection
description: The TLS certificate presented by a forwarder or its receiving indexer changed unexpectedly, without a corresponding entry in the certificate-rotation change log — a possible sign of an adversary-in-the-middle interception between the forwarder and its indexer.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: TLS handshake events with certificate fingerprint, compared against a known-good baseline.

detection_logic: Compares observed certificate fingerprints for forwarder-indexer connections against a maintained known-good baseline.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component IN (TcpInputProc, TcpOutputProc) "certificate"
| lookup update=true known_cert_fingerprints.csv host OUTPUT expected_fingerprint
| where isnotnull(expected_fingerprint) AND cert_fingerprint!=expected_fingerprint
| table _time, host, cert_fingerprint, expected_fingerprint
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained certificate-fingerprint baseline and a documented rotation-change log to cross-reference against.
investigation_steps: Confirm the change against a documented certificate-rotation ticket.
If unexplained, treat as a possible interception incident.
response_guidance: Investigate the network path between the forwarder and indexer if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sudden Forwarder Disconnect Across Many Hosts Coinciding with Cloud Receiver Change
description: A large number of customer-managed forwarders disconnected from a Splunk Cloud receiver in a short window, coinciding with a change to the Cloud-side receiver configuration (certificate, port, or IP allow-list) — the flagship hybrid-architecture availability/logging-gap chain, since the customer manages the forwarders but the receiving endpoint sits in Splunk Cloud.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Mass forwarder-disconnect events correlated with a Splunk Cloud receiver-configuration change (IP allow-list, certificate) within a short window
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Counts distinct forwarders disconnecting within a rolling window and correlates against any recent Cloud-side receiver/allow-list configuration change.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpOutputProc "Connection to * timed out" OR "closed"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(hostname) AS disconnect_count values(hostname) AS hosts by _time
| where disconnect_count>=20
tuning_guidance: Correlate against Splunk Cloud maintenance notifications and any recent IP allow-list/certificate change before escalating; a strong hybrid-architecture Tier-1 candidate otherwise.
investigation_steps: Check for a concurrent Splunk Cloud IP allow-list or certificate change.
Determine whether the disconnect is provider-side maintenance or a customer-side configuration issue.
response_guidance: Coordinate with Splunk Cloud support if provider-side; revert the customer-side configuration if that is the cause.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Deployment Client Registered
description: A new client registered with the Deployment Server. Routine during legitimate fleet growth, but a necessary building block for detecting an unauthorized client joining the fleet-management trust relationship.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: New deployment-client registration events.

detection_logic: Joins client registration events against a lookup of previously-known client identities.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=DeployedServerclass "New serverclass"
| lookup update=true known_deployment_clients.csv clientName OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, clientName, hostname
tuning_guidance: Confirm against provisioning records.
investigation_steps: Verify the new client against an approved asset inventory.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Client Count for Server Class Grows Unusually Fast
description: The number of distinct clients matching a server class grew far faster than the fleet's normal onboarding rate, which can indicate either a legitimate mass-provisioning event or a server class's matching criteria being broadened (SPL-DS-003) causing unintended clients to suddenly qualify.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Server class membership counts compared to a historical growth-rate baseline.

detection_logic: Compares each server class's client-count growth over a rolling window against its historical rate.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=DeployedServerclass
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats dc(clientName) AS client_count by _time, serverclass_name
| streamstats window=24 avg(client_count) AS avg_count by serverclass_name
| where client_count > (avg_count*2)
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known mass-provisioning projects.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for a recent server-class matching-criteria change (SPL-DS-003).
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1018: Remote System Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Server Class Matching Criteria Broadened
description: A server class's client-matching pattern (whitelist/blacklist regex in serverclass.conf) was broadened, which — since apps assigned to a server class are pushed to every matching client — expands the population of forwarders that will receive whatever apps that server class delivers, a critical precursor to the fleet-wide-compromise attack path.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Server class matching-criteria configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters server class configuration-change events touching the whitelist/blacklist matching pattern.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_serverclass (info="*whitelist*" OR info="*blacklist*")
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; alert on all occurrences given the fleet-wide blast-radius implication.
investigation_steps: Determine what apps this server class delivers.
Enumerate the new set of matching clients that will now receive them.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deployment App Content Modified
description: An app in the Deployment Server's deployment-apps repository was modified — since this repository is the source of truth pushed out to every matching forwarder, any malicious change here (a new scripted input, a modified binary) is automatically distributed fleet-wide on the next check-in cycle without any additional attacker action required.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.description: Deployment-app repository file-modification events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the Deployment Server's deployment-apps directory.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/deployment-apps/*"
| table _time, file_path, user, action
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage on the Deployment Server — a Splunk Cloud limitation since the Deployment Server, when used, typically remains customer-managed infrastructure outside Splunk Cloud's provider-managed boundary.
investigation_steps: Diff the app content against the last known-good version.
Determine which server classes deliver this app and enumerate all affected clients.
response_guidance: Restore the known-good version immediately and treat as a live fleet-wide incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deployment App Deleted from Repository
description: An app was deleted from the Deployment Server's deployment-apps repository, which will remove it from every client that receives it on their next check-in — if the app provided security monitoring/data collection, this can create a fleet-wide logging gap.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.description: Deployment-app repository deletion events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the Deployment Server's deployment-apps directory, filtered to deletion actions.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/deployment-apps/*" action=deleted
| table _time, file_path, user
tuning_guidance: Confirm against decommission tickets; Splunk Cloud limitation as with SPL-DS-004.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess the resulting fleet-wide coverage gap.
response_guidance: Restore if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: App Deployed to Unusually Many Clients
description: A single app deployment reached an unusually large number of distinct forwarder clients within a short window — the Deployment Server-side companion to SPL-APP-022, confirming the deployment infrastructure's own logs show the same fleet-wide push pattern.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: App deployment events aggregated per app per window across target clients.

detection_logic: Counts distinct clients receiving the same app within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=DeployedApplication
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats dc(clientName) AS target_count by _time, app_name
| where target_count>=20
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known org-wide rollouts with a documented change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a deployment change ticket.
Review the app's contents.
response_guidance: Halt further rollout if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Outputs Configuration Redirected Fleet-Wide via Deployment App
description: A deployment app containing an outputs.conf stanza with a changed receiver address was pushed to a large number of clients, which — combining SPL-DS-004's app-content tampering with SPL-DATA-010's data-diversion pattern — is the flagship Deployment-Server-to-fleet-wide-data-diversion attack chain named explicitly in the specification.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Deployment-app content change introducing/modifying outputs.conf, followed by fleet-wide deployment of that app
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a deployment-app content change touching outputs.conf followed by that app's deployment to an unusually large number of clients within a short window.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/deployment-apps/*/local/outputs.conf"
| eval stage="1_app_modified"
| append [search index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=DeployedApplication | bucket _time span=1h | stats dc(clientName) AS target_count by _time, app_name | where target_count>=20 | eval stage="2_mass_deploy"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by app_name
| where stage_count>=2 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=3600
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM on the Deployment Server plus correlation-search support; a flagship Tier-1 fleet-wide-compromise chain — Splunk Cloud limitation noted per SPL-DS-004.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed fleet-wide data-diversion incident.
Enumerate every client that received the app and verify their current outputs.conf state.
response_guidance: Full incident response: pull the app immediately, revert every affected client's outputs.conf, and audit what data was diverted during the exposure window.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools
MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Monitoring Disabled Fleet-Wide via Deployment App
description: A deployment app containing an inputs.conf change that disables a previously-monitored data source was pushed fleet-wide, the defense-evasion counterpart to SPL-DS-007 — instead of diverting data, this variant simply stops its collection across every affected client at once.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Deployment-app content change disabling an input, followed by fleet-wide deployment of that app
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a deployment-app content change disabling an inputs.conf stanza followed by that app's fleet-wide deployment within a short window.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/deployment-apps/*/local/inputs.conf" content="*disabled=1*"
| eval stage="1_app_modified"
| append [search index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=DeployedApplication | bucket _time span=1h | stats dc(clientName) AS target_count by _time, app_name | where target_count>=20 | eval stage="2_mass_deploy"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by app_name
| where stage_count>=2 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=3600
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM on the Deployment Server plus correlation-search support; Splunk Cloud limitation as with SPL-DS-007.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed fleet-wide defense-evasion incident.
Enumerate every client that received the app and re-enable the affected input.
response_guidance: Full incident response: pull the app, re-enable monitoring fleet-wide, and audit the exposure window for malicious activity that may have gone uncollected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deployment Server Admin Login
description: An admin-capable account authenticated to the Deployment Server. Given the Deployment Server's role as a fleet-management security boundary, every admin login is a building block for the higher-confidence correlations elsewhere in this section.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=login attempt=success, restricted to Deployment Server host
data_sources.description: Admin login events on the Deployment Server.

detection_logic: Filters admin-account login events where the target host is the Deployment Server.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success host=<deployment_server_host>
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where is_admin=1
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: Requires knowing the Deployment Server's hostname; high routine volume by design.
investigation_steps: Track for use in downstream correlations.
response_guidance: No standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: First-Seen Source for Deployment Server Admin Login
description: An admin-capable account authenticated to the Deployment Server from a source IP never previously seen for that account — given the fleet-wide blast radius of a compromised Deployment Server, this is a materially higher-priority variant of the general first-seen-admin-source detection (SPL-AUTH-007).

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=login attempt=success, restricted to Deployment Server host, compared against a source-IP baseline
data_sources.description: Admin login events on the Deployment Server compared against a per-user source baseline.

detection_logic: Joins Deployment-Server admin logins against the same source-IP baseline used by SPL-AUTH-007.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success host=<deployment_server_host>
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where is_admin=1
| lookup update=true splunk_auth_src_baseline.csv user, src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: A Tier-1 candidate given the fleet-wide blast radius of Deployment Server compromise.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the admin whether this login is expected.
Review all actions taken during the session for server-class or app changes.
response_guidance: Verify immediately; reset credentials and terminate the session if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deployment Server Restart or Configuration Reload Outside Maintenance Window
description: The Deployment Server was restarted or its configuration was reloaded outside a documented maintenance window, which — while frequently benign — can also indicate an attacker forcing a configuration reload to accelerate propagation of a just-modified serverclass/app change.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.path: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=ServerConfig, restricted to Deployment Server host
data_sources.description: Restart/reload events on the Deployment Server.

detection_logic: Filters restart/reload events on the Deployment Server host outside a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd host=<deployment_server_host> "restarting" OR "Server config reload"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a maintenance ticket.
Check for a concurrent server-class or app change.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deployment Server Certificate or Trust Configuration Changed
description: The Deployment Server's TLS certificate or client-trust configuration was changed, which can be used to either present a compromised certificate to clients or relax validation requirements ahead of a rogue-Deployment-Server impersonation attack.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_server info=*sslVerify* OR info=*serverCert*, restricted to Deployment Server host
data_sources.description: TLS/trust configuration-change events on the Deployment Server.

detection_logic: Filters TLS/certificate configuration-change events on the Deployment Server host.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_server host=<deployment_server_host> (info="*sslVerify*" OR info="*serverCert*")
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against certificate-rotation change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the change is part of an authorized rotation.
Confirm clients still validate the Deployment Server's identity correctly.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Head High Search Volume Anomaly
description: A search head's total concurrent search load rose far above its historical baseline, which — beyond the per-user resource-abuse detections in the SPL-SEARCH section — is a platform-health signal worth its own dedicated coverage since it can indicate a coordinated multi-account resource-exhaustion attempt.

data_sources.name: introspection_generator
data_sources.description: Search head resource-utilization introspection metrics.

detection_logic: Compares search head CPU/search-concurrency metrics against a historical baseline.
spl:
index=_introspection component=Hostwide data.cpu_system_pct=*
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats avg(data.cpu_system_pct) AS avg_cpu by _time, host
| eventstats avg(avg_cpu) AS baseline_cpu stdev(avg_cpu) AS stdev_cpu by host
| where avg_cpu > (baseline_cpu + 3*stdev_cpu)
tuning_guidance: Correlate with SPL-SEARCH-010/011 for per-user attribution before treating as a platform-wide incident.
investigation_steps: Identify the top resource-consuming searches/users during the anomaly window.
response_guidance: Kill offending searches; escalate to SPL-SEARCH-011's SOC-impact correlation if scheduled searches are affected.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Head Admin App Modification
description: An app was installed or modified directly on a search head, warranting the same scrutiny as any other app-management event (see SPL-APP-###) but scoped specifically to the search-head tier where the resulting content (dashboards, saved searches, custom commands) is most directly exposed to interactive analyst use.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_app, restricted to search-head-tier hosts
data_sources.description: App-management events on search-head-tier hosts.

detection_logic: Filters app-management events where the target host is on the search-head inventory.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app
| lookup search_head_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_sh
| where is_sh=1
| table _time, user, object, host, info
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with SPL-APP-### for the underlying app-content-risk detections.
investigation_steps: Review the app's contents.
See SPL-APP-### for detailed follow-up guidance.
response_guidance: See SPL-APP-### response guidance.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: REST API Abuse Targeting Search Head Configuration Endpoints
description: An unusually large number of distinct REST configuration-endpoint (/services/properties, /services/data/*) calls were made to a search head in a short window by a single principal, consistent with an attacker enumerating the platform's own configuration through the REST API rather than Splunk Web.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: REST configuration-endpoint access events aggregated per principal per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct configuration-related REST endpoints accessed per principal within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/services/properties*" OR uri="/services/data/*"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(uri) AS endpoint_count values(uri) AS endpoints by _time, user
| where endpoint_count>=20
tuning_guidance: Exclude known monitoring/automation service accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for broad configuration enumeration.
Check for a subsequent privileged action.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: SHC Member Added or Removed
description: A member was added to or removed from the Search Head Cluster, which changes both search-capacity distribution and the set of nodes trusted to replicate the cluster's knowledge-object bundle.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: SHC membership-change events.

detection_logic: Filters SHC membership-change events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=SHCMasterMemberInfo (action=added OR action=removed)
| table _time, member_name, action
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new/removed member against an approved change.
response_guidance: Investigate if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SHC Captain Election Anomaly
description: An unusually large number of captain elections occurred within a short window, which can indicate cluster instability from a legitimate infrastructure issue or a deliberate attempt to disrupt the SHC's ability to coordinate replication and scheduled-search delegation.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Captain-election events aggregated per window.

detection_logic: Counts captain-election events within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=SHCMasterMemberInfo "elected captain"
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats count values(member_name) AS captains by _time
| where count>=3
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known network/infrastructure incidents affecting the SHC's member connectivity.
investigation_steps: Investigate the underlying cause of instability.
Check for scheduled-search execution gaps during the instability window.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call; escalate to security if no infrastructure cause is found.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SHC Deployer Pushes App Fleet-Wide
description: The SHC Deployer pushed an app to the cluster's member search heads, which — since every SHC member is an interactive search environment for the analysts using it — means a malicious app deployed via the deployer instantly reaches every analyst's session across the entire cluster.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: SHC deployer app-push events.

detection_logic: Filters SHC deployer app-push events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=ShcDeployer "push"
| table _time, app_name, member_count
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; treat all pushes with the same scrutiny as SPL-APP-001/SPL-APP-020.
investigation_steps: Review the app's contents.
Confirm against an approved deployment ticket.
response_guidance: Roll back if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: SHC Deployer Configuration Changed Outside Maintenance
description: The SHC Deployer's own configuration (target URI, push mode) was changed outside a documented maintenance window, warranting the same review given the deployer's role as trusted management infrastructure for the entire cluster's content.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_server info=*shcluster*, restricted to the deployer host
data_sources.description: Deployer configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters deployer-configuration-change events outside a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_server host=<shc_deployer_host> info="*shcluster*"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bundle Replication Failure or Anomaly Across SHC Members
description: Knowledge-object bundle replication failed across multiple SHC members, which — beyond the operational impact of inconsistent search results between members — can indicate deliberate interference intended to keep a malicious knowledge-object change from propagating for later cross-referencing, or simply mask its origin by making members' bundle versions diverge.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Bundle replication failure events.

detection_logic: Counts bundle-replication failure events per member within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=SHCBundleReplicationLifecycleManager status=failed
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count values(member_name) AS members by _time
| where count>=3
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known network/infrastructure issues before escalating.
investigation_steps: Investigate the underlying cause.
Verify knowledge-object consistency across members once resolved.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call.
author: Threat Detection Library
