title: KV Store Replication Issue on Search Head Cluster
description: KV Store replication status degraded across SHC members, which — since Enterprise Security stores critical state (notable-event status, asset/identity data) in KV Store collections — can threaten the consistency and availability of security-relevant data across the cluster.

data_sources.name: mongod.log
data_sources.description: KV Store replication-status log events.

detection_logic: Filters KV Store replication-status events indicating a degraded or failed state.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=mongod (status=SECONDARY_LAGGED OR status=DOWN OR "replication error")
| table _time, host, status
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known infrastructure issues before escalating.
investigation_steps: Investigate the underlying cause.
Verify ES data consistency once resolved.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Local Configuration File Changed on Search Head Outside Deployment
description: A local configuration file was changed directly on a search head's filesystem rather than through the standard app-deployment or knowledge-object management workflow, bypassing whatever change-review process normally applies.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.description: Local configuration-directory file-modification events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the search head's local configuration directories.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/system/local/*" OR file_path="*/etc/apps/*/local/*"
| lookup deployment_push_events.csv host, _time OUTPUT is_deployment_push
| where isnull(is_deployment_push)
| table _time, host, file_path, user
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage — a Splunk Cloud limitation given customers have no filesystem access to provider-managed search heads.
investigation_steps: Diff the file content.
Determine whether the change bypassed an expected change-management process.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Head Compromise Path: Admin Login to Detection Disabled to Matching Activity
description: The named search-head-compromise attack path: an admin login (SPL-AUTH-007), followed by a security detection being modified/disabled (SPL-KO-001/003), followed by the suspicious event that detection would have caught occurring without alerting (SPL-KO-006). This entry exists to expose the specification's explicitly-named chain under the SPL-SH namespace as a cross-reference to the underlying SPL-KO-006 logic.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: See SPL-KO-006 for the full underlying detection logic.
data_sources.description: Cross-referenced from SPL-KO-006 combined with SPL-AUTH-007.

detection_logic: See SPL-AUTH-007 and SPL-KO-006; this entry documents the named search-head attack path without duplicating SPL logic.
spl: | savedsearch "SPL-KO-006 Detection Tampering Followed by Matching Activity"
tuning_guidance: See SPL-KO-006.
investigation_steps: See SPL-KO-006 and SPL-AUTH-007 investigation steps.
response_guidance: See SPL-KO-006 response guidance.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Search Head REST API Used to Modify Configuration Outside Splunk Web Session
description: A configuration-changing REST call was made without a corresponding Splunk Web session cookie, indicating the change was made programmatically (via curl, a script, or an API client) rather than through the UI — not inherently malicious, since this is how automation is expected to work, but worth correlating against known automation accounts for anomaly detection.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.path: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/servicesNS/*" method IN (POST, DELETE)
data_sources.description: Configuration-changing REST calls without a Splunk Web session cookie.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-changing REST calls where the User-Agent does not match a Splunk Web browser session pattern, excluding known automation accounts.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="/servicesNS/*" method IN ("POST","DELETE")
| where NOT match(useragent, "(?i)(mozilla|chrome|safari)")
| lookup deployment_automation_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_automation
| where isnull(is_automation)
| table _time, user, uri, useragent
tuning_guidance: Expect noise from legitimate scripts/integrations not yet on the automation-account allowlist; use to discover and formally register new automation accounts as much as to catch abuse.
investigation_steps: Identify the calling script/tool.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained; add to the automation allowlist if legitimate.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Cluster Manager Admin Login
description: An admin-capable account authenticated to the Cluster Manager. Given the Cluster Manager's control over every indexer peer's configuration bundle, every admin login is a necessary building block for this section's higher-confidence correlations.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=login attempt=success, restricted to Cluster Manager host
data_sources.description: Admin login events on the Cluster Manager.

detection_logic: Filters admin-account login events where the target host is the Cluster Manager.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success host=<cluster_manager_host>
| lookup splunk_admin_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_admin
| where is_admin=1
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: High routine volume by design; a correlation building block.
investigation_steps: Track for use in downstream correlations.
response_guidance: No standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Cluster Manager Configuration Bundle Modified and Pushed
description: The Cluster Manager's configuration bundle (apps, indexes.conf, and other peer-shared configuration) was modified and pushed to every indexer peer in the cluster — since this bundle is applied to the entire indexing tier at once, a malicious change here has the same fleet-wide blast radius as a Deployment Server compromise, but against indexers rather than forwarders.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Configuration-bundle push events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-bundle push events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMPeer "apply bundle"
| table _time, user, bundle_checksum
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; alert on all occurrences given the fleet-wide indexer-tier blast radius.
investigation_steps: Review the bundle's content diff.
Confirm against an approved change.
response_guidance: Roll back if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Peer Removed from Cluster
description: An indexer peer was removed from the cluster, which reduces search/replication capacity and — if the replication factor is not maintained by remaining peers — can threaten data durability for buckets that were only replicated to the removed peer.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Peer-removal events.

detection_logic: Filters peer-removal events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMMaster "peer removed" OR "peer decommissioned"
| table _time, peer_name
tuning_guidance: Confirm against decommission tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify replication/search factor is still met by remaining peers.
response_guidance: Re-add if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Peer Loss from Indexer Cluster
description: Multiple indexer peers went down or were removed from the cluster within a short window, consistent with a coordinated availability attack against the indexing tier or a cascading infrastructure failure — either way, a severe threat to both search availability and, if replication factor is exceeded, data durability.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Peer down/removal events aggregated per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct peers going down/removed within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMMaster ("peer down" OR "peer removed")
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(peer_name) AS peer_count values(peer_name) AS peers by _time
| where peer_count>=2
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known infrastructure/network incidents before escalating.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent a known infrastructure cause.
Verify replication/search factor status immediately.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call immediately; failover/restore capacity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Cluster Maintenance Mode Enabled Outside Window
description: Maintenance mode was enabled on the indexer cluster outside a documented maintenance window, which suppresses certain cluster health/rebalancing alerts and can be used to mask ongoing disruptive activity as expected maintenance-window noise.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Maintenance-mode enable events.

detection_logic: Filters maintenance-mode-enable events outside a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMMaster "maintenance mode" "enabled"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a maintenance ticket.
Review cluster activity during the maintenance-mode window with elevated scrutiny.
response_guidance: Disable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Replication Factor or Search Factor Reduced
description: The cluster's configured replication factor or search factor was reduced, which lowers data durability and search-availability guarantees — a structural weakening that reduces resilience against subsequent peer loss or data destruction, similar in spirit to the retention-shortening detections in the SPL-DATA section but at the cluster-durability level rather than the individual-index level.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Replication/search factor configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters cluster-configuration-change events where the new replication/search factor value is lower than the prior value.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_server (info="*replication_factor*" OR info="*search_factor*")
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the durability implications; confirm against a documented capacity-planning ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess the resulting durability/availability risk.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bucket Fixup Activity Unusually High
description: The volume of bucket-fixup activity (re-replication of under-replicated buckets) rose sharply, which is normal following a single peer's brief outage but, at a sustained high volume, can indicate an ongoing structural problem — including a deliberate pattern of intermittent peer disruption designed to keep the cluster in a persistently degraded state.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Bucket-fixup event volume compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Compares bucket-fixup event volume against a historical baseline.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMMaster "fixup"
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count AS fixup_count by _time
| eventstats avg(fixup_count) AS avg_count stdev(fixup_count) AS stdev_count
| where fixup_count > (avg_count + 3*stdev_count)
tuning_guidance: Correlate with SPL-CM-004's peer-loss detection for a common root cause.
investigation_steps: Investigate the underlying cause of sustained fixup activity.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Rolling Restart Initiated Outside Maintenance Window
description: A cluster-wide rolling restart was initiated outside a documented maintenance window, which — beyond its operational impact — can be used to force new configuration (including a just-pushed malicious bundle) to take effect across every peer more quickly than the normal check-in cycle would allow.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Rolling-restart initiation events.

detection_logic: Filters rolling-restart initiation events outside a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMMaster "rolling restart"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a maintenance ticket.
Check for a recent bundle push (SPL-CM-002) this restart may be accelerating.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Local Interactive Login
description: A user authenticated to Splunk Web directly on an indexer peer, which — since indexers are typically operated as headless data-storage/search-execution infrastructure managed through the Cluster Manager rather than an interactive tool — is unusual and warrants review.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=login attempt=success, restricted to indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: Login events on indexer-tier hosts.

detection_logic: Filters successful login events where the target host is on the indexer inventory.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=success
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| table _time, user, host
tuning_guidance: Exclude known operations-team accounts with a documented reason for direct indexer administration.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review actions taken during the session.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Splunk Service Stopped
description: The splunkd service was stopped directly on an indexer at the OS level outside a documented maintenance window, halting both ingestion and search for whatever data that indexer holds until the peer is restored or its buckets are re-replicated elsewhere.

data_sources.name: Windows Event Log / systemd journal
data_sources.path: service-stop events for the Splunkd service on indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: OS-level service-control events.

detection_logic: Filters OS service-management events where splunkd stops on an indexer-tier host outside a maintenance window.
spl:
index=<endpoint_index> sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog:System", "linux_secure") service_name="Splunkd" action=stopped
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level service-management telemetry on indexers.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a maintenance ticket.
If unexplained, investigate for concurrent malicious activity and check replication/search factor status.
response_guidance: Restart the service; investigate the host as a potential defense-evasion/availability incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Local Configuration Changed Outside Cluster Bundle Push
description: A local configuration file was changed directly on an indexer's filesystem rather than through the Cluster Manager's bundle-push mechanism, bypassing the change-review process the cluster architecture is designed to centralize.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.path: file-integrity-monitoring events for $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/local and $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/*/local on indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: Local configuration-directory file-modification events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on indexer local configuration directories, filtered to changes not attributable to a bundle push.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/system/local/*" OR file_path="*/etc/apps/*/local/*"
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| lookup cm_bundle_push_events.csv host, _time OUTPUT is_bundle_push
| where isnull(is_bundle_push)
| table _time, host, file_path, user
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM coverage on indexers — a Splunk Cloud limitation since indexer infrastructure is provider-managed and not customer-visible at the filesystem level.
investigation_steps: Diff the file content.
Determine whether this bypasses the Cluster Manager's centralized change process.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unexpected Binary Present in Indexer Application Directory
description: A binary/executable file appeared in an indexer's application or bin directory that was not part of the app's expected content baseline, consistent with a persistence mechanism dropped directly onto the indexer's filesystem rather than delivered through Splunk's own configuration/app-management path.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.path: file-integrity-monitoring events for executable files under $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/*/bin on indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: Unexpected executable file-creation events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM comparing new executable files against each app's expected content baseline.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/etc/apps/*/bin/*" action=created
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| lookup app_content_baseline.csv file_path OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, host, file_path
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM and a maintained per-app content baseline — a Splunk Cloud limitation as with SPL-IDX-003.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Isolate the host and analyze the binary.
response_guidance: Remove the binary and conduct full incident response on the host.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1574: Hijack Execution Flow

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Root/Admin Shell Activity on Indexer Host
description: A root/administrator-level interactive shell session was established on an indexer host, warranting the same scrutiny given to any Tier-0 infrastructure since the indexer holds the organization's raw indexed security data at rest.

data_sources.name: Sysmon / auditd
data_sources.path: interactive shell process creation with root/administrator privilege on indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: Privileged interactive-session process telemetry.

detection_logic: Filters privileged interactive shell process-creation events on indexer-tier hosts.
spl:
index=<endpoint_index> sourcetype IN (Sysmon, auditd) (process_name="bash" OR process_name="sh" OR process_name="powershell.exe") user IN ("root","Administrator")
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| table _time, host, user, process_name
tuning_guidance: Exclude known break-glass/on-call access with a documented ticket; a Splunk Cloud limitation given no customer OS access exists on provider-managed indexers.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented access request.
Review commands executed during the session.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Index Path Modified at Indexer Level
description: An index's homePath/coldPath storage location was changed on an individual indexer, which — outside a coordinated storage-migration project pushed via the Cluster Manager bundle — can redirect where a specific index's data is physically stored, potentially to storage outside the organization's normal backup/protection scope.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_indexes info=*homePath* OR info=*coldPath*, restricted to indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: Index storage-path configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters index storage-path configuration-change events on indexer-tier hosts.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_indexes (info="*homePath*" OR info="*coldPath*")
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| table _time, user, object, info, host
tuning_guidance: Confirm against storage-migration change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new path is authorized, protected storage.
Confirm data was migrated correctly rather than silently starting fresh at the new path.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Firewall/Network Exposure Changed
description: A network-layer firewall rule change exposed an indexer's receiving or management port to a broader network range than intended, widening the attack surface against Tier-0 infrastructure that should typically be reachable only from a small set of known forwarders and management hosts.

data_sources.name: Firewall Change Log
data_sources.description: Firewall rule-change events affecting indexer host/port ranges.

detection_logic: Filters firewall rule-change events where the destination matches an indexer host/port and the new source scope is broader than before.
spl:
index=<firewall_index> sourcetype=<firewall_change_sourcetype>
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv destination AS host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| table _time, user, rule_id, destination, old_source_scope, new_source_scope
tuning_guidance: Requires network firewall change telemetry, not visible from Splunk's own logs; confirm against network change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new scope against the intended architecture.
Assess resulting exposure.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: T1562 (Impair Defenses) most directly describes broadening network exposure to a protected asset but is not present in this library's validated MITRE technique cache; the citation below uses the closest validated alternative.

title: Indexer Storage Capacity Approaching Exhaustion
description: An indexer's storage utilization approached capacity exhaustion, which — beyond ordinary operational concern — can be induced deliberately through the volume-based ingestion attacks covered elsewhere in this catalogue (SPL-DATA-024/025, SPL-HEC-012) to force premature data aging or search-blocking behavior.

data_sources.name: introspection_generator
data_sources.description: Disk-utilization introspection metrics for indexer volumes.

detection_logic: Flags indexer volumes with available capacity below a threshold.
spl:
index=_introspection component=DiskObjects
| where 'data.available_pct'<10
| table _time, host, 'data.available_pct'
tuning_guidance: Tune the threshold to your capacity-planning alerting standards; correlate with SPL-DATA-024/025/SPL-HEC-012 for a possible malicious cause.
investigation_steps: Determine the cause of the capacity pressure.
Check for a concurrent ingestion-volume anomaly.
response_guidance: Add capacity or reduce retention on lower-priority indexes as an interim mitigation; investigate if malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer TLS Certificate Changed Unexpectedly
description: An indexer's TLS certificate for the receiving connection changed without a corresponding entry in the certificate-rotation change log, warranting the same interception-risk review as the equivalent forwarder-side detection (SPL-FWD-014).

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.path: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc, restricted to indexer-tier hosts
data_sources.description: TLS handshake events compared against a known-good baseline.

detection_logic: Compares observed indexer certificate fingerprints against a maintained known-good baseline.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc "certificate"
| lookup indexer_inventory.csv host OUTPUT is_indexer
| where is_indexer=1
| lookup update=true known_cert_fingerprints.csv host OUTPUT expected_fingerprint
| where isnotnull(expected_fingerprint) AND cert_fingerprint!=expected_fingerprint
| table _time, host, cert_fingerprint, expected_fingerprint
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained certificate-fingerprint baseline.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented rotation ticket.
If unexplained, treat as a possible interception incident.
response_guidance: Investigate the network path if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Log File Deleted or Truncated at OS Level
description: Splunk's own operational log files (splunkd.log, audit.log) were deleted or truncated directly at the OS level on an indexer, which — since these are the source logs this entire catalogue's SPL-INT section depends on for the platform's own self-monitoring — is a direct attack on the observability of the security infrastructure itself.

data_sources.name: FIM
data_sources.description: Splunk operational log-file deletion/truncation events.

detection_logic: Requires OS-level FIM on the Splunk operational log directory, filtered to deletion/truncation actions.
spl:
index=<fim_index> sourcetype=<fim_sourcetype> file_path="*/var/log/splunk/*" action IN (deleted, truncated)
| table _time, host, file_path, user
tuning_guidance: Requires FIM — a Splunk Cloud limitation since customers have no filesystem access to provider-managed indexer log directories.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed anti-forensics incident.
Preserve any remaining log evidence and any downstream-forwarded copy that survived the deletion.
response_guidance: Full incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Added to Cluster from Unrecognized Network Segment
description: A new indexer peer joined the cluster from a network segment/CIDR range not on the organization's expected data-center inventory, consistent with a rogue peer attempting to join the cluster's replication trust relationship from unauthorized infrastructure.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Peer-addition events with source network.

detection_logic: Joins new-peer-addition events against an expected-datacenter-CIDR lookup.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=CMMaster "peer added"
| lookup expected_indexer_networks.csv peer_ip OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, peer_name, peer_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-network lookup.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Verify the new peer's identity and ownership.
response_guidance: Remove the peer immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Indexer Cluster Bucket Integrity Check Failure
description: A bucket integrity check (hash verification) failed on an indexer, which can indicate either underlying storage corruption or deliberate tampering with indexed bucket data at the filesystem level, bypassing Splunk's own indexing pipeline entirely.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Bucket integrity-check failure events.

detection_logic: Filters bucket integrity-check failure events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=BucketReplicator "integrity check failed"
| table _time, host, bucket_id
tuning_guidance: Rule out disk/hardware failure via infrastructure monitoring before attributing to tampering.
investigation_steps: Determine if the cause is hardware failure or unauthorized bucket modification.
If tampering is suspected, isolate the host for forensic imaging.
response_guidance: Engage incident response if tampering is confirmed; otherwise remediate the storage issue.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: KV Store Collection Created
description: A new KV Store collection was created. Routine during legitimate app development, but a necessary building block for detecting an unauthorized collection used to stage exfiltrated data or store attacker configuration.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: KV Store collection-creation events.

detection_logic: Filters KV Store collection-creation audit events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_kvstore info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against app-development change tickets.
investigation_steps: Review the collection's owning app and purpose.
response_guidance: No standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: KV Store Collection Permissions Broadened
description: A KV Store collection's sharing/permission level was broadened, particularly concerning for collections backing Enterprise Security's asset/identity or notable-event state, which — if made broadly readable/writable — expose or allow tampering with security-critical state data.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: KV Store collection permission-change events.

detection_logic: Filters KV Store permission-change events, prioritized by an ES-collection tag lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_kvstore info="*sharing*"
| lookup es_kvstore_collections.csv collection_name AS object OUTPUT is_es_data
| table _time, user, object, info, is_es_data
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; alert on all occurrences for ES-tagged collections.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess who now has access to this collection.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bulk Document Deletion from KV Store Collection
description: A large number of documents were deleted from a KV Store collection in a short window, which — for collections backing ES asset/identity data, notable-event workflow state, or app-critical lookups — is a significant data-destruction event with the same evidence-destruction implications as the index-level detections in SPL-DATA.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: KV Store bulk-delete REST calls aggregated per collection per window.

detection_logic: Counts DELETE calls against a KV Store collection's data endpoint within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="*/storage/collections/data/*" method=DELETE
| rex field=uri "/collections/data/(?<collection_name>[^/]+)"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, user, collection_name
| where count>=50
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented data-remediation process; alert on all occurrences for ES-tagged collections.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent an approved remediation ticket.
Determine what data was deleted and whether backups/exports exist.
response_guidance: Restore from backup if available; investigate the acting account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unusual Bulk Export from KV Store Collection
description: A user retrieved an unusually large number of documents from a KV Store collection via the REST API in a short window, consistent with bulk exfiltration of the collection's contents (which may include asset/identity data, credentials referenced by lookups, or other sensitive app state).

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.description: KV Store GET requests with response size, compared against a per-user baseline.

detection_logic: Compares each user's KV Store GET response size against their own historical baseline.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="*/storage/collections/data/*" method=GET
| rex field=uri "/collections/data/(?<collection_name>[^/]+)"
| eventstats avg(bytes) AS avg_bytes stdev(bytes) AS stdev_bytes by user
| where bytes > (avg_bytes + 3*stdev_bytes) AND bytes>1000000
| table _time, user, collection_name, bytes
tuning_guidance: Exclude known automation/integration accounts with legitimately large bulk reads.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Determine what the collection contains.
response_guidance: Investigate for exfiltration if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES Asset/Identity KV Store Data Modified at Scale
description: A large number of records were modified in the KV Store collections backing Enterprise Security's asset or identity framework, which can be used to strip criticality/priority metadata from sensitive assets at scale, degrading risk-based alerting and notable-event prioritization fleet-wide.

data_sources.name: splunkd_access.log
data_sources.path: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="*/storage/collections/data/*" method IN (POST, PUT)
data_sources.description: Bulk write operations against ES asset/identity KV Store collections.

detection_logic: Counts write operations against ES-tagged asset/identity collections per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_access uri="*/storage/collections/data/*" method IN ("POST","PUT")
| rex field=uri "/collections/data/(?<collection_name>[^/]+)"
| lookup es_kvstore_collections.csv collection_name OUTPUT is_asset_identity
| where is_asset_identity=1
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count by _time, user, collection_name
| where count>=50
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented asset/identity data-refresh project (e.g. a scheduled CMDB sync).
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess the resulting impact on ES risk scoring and notable-event prioritization.
response_guidance: Restore from backup if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: KV Store Service Failure on Search Head
description: The KV Store (mongod) service failed or became unreachable on a search head, which — beyond general operational impact — can disrupt Enterprise Security's ability to read/write notable-event workflow state, asset/identity data, and other app-critical collections.

data_sources.name: mongod.log
data_sources.description: KV Store service failure/unreachable events.

detection_logic: Filters KV Store service failure events.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=mongod ("failed to start" OR "connection refused" OR status=DOWN)
| table _time, host
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known infrastructure incidents before escalating.
investigation_steps: Investigate the underlying cause.
Assess ES functionality impact.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: KV Store Lookup-Backed Definition Modified
description: A lookup definition backed by a KV Store collection (rather than a static CSV) was modified, which — since these lookups are frequently used in security correlation searches for allowlisting/threat-intel purposes — carries the same tampering risk as the CSV-based lookup detections in SPL-KO but through the KV Store configuration path specifically.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: KV Store-backed lookup definition-change events.

detection_logic: Filters lookup-definition modification events specifically for KV Store-backed (as opposed to file-based) lookups.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup info="*kvstore*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Diff the lookup definition before and after.
Determine which searches depend on it.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: KV Store Accessed Directly via mongo Shell/Driver
description: A connection was made to the KV Store's underlying mongod process directly (bypassing Splunk's REST API and, with it, Splunk's own RBAC and audit trail entirely), which — if the KV Store port is reachable and the shared secret is known or guessable — is a way to read or modify security-relevant collection data with none of the visibility SPL-KV-001 through SPL-KV-005 depend on.

data_sources.name: Network flow / auditd
data_sources.path: network connections to the KV Store port (default 8191) from a source other than the local splunkd process
data_sources.description: Non-splunkd connections to the KV Store listener port.

detection_logic: Filters network connection events to the KV Store port where the connecting process is not splunkd itself.
spl:
index=<network_index> dest_port=8191
| where src_process!="splunkd"
| table _time, host, src_ip, src_process, dest_port
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level network/process telemetry correlating connections to their originating process — a Splunk Cloud limitation given no direct network path to provider-managed KV Store infrastructure exists for customers in the first place.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed direct-access incident bypassing Splunk's own audit trail.
Determine what was read or modified using KV Store's own oplog if available.
response_guidance: Block direct network access to the KV Store port from anything other than localhost/splunkd; rotate the KV Store shared secret.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES Correlation Search Disabled at Scale
description: An unusually large number of Enterprise Security correlation searches were disabled by a single actor in a short window — the fleet-wide variant of SPL-KO-001, confirming a coordinated attempt to blind detection coverage across the ES app broadly rather than a single targeted search.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info=*disabled=1*, restricted to the ES app
data_sources.description: Correlation-search disable events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts ES-app correlation-search disable events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*disabled=1*" app=SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(object) AS searches by _time, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; ES correlation-search tuning projects should disable searches incrementally with review, not in bulk.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Re-enable all affected searches immediately.
response_guidance: Re-enable immediately and investigate for a subsequent matching malicious event during the gap.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES Correlation Search Skipped Due to Concurrency
description: One or more ES correlation searches were skipped due to search concurrency limits, meaning detection coverage had a gap during the skipped run regardless of cause — the ES-specific instance of the general scheduled-search-skip detection (SPL-SEARCH-011).

data_sources.name: scheduler.log
data_sources.description: Skipped ES correlation-search events.

detection_logic: Filters skipped scheduled-search events for ES correlation searches specifically.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=scheduler status=skipped app=SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite
| table _time, savedsearch_name, reason
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the direct detection-coverage-gap implication.
investigation_steps: Determine what caused the concurrency saturation (see SPL-SEARCH-011).
Manually run the skipped search against the missed window.
response_guidance: Address the concurrency constraint and backfill the skipped search's coverage.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES Notable Event Mass Status Change
description: A single analyst account changed the status of an unusually large number of notable events (e.g. bulk-closing as resolved/false-positive) in a short window, which — beyond a legitimate backlog-clearing exercise — can be used to hide evidence of a genuine intrusion by closing out the notables that would otherwise flag it for investigation.

data_sources.name: notable_events lookup / KV Store
data_sources.path: index=_audit OR notable-event workflow change events
data_sources.description: Notable-event status-change events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts notable-event status-change events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
`notable`
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(status) AS statuses by _time, user
| where count>=20
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented backlog-triage session; scope closer scrutiny to bulk closures marked as false-positive without individual review notes.
investigation_steps: Sample a subset of the bulk-closed notables and verify the closure justification.
Check whether any closed notable correlates with confirmed malicious activity elsewhere.
response_guidance: Reopen incorrectly-closed notables and investigate the underlying activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES Notable Event Closed Within Minutes of Creation
description: A notable event was closed (particularly as resolved or false-positive) within minutes of being created, well before a genuine investigation could plausibly have been completed, consistent with an insider or compromised analyst account rubber-stamping closures to suppress alerting on their own or an accomplice's activity.

data_sources.name: notable_events lookup / KV Store
data_sources.path: Notable-event creation and closure timestamps for the same rule_id
data_sources.description: Time-to-close computed per notable event.

detection_logic: Computes the gap between notable-event creation and closure timestamps and flags closures under a threshold.
spl:
`notable`
| stats earliest(_time) AS created latest(_time) AS closed_time values(status) AS statuses by rule_id, user
| eval time_to_close=closed_time-created
| where time_to_close<120 AND match(statuses, "(?i)(resolved|false positive)")
| table rule_id, user, time_to_close
tuning_guidance: Exclude genuinely obvious false-positive patterns (e.g. a known noisy detection with a documented rapid-triage runbook).
investigation_steps: Review the notable's underlying evidence independently.
Interview the analyst if the pattern repeats.
response_guidance: Reopen and properly investigate if the closure appears unjustified.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Risk-Based Alerting Rule Modified to Reduce Score
description: A risk-scoring rule was modified to reduce the risk score it assigns, which — since risk-based alerting aggregates scores across many low-severity events into a cumulative risk-notable trigger — can be used to keep a specific pattern of activity permanently below the alerting threshold without disabling the underlying detection entirely.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info=*risk_score*, restricted to the ES app
data_sources.description: Risk-scoring configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters risk-scoring rule modification events where the new score is lower than the prior value.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*risk_score*" app=SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite
| rex field=info "risk_score=(?<new_score>\d+)"
| lookup update=true risk_score_baseline.csv object OUTPUT prior_score
| where new_score<prior_score
| table _time, user, object, prior_score, new_score
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented risk-scoring tuning project.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess whether this rule's contribution to any recent risk-notable threshold was materially affected.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Risk Index Stops Receiving Events
description: The risk index stopped receiving new risk events entirely, which — since risk-based alerting depends on the continuous accumulation of risk events to trigger risk notables — silently disables the entire risk-based-alerting detection strategy across every correlation search that feeds it.

data_sources.name: risk index metadata
data_sources.path: | tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=risk
data_sources.description: Risk index ingestion-gap check.

detection_logic: Checks for a gap in risk-index ingestion exceeding the expected interval.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=risk
| eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60)
| where minutes_since>=30
tuning_guidance: A Tier-1 heartbeat detection; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Determine why risk events stopped — check for a disabled risk action (SPL-KO-005) or a broader ingestion issue.
Treat as a top-priority visibility gap.
response_guidance: Restore immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Excessive Negative or Zero Risk-Score Adjustments Applied
description: An unusually large number of manual risk-score adjustments (used to correct/offset an entity's accumulated risk) were applied in a short window, which — if applied to suppress a specific entity's risk score ahead of a threshold-based risk-notable trigger — can be used to keep an actively compromised account or asset from ever surfacing as a risk notable.

data_sources.name: risk adjustment log
data_sources.path: risk-score manual-adjustment events aggregated per actor per window
data_sources.description: Manual risk-score adjustment events.

detection_logic: Counts manual risk-score adjustment events per actor within a rolling window, filtered to negative adjustments.
spl:
`risk_adjustment` adjustment<0
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count values(risk_object) AS objects by _time, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Confirm against documented risk-tuning exceptions.
investigation_steps: Review each affected entity's actual current risk posture independently of the adjustment.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Reverse unauthorized adjustments and re-evaluate the affected entities' risk.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged Asset Criticality Reduced or Category Removed
description: An asset previously tagged as high-criticality or belonging to a privileged category (domain controller, Tier-0 infrastructure) had its criticality reduced or category removed in the asset lookup, which — since many correlation searches and risk rules weight severity by asset criticality — can silently lower the alerting priority of activity against that specific asset.

data_sources.name: asset lookup
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_lookup object=asset_lookup, or the equivalent ES asset-management workflow
data_sources.description: Asset criticality/category modification events.

detection_logic: Compares each asset-lookup edit's resulting criticality/category against the prior value and flags downgrades for previously-high-value assets.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup object="asset_lookup"
| lookup update=true asset_criticality_baseline.csv asset OUTPUT prior_criticality
| where prior_criticality="high" AND new_criticality!="high"
| table _time, user, asset, prior_criticality, new_criticality
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented asset-inventory refresh process; alert on all occurrences for Tier-0-tagged assets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the criticality change.
Restore if unauthorized.
response_guidance: Restore the original criticality/category if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Identity Privileged Flag Removed
description: A user identity previously flagged as privileged/watchlisted in the identity lookup had that flag removed, which — like the asset-criticality equivalent (SPL-ES-008) — can silently lower the alerting priority of that user's subsequent activity across every correlation search weighting by identity privilege.

data_sources.name: identity lookup
data_sources.description: Identity privilege-flag modification events.

detection_logic: Compares each identity-lookup edit against the prior privileged-flag value and flags removals.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_lookup object="identity_lookup"
| lookup update=true identity_privilege_baseline.csv identity OUTPUT prior_flag
| where prior_flag="privileged" AND new_flag!="privileged"
| table _time, user, identity, prior_flag, new_flag
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented identity-inventory refresh (e.g. HR-driven role changes).
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Restore if unauthorized.
response_guidance: Restore the flag if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Asset/Identity Lookup Enrichment Disappears
description: The scheduled search populating the asset or identity lookup stopped running or started returning zero results, which will cause the lookup's enrichment data to silently go stale — new assets/identities added to the environment since the failure will not receive criticality/privilege classification, understating their risk.

data_sources.name: scheduler.log
data_sources.description: Asset/identity lookup-generation search execution status.

detection_logic: Filters asset/identity lookup-generation search executions with a failed status or zero result count.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=scheduler (savedsearch_name="*Asset*" OR savedsearch_name="*Identity*") app=SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite
| where status="failed" OR result_count=0
| table _time, savedsearch_name, status, result_count
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the stale-enrichment implication.
investigation_steps: Investigate the search failure cause.
Determine how long the lookup has been stale.
response_guidance: Fix the underlying search and manually refresh the lookup.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Threat Intelligence Feed Source Disabled
description: A threat-intelligence feed source was disabled, which stops that feed's IOCs from being ingested into the threat-intel framework — the ES-level equivalent of SPL-KO-011's lookup-tampering detection, but at the feed-configuration level rather than the resulting lookup file.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Threat-intel source configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters threat-intel source configuration-change events where the source is disabled.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_ta_source info="*disabled=1*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against feed-management change tickets; alert on all occurrences given detection-coverage impact.
investigation_steps: Re-enable immediately.
Determine how long the feed was disabled and what IOC updates were missed.
response_guidance: Re-enable and manually trigger a feed refresh.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Threat Intelligence Feed URL Changed
description: A threat-intelligence feed's source URL was changed, which — if pointed at an attacker-controlled or simply inert endpoint — can starve the threat-intel framework of legitimate IOCs while appearing to remain active and functioning.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Threat-intel source URL configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters threat-intel source configuration-change events touching the feed URL.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_ta_source info="*url*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against feed-management change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new URL is the authorized, legitimate feed source.
Confirm IOC ingestion continues correctly post-change.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Threat Intel Feed Stops Updating
description: A threat-intelligence feed that has historically updated on a regular schedule has not produced new IOC records in an unexpectedly long time, whether due to a silent feed-side outage, a network path issue, or the configuration tampering covered by SPL-ES-011/012.

data_sources.name: threat_activity / KV Store
data_sources.path: | tstats latest(_time) AS last_update by ta_source
data_sources.description: Per-feed last-update timestamp compared to expected refresh cadence.

detection_logic: Flags threat-intel sources with no update within 3x their configured refresh interval.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) AS last_update where index=threat_activity by ta_source
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_update)/3600)
| where hours_since>=48
| table ta_source, last_update, hours_since
tuning_guidance: Tune the threshold to each feed's actual documented refresh cadence.
investigation_steps: Check for SPL-ES-011/012-style tampering.
If not tampering, check the feed provider's own service status.
response_guidance: Restore feed updates; escalate to the feed provider if the issue is upstream.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Investigation Field Altered Anomalously
description: A field on an active investigation/incident was modified in a way inconsistent with normal investigation workflow (e.g. removed evidence attachments, altered timeline entries), which can indicate tampering with the record of an ongoing incident response.

data_sources.name: Investigation workflow log
data_sources.description: Investigation record field-change events.

detection_logic: Lists investigation field-modification events for manual review; automated anomaly scoring depends on your ES version's specific investigation-workbench audit schema.
spl:
`investigation_change`
| table _time, user, investigation_id, field_changed, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Requires validation against your specific ES version's investigation-workbench audit event schema; treat as a hunting query pending richer telemetry.
investigation_steps: Review the change against the investigation's own change history for context.
Confirm with the assigned analyst.
response_guidance: Restore if the change appears to be evidence tampering.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Suppression Rule Created with No Expiration
description: A notable-event suppression rule was created without an expiration date, meaning it will silently continue suppressing matching notables indefinitely rather than being subject to periodic review — a durable, easy-to-forget detection-tampering mechanism.

data_sources.name: suppression configuration
data_sources.path: index=_audit action=edit_suppression, or the equivalent ES suppression-management workflow
data_sources.description: Suppression-rule creation events with expiration field.

detection_logic: Filters suppression-rule creation events where the expiration field is empty/null.
spl:
`suppression_created` OR (index=_audit action=edit_suppression info=created)
| where isnull(expiration) OR expiration=""
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Enforce a mandatory-expiration policy for suppression rules organizationally; alert on all occurrences of a non-expiring rule.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Set an appropriate expiration or review date.
response_guidance: Add an expiration date if the suppression is legitimate; remove if not.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Suppression Rule Applies to Unusually Many Correlation Searches
description: A single suppression rule's matching criteria are broad enough to apply across an unusually large number of distinct correlation searches, which — unlike a narrowly-scoped, single-search suppression — can mask a broad category of activity across the entire detection portfolio.

data_sources.name: suppression configuration
data_sources.path: Suppression-rule matching criteria compared against the correlation-search inventory
data_sources.description: Suppression-rule breadth analysis.

detection_logic: A scheduled review search evaluating each suppression rule's matching criteria against the full correlation-search inventory and flagging rules matching an unusually large count.
spl:
`suppression_rules`
| eval matching_search_count=<computed_match_count_against_correlation_searches>
| where matching_search_count>=10
| table suppression_id, matching_search_count
tuning_guidance: Requires computing each rule's actual match breadth against the correlation-search inventory — implementation depends on your ES version's suppression-rule matching model.
investigation_steps: Review the suppression rule's matching criteria for unintended breadth.
Narrow the scope to the minimum necessary.
response_guidance: Narrow the suppression scope.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Suppression Rule Created by Unusual User
description: A suppression rule was created by an account outside the small, well-established set of analysts/engineers who typically manage suppression policy, which — given how directly suppression rules can blind the SOC — warrants elevated scrutiny for any account creating one for the first time.

data_sources.name: suppression configuration
data_sources.path: Suppression-rule creation events compared against a known-suppression-manager account lookup
data_sources.description: Suppression-rule creation events by non-standard actors.

detection_logic: Filters suppression-rule creation events where the actor is not on the known-suppression-manager lookup.
spl:
`suppression_created`
| lookup suppression_manager_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_known_manager
| where isnull(is_known_manager)
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Maintain the known-suppression-manager lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review the suppression's scope with elevated scrutiny given the account's unfamiliarity with the process.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES App Permission Broadened
description: A role's access to the Enterprise Security app itself (or a specific ES capability like ess_admin) was broadened, granting the ability to view or modify security-critical content beyond what the standard SOC-analyst role provides.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Role capability-change events for ES-specific capabilities.

detection_logic: Filters role-modification events adding ES-specific capabilities (ess_admin, ess_analyst with elevated scope).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_roles info="*ess_*"
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against RBAC change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Review the target role's user membership.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ES Data Model Coverage Percentage Declines Sharply
description: The Security Posture or Data Model Audit dashboard's reported CIM coverage percentage declined sharply, aggregating the individual data-model-coverage detections (SPL-KO-018) into a single platform-health signal that ES itself is positioned to surface.

data_sources.name: Data Model Audit dashboard data
data_sources.description: Aggregated CIM coverage percentage compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Compares ES's self-reported data-model coverage percentage against a historical baseline.
spl:
`datamodel_audit`
| eventstats avg(coverage_pct) AS avg_coverage stdev(coverage_pct) AS stdev_coverage by datamodel
| where coverage_pct < (avg_coverage - 3*stdev_coverage)
tuning_guidance: Version-dependent on ES's specific Data Model Audit implementation; validate the underlying macro/lookup against your deployment.
investigation_steps: Identify which underlying sourcetypes/tags are responsible for the decline.
Cross-reference with SPL-KO-016 through SPL-KO-020.
response_guidance: Restore the affected tag/data-model configuration.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Federated Search Provider Added or Changed
description: A federated search provider was added or its connection configuration changed, which — since federated search allows querying remote Splunk deployments' data as though local — can be used to either exfiltrate data to an attacker-controlled remote Splunk instance or introduce a persistent, remote data-access path that bypasses this instance's own local RBAC on the remote side.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Federated search provider configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters federated search provider configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_federated_provider
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; alert on all occurrences given the cross-instance data-access implication.
investigation_steps: Verify the provider is an authorized, known Splunk deployment.
Review the credential used for the federated connection.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Federated Search Credentials Changed
description: The stored credential used for a federated search connection was changed, warranting confirmation that the change was performed through an authorized rotation process given the credential's cross-instance data-access scope.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Federated search credential-change events.

detection_logic: Filters federated provider configuration-change events touching the credential field.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_federated_provider info="*credential*"
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a credential-rotation change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the rotation was performed by an authorized administrator.
response_guidance: Rotate again through the proper channel if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Large Federated Query Against Remote Dataset
description: A federated search returned an unusually large result set from a remote provider, which — like the local-search export detections (SPL-SEARCH-014) — can indicate bulk data collection from a remote Splunk deployment via the federated search capability.

data_sources.name: searches.log
data_sources.description: Federated search job completion events with result count.

detection_logic: Filters federated search completions with an unusually large result count.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=searches search="*federated:*"
| where result_count>10000
| table _time, user, search, result_count
tuning_guidance: Exclude known reporting/dashboard use cases with legitimately large federated result sets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for a subsequent export.
response_guidance: Investigate for exfiltration if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Federated Search for S3 Bucket/Catalog Changed
description: Federated Search for Amazon S3's bucket or catalog configuration was changed, which — where deployed — can redirect S3-backed federated queries to an unauthorized or attacker-controlled S3 location, or grant broader storage access than intended.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Federated Search for S3 configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters Federated Search for S3 configuration-change events.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_federated_s3_config
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — only applicable where Federated Search for S3 is deployed; validate against your specific configuration's audit schema.
investigation_steps: Verify the new bucket/catalog is authorized.
Confirm the resulting access scope.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: SOAR Integration Credential Changed
description: The credential used for the ES-to-SOAR integration was changed, which — since this integration typically drives automated containment/remediation actions — could allow an attacker to redirect or disable the automated response workflow, or (if the new credential is attacker-supplied) intercept the notables/data sent to SOAR.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: SOAR integration credential/endpoint configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters app-configuration-change events touching the SOAR/Phantom integration credential or endpoint.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app (info="*soar*" OR info="*phantom*")
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented credential-rotation ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the change was authorized.
Verify the SOAR integration still functions correctly.
response_guidance: Rotate again through the proper channel if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SOAR Automated Playbook Trigger Removed or Disabled
description: A SOAR playbook's automated trigger was disabled or removed, which — like an ES correlation search being disabled — silently stops the automated containment/enrichment response that would otherwise fire when the associated event occurs, without necessarily disabling the underlying detection that feeds it.

data_sources.name: SOAR Audit Log
data_sources.description: Playbook trigger disable/removal events.

detection_logic: Filters SOAR playbook trigger configuration-change events where the trigger transitions to disabled.
spl:
index=<soar_audit_index> sourcetype=<soar_audit_sourcetype> event="PlaybookTriggerChanged" trigger_status="disabled"
| table _time, user, playbook_name, trigger_status
tuning_guidance: Product/version dependent — validate against your SOAR deployment's actual audit event schema; alert on all occurrences for playbooks handling containment actions.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent an approved change ticket.
Re-enable immediately.
response_guidance: Re-enable and audit for a subsequent matching event that should have triggered the playbook.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACS API Authentication Failure Burst
description: Repeated failed authentication attempts occurred against the Splunk Cloud Admin Config Service (ACS) API, consistent with an attacker attempting to brute-force or guess the ACS API token that governs Cloud-side administrative operations.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: ACS API authentication failure events.

detection_logic: Counts ACS API authentication failures per source within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=login attempt=failure
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, src
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Validate the exact ACS audit sourcetype/event schema against your Splunk Cloud stack; do not assume literal field names without confirming against your own environment's ACS activity log.
investigation_steps: Identify the source.
Check for a subsequent successful ACS authentication.
response_guidance: Rotate the ACS API token if a subsequent success is confirmed from an unrecognized source.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: First-Seen Source for ACS API Access
description: The ACS API was accessed from a source IP never previously seen using this stack's ACS token, which — since ACS tokens are typically used from a small, stable set of CI/CD or administrative automation sources — is a strong signal the token has been exfiltrated and is in use elsewhere.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: ACS API access events compared against a source-IP baseline.

detection_logic: Joins ACS API access events against a lookup of previously-seen source IPs for this stack's ACS usage.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=login attempt=success
| lookup update=true acs_src_baseline.csv src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, src
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained source-IP baseline; validate the ACS audit schema against your stack.
investigation_steps: Verify the source is an expected, authorized automation host.
Rotate the token if not.
response_guidance: Rotate the ACS token if the source cannot be confirmed as legitimate.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACS-Driven User or Role Administration
description: A user or role was created/modified through the ACS API rather than Splunk Web/REST directly, warranting the same RBAC change-management review as any other role/user change (see SPL-AUTH-023 and SPL-RBAC-020) but confirmed here specifically through the ACS-side audit trail.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: ACS-driven user/role administration events.

detection_logic: Filters ACS API calls to user/role administration endpoints.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action IN ("user_admin","role_admin")
| table _time, user, object, action
tuning_guidance: Validate against your stack's actual ACS audit schema; cross-reference with SPL-RBAC-020.
investigation_steps: Confirm against an approved ACS-driven RBAC request.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACS IP Allow-List Broadened
description: A Splunk Cloud IP allow-list (management access, search-head access, or HEC access) was broadened to include a new, wider CIDR range or removed entirely — since Splunk Cloud customers cannot rely on OS-level network controls the way an on-premises deployment could, these allow-lists are one of the primary network-exposure controls actually available to a Cloud customer, making changes here especially consequential.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: IP allow-list configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters IP allow-list configuration-change events where the new CIDR range is broader than the prior range or the list was removed.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=ip_allowlist_changed
| table _time, user, allowlist_type, old_cidrs, new_cidrs
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given how central this control is to Splunk Cloud's network-exposure posture; validate against your stack's ACS audit schema.
investigation_steps: Verify the new CIDR range is authorized and as narrow as operationally necessary.
Treat any removal of the allow-list entirely as a critical incident.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HEC IP Allow-List Broadened
description: The IP allow-list governing which networks may submit events to Splunk Cloud's HEC endpoint was broadened — the HEC-specific variant of SPL-CLOUD-004, which combined with a leaked HEC token, expands the population of network locations from which that token can be abused.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: HEC-specific IP allow-list configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters IP allow-list configuration-change events scoped specifically to the HEC allow-list type.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=ip_allowlist_changed allowlist_type=hec
| table _time, user, old_cidrs, new_cidrs
tuning_guidance: Validate against your stack's ACS audit schema.
investigation_steps: Verify the new range against your organization's actual HEC-sending infrastructure.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud App Uploaded
description: An app was uploaded to Splunk Cloud through the customer-visible self-service app-installation workflow, which passes through Splunk's own vetting process before activation but should still be tracked and reviewed the same as any other app-installation event given the code-execution surface apps introduce.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App-upload events on a Splunk Cloud stack.

detection_logic: Filters app-installation events (same underlying event as SPL-APP-001, called out separately here for the Cloud-specific vetting-workflow context).
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info=created
| table _time, user, object
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with SPL-APP-001; on Splunk Cloud this event should also correlate with a vetting-approval record.
investigation_steps: Confirm the app passed Splunk Cloud's vetting process.
Review the app's contents (see SPL-APP-### for detailed guidance).
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized or unvetted.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud App Version Unexpectedly Changed
description: An app's reported version on Splunk Cloud changed without a corresponding entry in the change-management record, which — since Splunk Cloud's vetting process re-validates each new version — should always leave an audit trail if performed through the sanctioned upgrade path.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App version-change events compared against a change-ticket lookup.

detection_logic: Filters app version-change events not correlated with an approved change ticket.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info="*version*"
| lookup app_change_tickets.csv object, _time OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, user, object, info
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained change-ticket lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm the version change went through Splunk Cloud's vetting workflow.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud App Disabled or Removed
description: An app was disabled or removed on Splunk Cloud through the customer-visible workflow, warranting the same review given to any app-removal event elsewhere in this catalogue (SPL-APP-018) since disabling/removing security-relevant apps remains available to Cloud customers within their own management scope.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: App disable/removal events on a Splunk Cloud stack.

detection_logic: Filters app disable/removal events, cross-referenced with a security-relevant app lookup.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info IN ("disabled","removed")
| lookup security_relevant_apps.csv app_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_relevant
| table _time, user, object, info, is_security_relevant
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with SPL-APP-018.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess coverage impact for security-relevant apps.
response_guidance: Re-enable/reinstall if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Data Source Interruption Coinciding with Splunk Cloud Maintenance
description: An ingestion-volume drop for a customer-managed source coincided with a scheduled Splunk Cloud maintenance window, which is most often benign provider-side maintenance impact but should still be reconciled to confirm the source actually recovers post-maintenance rather than remaining silently broken.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Ingestion-volume-drop events (per SPL-INT-###) correlated against Splunk Cloud's published maintenance-window schedule
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: volume drop, coinciding with maintenance.

detection_logic: Joins ingestion-volume-drop events against Splunk Cloud's maintenance-notification schedule (imported via API or manual lookup).
spl:
| tstats count where index=* by sourcetype, _time span=1h
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count stdev(count) AS stdev_count by sourcetype
| where count < (avg_count - 3*stdev_count)
| lookup splunk_cloud_maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT maintenance_reason
| where isnotnull(maintenance_reason)
tuning_guidance: Requires importing Splunk Cloud's maintenance schedule into a lookup; primarily an operational-reconciliation search rather than a security alert.
investigation_steps: Confirm the source recovers once maintenance concludes.
If it does not, escalate as an unresolved ingestion-gap incident (see SPL-INT-### for the security-relevant escalation path).
response_guidance: No security action needed if the source recovers; escalate if it does not.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Same cost profile as SPL-DATA-014's tstats-based volume check; schedule at a lower frequency and scope to known-critical sourcetypes.

title: Customer Configuration Change Immediately Preceding Splunk Cloud Maintenance
description: A customer-side configuration change (particularly a detection-tampering or data-diversion change from elsewhere in this catalogue) occurred immediately before a scheduled Splunk Cloud maintenance window, which — while very likely coincidental in the vast majority of cases — is worth flagging since maintenance-window platform state changes could otherwise mask a deliberately-timed malicious change from immediate notice.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Any SPL-KO/SPL-DATA-tagged critical-control change event occurring within a short window before a scheduled Splunk Cloud maintenance window
data_sources.description: Correlation between critical-control changes and maintenance timing.

detection_logic: Joins critical-control-tagged change events against the maintenance-window schedule lookup, flagging changes shortly before a window begins.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search OR action=edit_indexes OR action=edit_tcp
| lookup splunk_cloud_maintenance_windows.csv OUTPUT upcoming_maintenance_start
| where (upcoming_maintenance_start-_time)<=1800 AND (upcoming_maintenance_start-_time)>=0
| table _time, user, object, upcoming_maintenance_start
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate given the coincidental nature of most matches; use as a contextual enrichment on top of the underlying SPL-KO/SPL-DATA detections, not as a standalone alert.
investigation_steps: Review the underlying change on its own merits per the relevant SPL-KO/SPL-DATA detection guidance.
response_guidance: Follow the underlying detection's response guidance; the maintenance-timing correlation itself does not change the response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud IDM/Identity Integration Configuration Changed
description: Splunk Cloud's identity management/SSO integration configuration was changed through the Cloud-specific administration path, the Cloud-side counterpart to the general SAML/SSO configuration-tampering detections (SPL-AUTH-015) that also accounts for Splunk Cloud's own identity-integration surface.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=idm_config_changed, or index=_audit action=edit_authentication on a Splunk Cloud stack
data_sources.description: Cloud identity-integration configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters identity-integration configuration-change events specific to the Splunk Cloud IDM administration surface.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=idm_config_changed
| table _time, user, info
tuning_guidance: Validate against your stack's actual Cloud IDM audit schema; alert on all occurrences given the severity.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Verify the new configuration against the authorized identity provider.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud Support/Break-Glass Access Session
description: Splunk Cloud support or provider-side operations personnel accessed the customer's stack through a documented support-access mechanism, which — while provider-managed and outside customer control — the customer should still track via whatever audit trail Splunk Cloud exposes for support-access events, correlating against open support tickets.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Documented support-access session events, where exposed to the customer.

detection_logic: Filters support-access session events where exposed via the customer-visible audit trail.
spl:
index=_audit sourcetype=*acs* action=support_access
| table _time, user, ticket_id
tuning_guidance: Availability and exact event schema of provider support-access visibility varies by Splunk Cloud offering; validate against your own stack rather than assuming this event type is universally exposed.
investigation_steps: Confirm the session against an open, legitimate support ticket.
response_guidance: Contact Splunk Cloud support if a session cannot be matched to a ticket.
