author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud Stack Configuration Drift from IaC Baseline
description: A configuration element managed through Infrastructure-as-Code (via the ACS API/Terraform provider) was found to differ from its declared IaC state, which can indicate either manual out-of-band tampering or a legitimate emergency change that has not yet been reconciled back into the IaC source of truth.

data_sources.name: ACS API drift check
data_sources.path: Scheduled comparison of live ACS-managed configuration against the IaC repository's declared state
data_sources.description: IaC drift-detection results.

detection_logic: A scheduled drift-detection job (e.g. `terraform plan` against the ACS provider) run outside Splunk itself, with results ingested for review.
spl:
index=<iac_drift_index> sourcetype=<terraform_plan_sourcetype> drift_detected=true
| table _time, resource_type, resource_id, drift_details
tuning_guidance: Requires an external IaC drift-detection pipeline feeding Splunk; not a native Splunk-internal-log detection.
investigation_steps: Determine if the drift reflects an emergency change or unauthorized tampering.
Reconcile the IaC state or revert the drift.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized drift; update IaC for legitimate emergency changes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud Trial-to-Production Migration Configuration Left Enabled
description: A permissive configuration setting typical of a trial/evaluation stack (broader default index access, relaxed IP allow-listing) was found still enabled well after the stack transitioned to production use, representing accumulated configuration debt rather than an active attack, but worth periodic review.

data_sources.name: REST configuration audit
data_sources.path: | rest /services/authorization/roles, compared against a known-trial-defaults baseline
data_sources.description: Periodic review of role/allow-list configuration against trial-default patterns.

detection_logic: A scheduled review search comparing current configuration against known Splunk Cloud trial-default values.
spl:
| rest /services/authorization/roles splunk_server=local
| where match(srchIndexesAllowed, "\*")
| table title, srchIndexesAllowed
tuning_guidance: Run monthly/quarterly as a hygiene check rather than a real-time alert.
investigation_steps: Confirm the stack's current production status.
Tighten the configuration to production-appropriate defaults.
response_guidance: Remediate as part of routine configuration hardening.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Splunk Cloud Privileged Admin Anomaly Correlation
description: The named Splunk-Cloud-customer-visible attack path: an SSO/login compromise (SPL-AUTH-007/016), followed by a role change (SPL-RBAC-008/SPL-CLOUD-003), followed by knowledge-object/detection modification (SPL-KO-001/003), followed by a sensitive search/export (SPL-SEARCH-005/014/018) — all observable through customer-visible Splunk Cloud telemetry without requiring provider-side host access, since Cloud customers cannot rely on OS-level detections for this chain the way an on-premises deployment could.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Login anomaly, role change, knowledge-object tampering, and sensitive search/export events for the same actor within a short window
data_sources.description: Four-stage correlation, entirely within customer-visible Splunk Cloud audit data.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) a login anomaly, (2) a role/capability change, (3) a knowledge-object/detection-tampering event, (4) a sensitive search or export — all for the same actor within a 2-hour window.
spl:
index=_audit
| eval stage=case(
    action="login" AND attempt="success", "1_login",
    action IN ("edit_user","edit_roles"), "2_privilege_change",
    action="edit_search_saved_search" AND match(info, "disabled|search="), "3_ko_tampering",
    action="search" AND match(search, "(?i)index=(security|authentication|audit)"), "4_sensitive_search")
| where isnotnull(stage)

investigation_steps: See SPL-APP-009.
response_guidance: See SPL-APP-009.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: _audit Ingestion Volume Suddenly Drops
description: The volume of events flowing into _audit dropped sharply compared to its historical baseline, which — since _audit is this catalogue's primary source for authentication, search, and administrative-activity detections — represents a platform-wide blind spot for exactly the behaviors this library is designed to catch.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: _audit ingestion volume compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Compares _audit's hourly event volume against its historical baseline.
spl:
| tstats count where index=_audit by _time span=1h
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count stdev(count) AS stdev_count
| where count < (avg_count - 3*stdev_count)
tuning_guidance: A Tier-1 heartbeat detection; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Determine if the drop is fleet-wide or scoped to a single host (SPL-INT-003).
Check for a recent logging-configuration change.
response_guidance: Treat as a top-priority visibility-gap incident; restore ingestion immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Administrative Activity Occurs Without Corresponding Audit Trail
description: Evidence of an administrative change (e.g. a knowledge object's modification timestamp, an app's version metadata) exists without a corresponding _audit event explaining who made it, which can indicate either a gap in what _audit records for a specific action type or a deliberate attempt to make a change without generating the expected audit trail.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Knowledge-object/configuration metadata timestamps compared against the _audit trail for a matching change event
data_sources.description: Reconciliation between observed state changes and their expected audit record.

detection_logic: A periodic reconciliation search comparing each knowledge object's modification timestamp (from its own metadata) against whether a corresponding _audit event exists for that object at that time.
spl:
| rest /servicesNS/-/-/saved/searches
| where updated>relative_time(now(),"-1d")
| join type=outer title [search index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search earliest=-1d | rename object AS title]
| where isnull(user)
| table title, updated
tuning_guidance: Do not assume every administrative change necessarily appears in _audit — some actions on some Splunk versions are known gaps rather than tampering; validate against your specific version's documented audit coverage before treating a mismatch as confirmed tampering.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether this is a known audit-coverage gap for this action type on your Splunk version.
If not a known gap, treat as a possible anti-forensics incident.
response_guidance: Investigate further if not explained by a known audit-coverage limitation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Single Host Stops Sending Audit Data
description: A specific host that historically contributed events to _audit (e.g. a search head in a multi-instance deployment) stopped doing so while other hosts continue reporting normally, narrowing the scope of a potential audit-visibility gap to a single system.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.path: | tstats count where index=_audit by host
data_sources.description: Per-host _audit ingestion compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Flags hosts with no _audit contribution within 3x their expected reporting interval, while the aggregate index volume remains otherwise normal.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=_audit by host
| eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60)
| where minutes_since>=45
tuning_guidance: Exclude known decommissioned/maintenance-mode hosts.
investigation_steps: Investigate the specific host directly.
Check for a local logging or forwarding configuration change on that host.
response_guidance: Restore the host's audit contribution.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Audit Source Time Gap Detected
description: A time gap was detected in the sequence of _audit events for a specific source (a discontinuity between consecutive event timestamps larger than the source's normal event cadence would suggest), which — beyond the aggregate volume-drop signal — pinpoints exactly when a gap began and ended for forensic purposes.

data_sources.name: _audit
data_sources.description: Consecutive event timestamp deltas per source compared against the source's typical cadence.

detection_logic: Computes the delta between consecutive _audit events per host and flags gaps exceeding the host's typical inter-event interval by a wide margin.
spl:
index=_audit
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prior_time by host
| eval gap=_time-prior_time
| where gap>3600
| table _time, host, gap
tuning_guidance: Tune the gap threshold to each source's realistic event cadence; exclude known low-activity periods (weekends, off-hours).
investigation_steps: Determine what occurred immediately before and after the gap.
Correlate with other hosts to rule out a broader outage.
response_guidance: Investigate the gap window with elevated scrutiny for any activity that surfaces once ingestion resumes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: _internal Disappears for a Specific Splunk Component
description: A specific splunkd component (e.g. the scheduler, a specific TcpInputProc) stopped logging to _internal while other components continue normally, which can indicate that specific subsystem was disabled or is malfunctioning — worth review since _internal is this catalogue's primary source for platform-health and service-behavior detections.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.path: | tstats count where index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd by component
data_sources.description: Per-component _internal ingestion compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Flags splunkd components with no _internal contribution within an expected interval while the aggregate _internal volume remains otherwise normal.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd by component
| eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60)
| where minutes_since>=60
tuning_guidance: Exclude components that are legitimately dormant except when a specific feature is actively used.
investigation_steps: Investigate the specific component's health directly.
Determine if it was intentionally disabled.
response_guidance: Restore the component's logging.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Forwarder Internal Logs Stop
description: A forwarder's own internal splunkd logs (as opposed to the data it forwards from monitored sources) stopped appearing at the indexer, which — beyond the general forwarder-connectivity detection (SPL-FWD-001) — specifically signals a loss of the forwarder's own self-monitoring telemetry.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.path: | tstats count where index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd by host
data_sources.description: Per-forwarder _internal ingestion compared to a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Flags forwarders with no _internal contribution within an expected interval.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd by host
| lookup known_forwarder_guids.csv host OUTPUT is_forwarder
| where is_forwarder=1
| eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60)
| where minutes_since>=45
tuning_guidance: Exclude known decommissioned forwarders.
investigation_steps: Correlate with SPL-FWD-001/SPL-FWD-006.
Investigate the host directly.
response_guidance: Restore the forwarder's connectivity/service.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Entire Security Domain Stops Logging
description: Every source contributing to a security-relevant sourcetype category (e.g. all domain controller Windows Security logs, all firewall logs) stopped ingesting simultaneously, distinguishing a domain-wide logging outage — whether from a shared upstream cause or coordinated tampering — from a single-host issue.

data_sources.name: tstats
data_sources.path: | tstats count where index=* by sourcetype, _time span=1h
data_sources.description: Aggregate ingestion volume per security-relevant sourcetype category compared to baseline.

detection_logic: Compares aggregate ingestion volume per security-relevant sourcetype category against a historical baseline, flagging near-total (>90%) drops.
spl:
| tstats count where index=* by sourcetype, _time span=1h
| lookup security_relevant_sourcetypes.csv sourcetype OUTPUT is_security_relevant
| where is_security_relevant=1
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count by sourcetype
| where count < (avg_count*0.1)
tuning_guidance: A Tier-1 flagship detection given the domain-wide implication; correlate with SPL-DATA-012/014 for a possible root cause.
investigation_steps: Treat as a top-priority visibility-gap incident.
Determine whether the cause is a shared upstream failure or coordinated tampering across multiple sources.
response_guidance: Restore ingestion immediately across every affected source; escalate to full incident response if tampering is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Scope the underlying tstats to the security-relevant sourcetype list rather than every index/sourcetype combination to keep this tractable.

title: Timestamp Parser Configuration Changed for Security Sourcetype
description: A sourcetype's TIME_FORMAT or timezone configuration was changed, which can shift how events are chronologically ordered and correlated against other sources without any individual event itself being altered — a subtle way to disrupt time-based correlation searches or investigation timelines.

data_sources.name: REST configuration audit
data_sources.path: | rest /services/configs/conf-props, compared against a daily baseline for TIME_FORMAT/TZ fields
data_sources.description: Timestamp-parsing configuration changes.

detection_logic: A scheduled review search comparing each sourcetype's TIME_FORMAT/TZ configuration against a daily baseline.
spl:
| rest /services/configs/conf-props splunk_server=local
| where isnotnull(TIME_FORMAT) OR isnotnull(TZ)
| lookup update=true timestamp_config_baseline.csv title OUTPUT prior_time_format, prior_tz
| where TIME_FORMAT!=prior_time_format OR TZ!=prior_tz
| table title, prior_time_format, TIME_FORMAT, prior_tz, TZ
tuning_guidance: Confirm against source-onboarding change tickets for legitimate initial configuration.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess correlation-search impact from the timing shift.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Event-Time vs. Index-Time Anomaly at Scale
description: A large volume of events across an index showed a significant, sustained gap between event time (_time) and index time (_indextime), consistent with either a systemic forwarding-delay issue or bulk backfilling/injection of historically-timestamped events at scale — the aggregate, index-wide companion to SPL-HEC-010's per-token detection.

data_sources.name: tstats
data_sources.description: Aggregate event-time-to-index-time gap analysis per index.

detection_logic: Computes the aggregate distribution of (_indextime - _time) per index and flags indexes with an unusually large proportion of high-gap events.
spl:
index=*
| eval time_gap=_indextime-_time
| stats count, avg(time_gap) AS avg_gap, count(eval(time_gap>86400)) AS high_gap_count by index
| where high_gap_count>(count*0.1)
tuning_guidance: Exclude known batch-upload/backfill/archival-restoration workflows.
investigation_steps: Determine the source of the anomaly.
Cross-reference with SPL-HEC-010 for a per-token breakdown if HEC is the ingestion path.
response_guidance: Investigate further if not explained by a known legitimate backfill process.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Expensive at full-index scale; run as a sampled or summary-indexed scheduled search rather than ad-hoc.

title: Host Value Changes Unexpectedly for Same Device
description: A device that has historically logged consistently under one host identity began appearing under a different host value, which can indicate a legitimate rename, a forwarder misconfiguration, or an attempt to fragment a single device's activity across multiple identities to evade per-host behavioral baselines.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.description: Forwarder connection identity (by GUID or source IP) compared against its reported host field over time.

detection_logic: Joins forwarder connections against a per-GUID host-value baseline and flags changes (same underlying pattern as SPL-FWD-004, generalized here to the internal-telemetry section for non-forwarder sources too).
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=TcpInputProc "connected"
| lookup update=true forwarder_hostname_baseline.csv guid OUTPUT prior_hostname
| where isnotnull(prior_hostname) AND hostname!=prior_hostname
| table _time, guid, prior_hostname, hostname
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with SPL-FWD-004.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the rename.
response_guidance: Investigate further if unexplained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sourcetype Changes Unexpectedly for Known Source
description: A known, established source path began ingesting under a different sourcetype than its historical baseline, which — since sourcetype often drives field extraction, CIM mapping, and detection-search targeting — can silently remove events from detection coverage without any volume drop at all, since the events still arrive but under a classification no detection is watching for.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.path: | tstats count where index=* by source, sourcetype
data_sources.description: Per-source sourcetype distribution compared against a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Joins per-source sourcetype observations against a baseline of each source's historically-dominant sourcetype and flags shifts.
spl:
| tstats count where index=* by source, sourcetype, _time span=1d
| lookup update=true source_sourcetype_baseline.csv source OUTPUT prior_sourcetype
| where isnotnull(prior_sourcetype) AND sourcetype!=prior_sourcetype
| table _time, source, prior_sourcetype, sourcetype
tuning_guidance: Exclude known planned re-classification projects.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify detection/CIM coverage under the new sourcetype classification, or restore the original.
response_guidance: Restore the original sourcetype if unauthorized; if the change is intentional, update dependent detections/data models accordingly.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security Source Impersonation via Sourcetype/Source Spoofing
description: Events arrived claiming a sourcetype/source associated with a specific trusted security product (e.g. an EDR agent, a firewall) from a source infrastructure that does not match the product's known-legitimate sending hosts, consistent with an attacker crafting events to impersonate a trusted security data source — the general, non-HEC-specific companion to SPL-HEC-009.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.description: Security-product sourcetype events compared against a per-sourcetype expected-source lookup.

detection_logic: Joins events under security-product sourcetypes against a lookup of each sourcetype's expected sending infrastructure and flags mismatches.
spl:
index=* sourcetype IN ("*firewall*","*edr*","*ids*")
| lookup expected_source_infra.csv sourcetype OUTPUT expected_hosts
| where NOT <host_in_expected_hosts>
| table _time, sourcetype, source, host
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-sourcetype expected-infrastructure lookup; a strong candidate once tuned given the impersonation-of-trust severity.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed spoofing incident.
Quarantine the spoofed events and determine the actual ingestion path used.
response_guidance: Restrict ingestion to the legitimate expected source and quarantine spoofed events pending forensic review.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Field Removal Suspected from Sourcetype's Historical Schema
description: A field that has historically been present in events under a given sourcetype stopped appearing, which can indicate a source-side change, a broken field extraction, or deliberate field-suppression tampering — the general, non-HEC-specific companion to SPL-HEC-008.

data_sources.name: Field-presence sampling
data_sources.description: Sampled field-presence rate compared against a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Periodically samples events per sourcetype and computes each historically-common field's presence rate, flagging sharp declines.
spl:
index=* sourcetype=<sourcetype>
| fieldsummary
| table field, count
| lookup update=true field_presence_baseline.csv sourcetype, field OUTPUT prior_presence_rate
| eval current_rate=count/<total_events>
| where current_rate < (prior_presence_rate*0.5)
tuning_guidance: Exclude known source-side schema-evolution events; correlate with SPL-DATA-013/015 for a possible tampering root cause.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether a recent parsing/masking change explains the drop.
If not, investigate the source directly.
response_guidance: Restore the field extraction if tampering is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: fieldsummary over a large event population is expensive; scope to a sampled subset and run on a schedule rather than ad-hoc.

title: Encoding Anomaly Suggesting Data Corruption or Tampering
description: Events with unexpected character encoding (e.g. replacement characters, mismatched charset) appeared in a source that has historically been consistently encoded, which is most often a benign source-side issue but at scale can also indicate an attempt to break downstream text-processing/regex-based detections that assume clean input.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.description: Events matching a replacement-character or encoding-mismatch pattern, aggregated per source.

detection_logic: Filters events containing the Unicode replacement character or other encoding-anomaly markers, aggregated per source.
spl:
index=*
| regex _raw="\ufffd"
| stats count by source, sourcetype
| where count>100
tuning_guidance: Exclude known sources with legitimate binary/non-UTF8 content.
investigation_steps: Determine the cause — source-side malfunction or deliberate obfuscation.
Assess whether downstream detections against this source are still functioning correctly.
response_guidance: Fix the source encoding issue; investigate further if deliberate tampering is suspected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Malformed JSON/XML Ingestion Spike
description: A structured-data source (JSON/XML) began sending an unusually high proportion of malformed events, which — beyond the operational parsing impact — is the same signal as SPL-HEC-013's HEC-specific detection but generalized across any structured-data ingestion path, not just HEC.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.path: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=AggregatorMiningProcessor "JSON parse error" OR "XML parse error"
data_sources.description: Structured-data parse-error events aggregated per source.

detection_logic: Counts parse-error log lines per source within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=AggregatorMiningProcessor ("JSON parse error" OR "XML parse error")
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count by _time, source
| where count>=50
tuning_guidance: Exclude known misconfigured legitimate senders after confirmation.
investigation_steps: Determine the cause.
Cross-reference with SPL-HEC-013 if the source is HEC-based.
response_guidance: Fix the source or rate-limit/block if malicious.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Oversized Event Ingestion Pattern
description: A source began sending events significantly larger than the configured/expected maximum event size, which either indicates a broken multiline-event boundary configuration (causing many small events to be concatenated into one giant one) or a deliberate attempt to exhaust indexing resources with oversized payloads.

data_sources.name: splunkd.log
data_sources.description: Event-truncation events (occurring when an event exceeds TRUNCATE) aggregated per source.

detection_logic: Counts truncation events per source within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=LineBreakingProcessor "Truncating"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count by _time, source
| where count>=20
tuning_guidance: Correlate with a recent source-side logging-format change before attributing to malicious intent.
investigation_steps: Determine the cause.
Fix multiline-event boundary configuration if that is the root cause.
response_guidance: Fix the source's event-boundary configuration or rate-limit if malicious.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Multiline Event Boundary Parsing Corruption
description: A multiline-capable sourcetype's average events-per-line ratio shifted sharply from its historical baseline, consistent with either an application-side log-format change or a deliberate configuration change (props.conf's LINE_BREAKER/SHOULD_LINEMERGE) intended to merge distinct security-relevant log lines into fewer, harder-to-search composite events.

data_sources.name: metrics.log
data_sources.description: Events-per-line ratio compared against a historical baseline.

detection_logic: Compares the ratio of indexed events to raw ingested lines for a multiline sourcetype against its historical baseline.
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=LineBreakingProcessor
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count AS event_count by _time, sourcetype
| eventstats avg(event_count) AS avg_count stdev(event_count) AS stdev_count by sourcetype
| where event_count < (avg_count - 3*stdev_count)
tuning_guidance: Correlate with SPL-DATA-013/SPL-CONF-005 for a possible props.conf tampering root cause.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether a recent props.conf change explains the shift.
Verify no security-relevant log lines are being lost within merged events.
response_guidance: Revert the parsing configuration if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Coordinated Anti-Forensics Across Audit, Internal, and Data-Model Telemetry
description: Two or more distinct self-monitoring signals (an _audit visibility reduction, an _internal component gap, a data-model coverage decline, a security source removed) occurred within a short window, consistent with a deliberate, coordinated attempt to blind the platform's own observability across multiple independent telemetry paths simultaneously rather than a single, isolated operational issue.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: SPL-INT-001, SPL-INT-005, SPL-KO-018 events correlated within a rolling window
data_sources.description: Threshold correlation across independent self-monitoring signals.

detection_logic: Counts distinct self-monitoring anomaly signal types (audit-gap, internal-gap, data-model-decline) occurring within a rolling window.
spl:
| tstats count where index=_audit by _time span=1h
| eventstats avg(count) AS avg_audit stdev(count) AS stdev_audit
| eval signal_type=if(count < (avg_audit - 3*stdev_audit), "audit_gap", null())
| append [| tstats latest(_time) AS last_seen where index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd by component | eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60) | where minutes_since>=60 | eval signal_type="internal_gap"]
| where isnotnull(signal_type)
| stats dc(signal_type) AS signal_count values(signal_type) AS signals by _time
| where signal_count>=2
tuning_guidance: A Tier-1 flagship anti-forensics correlation; the specification's own guidance treats logging/source-volume loss as potential defense evasion, and this detection catches the coordinated, multi-signal variant specifically.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, coordinated anti-forensics incident.
Restore all affected telemetry paths and widen the investigation scope given the deliberate, multi-vector blinding.
response_guidance: Full incident response: restore all telemetry, then investigate using whatever sources remain plus any independent backup/export data.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Combines two already-expensive tstats-based checks; schedule at a lower frequency (hourly) given its correlation nature.

title: Attack Path: Identity Compromise to Splunk Admin Access
description: The named Identity-to-Splunk-Admin attack path: an identity-provider authentication anomaly (SSO failure burst, impossible travel) is followed by a successful Splunk admin-account login from a first-seen source — confirming a compromised upstream identity was actually used to reach Splunk's own administrative tier, the entry point for nearly every other attack path in this matrix.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: SAML/LDAP authentication-anomaly events (SPL-AUTH-013/016/019) followed by an admin login from a first-seen source (SPL-AUTH-007)
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring an identity-provider authentication anomaly followed by SPL-AUTH-007's first-seen-admin-source login for the same or a related identity within 2 hours.
spl:
| savedsearch "SPL-AUTH-016 Unexpected Local Admin Login Following SSO Failure"
| append [| savedsearch "SPL-AUTH-007 First-Seen Source for Splunk Admin Login"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen count by user
| where (last_seen-first_seen)<=7200
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; the entry point of the Attack-Path Matrix — telemetry required: _audit (login events), identity-provider logs where available.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed initial-access incident.
Follow the resulting admin session through every other applicable attack path below.
response_guidance: Suspend the account, rotate credentials, and audit every action taken during the admin session.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Attack Path: Splunk Admin to Detection Tampering
description: The named Splunk-Admin-to-Detection-Tampering attack path: an admin session (from SPL-X-001 or otherwise) modifies, disables, or deletes a security-relevant knowledge object or ES correlation search — the direct continuation of SPL-KO-001/002/003/005/006 and SPL-ES-001, presented here as the named path-level entry in the Attack-Path Matrix.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: See SPL-KO-006 for the full underlying detection logic.
data_sources.description: Cross-referenced from SPL-KO-006 and SPL-ES-001.

detection_logic: See SPL-KO-006 and SPL-ES-001; telemetry required: _audit (knowledge-object change events).
spl: | savedsearch "SPL-KO-006 Detection Modified Immediately Before Matching Malicious Activity"
tuning_guidance: See SPL-KO-006 and SPL-ES-001.
investigation_steps: See SPL-KO-006 investigation steps.
response_guidance: See SPL-KO-006 response guidance.

title: Attack Path: Splunk Admin to Sensitive Data Access
description: The named Splunk-Admin-to-Sensitive-Data attack path: an admin session performs a broad or sensitive-index search and exports the results — the direct continuation of SPL-SEARCH-019, presented here as the named path-level entry.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: See SPL-SEARCH-019 for the full underlying detection logic.
data_sources.description: Cross-referenced from SPL-SEARCH-019.

detection_logic: See SPL-SEARCH-019; telemetry required: _audit (login, search events), splunkd_access.log (export events).
spl: | savedsearch "SPL-SEARCH-019 Privileged Login Followed by Broad Search and Large Export"
tuning_guidance: See SPL-SEARCH-019.

title: Attack Path: Malicious App to Server-Side Execution
description: The named App-to-Server-Execution attack path: an app is installed, followed by a scripted or modular input being created within it, followed by splunkd spawning a shell or network-fetch process, followed by an outbound network connection — stringing together SPL-APP-001, SPL-APP-003/007, and SPL-APP-006 into the full execution chain.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: App installation, scripted/modular input creation, and splunkd-child process execution for the same host within a short window
data_sources.description: Three-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) app installation, (2) scripted/modular input creation in that app, (3) a splunkd-child shell/network process — all on the same host within 1 hour.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_app info=created
| eval stage="1_app_installed"
| append [search index=_audit action=edit_input info=created | eval stage="2_input_created"]
| append [search index=<endpoint_index> sourcetype IN (Sysmon, auditd) parent_process_name="splunkd*" | where match(process_name, "(?i)^(bash|sh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|curl|wget)$") | eval stage="3_execution"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by host
| where stage_count>=3 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=3600
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level process telemetry (Sysmon/auditd) plus correlation-search support; telemetry required: _audit, OS process auditing — a Splunk Cloud limitation for the execution stage given no customer OS access.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed persistence-and-execution incident.
Isolate the host and analyze the app/script content.
response_guidance: Full incident response: remove the app, isolate the host, and investigate the outbound connection's destination.

title: Attack Path: Deployment Server to Forwarder Fleet Compromise
description: The named Deployment-Server-to-Forwarder-Fleet attack path: a deployment app is modified, followed by a broadened server class, followed by fleet-wide push to many forwarders — the direct continuation of SPL-DS-003/004/006/007/008, presented here as the named path-level entry, the single highest-blast-radius chain against the forwarder tier.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: See SPL-DS-007/008 for the full underlying detection logic.
data_sources.description: Cross-referenced from SPL-DS-007/008.

detection_logic: See SPL-DS-007 and SPL-DS-008; telemetry required: OS file-integrity monitoring on the Deployment Server (a Splunk Cloud limitation), _internal (deployment events).
spl:

title: Multi-Stack Attack: Same Source Targeting Multiple Search Heads
description: For organizations with multiple Splunk deployments/stacks, the same source IP or account exhibited authentication anomalies against more than one distinct stack within a short window, consistent with an attacker who has obtained credentials (or a credential-reuse pattern) working across the entire Splunk estate rather than a single instance — requires log aggregation across stacks to a shared analysis point.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Authentication-failure/anomaly events for the same source or account across two or more distinct Splunk stack identifiers
data_sources.description: Cross-stack correlation, requiring a shared analysis point (e.g. a dedicated monitoring stack ingesting _audit from every managed stack).

detection_logic: Requires _audit data from multiple Splunk stacks forwarded to (or federated-searchable from) a shared monitoring point; counts distinct stacks showing authentication anomalies for the same source/account within a rolling window.
spl:
index=_audit action=login attempt=failure
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats dc(stack_id) AS stack_count values(stack_id) AS stacks by _time, src
| where stack_count>=2
tuning_guidance: Requires a multi-stack log-aggregation architecture (federated search or forwarded _audit from each stack) not present in every deployment; a single-instance deployment has no applicable telemetry for this detection.
investigation_steps: Identify every affected stack.
Coordinate credential rotation and investigation across the full estate.
response_guidance: Treat as an estate-wide incident; rotate credentials across every affected stack.

title: Consolidated Persistence-Through-Splunk Correlation
description: Two or more distinct persistence-capable mechanisms (an app, scripted input, modular input, custom search command, alert action, workflow action, scheduled search, deployment app, or REST/setup handler) were introduced by the same actor within a short window, consistent with an attacker methodically establishing redundant persistence across multiple independent mechanisms rather than a single, isolated legitimate configuration change.

data_sources.description: Persistence-mechanism-creation events across every relevant object type, aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct persistence-mechanism types introduced by the same actor within a rolling window.

index=_audit (action=edit_app info=created) OR (action=edit_input info=created) OR (action=edit_search_saved_search info=created)
| eval mechanism_type=case(action="edit_app","app", action="edit_input","input", action="edit_search_saved_search","scheduled_search")
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats dc(mechanism_type) AS mechanism_count values(mechanism_type) AS mechanisms by _time, user
| where mechanism_count>=2

title: Ransomware-Style Chain Against Splunk Itself: Tampering, Retention, and Mass Deletion
description: Detection tampering (SPL-KO-001), retention/index tampering (SPL-DATA-002/003), and mass data deletion (SPL-DATA-008/009) occurred in sequence within a short window — Splunk itself is Tier-0/Tier-1 infrastructure, and this chain mirrors a classic ransomware kill-chain's own pattern (disable defenses, disable recovery, destroy data) but applied against the security platform rather than production systems, exactly the framing the specification opens with for why Splunk compromise is catastrophic.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Correlation search requiring detection-tampering, retention/index-tampering, and mass-deletion events for the same or related actors within a rolling window
data_sources.description: Three-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) a detection-tampering event, (2) a retention/index-configuration-tampering event, (3) a mass-deletion event (delete command or bulk KV Store deletion) — all within a 4-hour window.
spl:
index=_audit action=edit_search_saved_search info="*disabled=1*"
| lookup security_detection_searches.csv search_name AS object OUTPUT is_security_detection
| where is_security_detection=1
| eval stage="1_detection_tampering"
| append [search index=_audit action=edit_indexes info="*frozenTimePeriodInSecs*" | eval stage="2_retention_tampering"]
| append [search index=_audit action=search info=granted (search="*| delete*" OR search="*|delete*") | eval stage="3_mass_deletion"]
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count values(user) AS actors by _time
| where stage_count>=2 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=14400
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; the platform-self-protection equivalent of a ransomware kill-chain detection — a Tier-1 flagship correlation.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, active destructive incident against Splunk itself.
Immediately isolate every implicated account and halt further deletion.
response_guidance: Declare a major incident; engage the full incident-response and business-continuity plan, and begin recovery from the most recent clean backup of both indexed data and knowledge-object/configuration content.

title: Fleet-Wide Splunk Platform Compromise: Simultaneous Critical Anomalies Across Multiple Components
description: Critical-severity anomalies from two or more distinct components of this catalogue (authentication, RBAC, detection tampering, data pipeline, deployment infrastructure, Enterprise Security) occurred within a short window, indicating an attack operating across the platform at scale rather than against a single isolated area — the top-level escalation trigger tying together every other correlation in this section, mirroring the fleet-wide aggregator pattern used elsewhere in this library.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Critical-severity tagged events across SPL-AUTH, SPL-RBAC, SPL-KO, SPL-DATA, SPL-DS, and SPL-ES within a rolling window
data_sources.description: Threshold correlation across independent catalogue sections.

detection_logic: Counts distinct catalogue sections (by namespace prefix) contributing a critical-severity event within a rolling window.
spl:
`notable` OR (index=_audit action IN (edit_roles, edit_search_saved_search, edit_indexes, edit_serverclass) severity=critical)
| eval component_section=case(match(sourcetype,"scheduler"),"ES", action="edit_roles","RBAC", action="edit_search_saved_search","KO", action="edit_indexes","DATA", action="edit_serverclass","DS")
| bucket _time span=2h
| stats dc(component_section) AS section_count values(component_section) AS sections by _time
| where section_count>=3

investigation_steps: Treat as a Priority-1, all-hands incident against Tier-0/Tier-1 security infrastructure itself.
Activate the full incident-response plan and assume the platform's own detection capability may be compromised — rely on external/backup telemetry where available.
response_guidance: Declare a major incident; isolate the Splunk platform's administrative access, engage backup/out-of-band monitoring, and begin full recovery and forensic reconstruction.
